2009675.name: Severe Acute Malnutrition
2009675.note: Acute form of MALNUTRITION which usually affects children, characterized by a very low weight for height (below -3z scores of the median World Health Organization standards), visible severe wasting, or occurrence of nutritional EDEMA. It can be a direct or indirect cause of fatality in children suff

2009691.name: Shellfish Hypersensitivity
2009691.note: Allergic reaction to SHELLFISH or shellfish products.

2009694.name: Symptom Flare Up
2009694.note: A transient exacerbation of symptoms of an existing disease or condition.

2009700.name: Obesity, Metabolically Benign
2009700.note: A sub-PHENOTYPE of obese individuals who have a risk for CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES between that of healthy individuals with normal weight and unhealthy individuals with obesity.

2009704.name: Cold Injury
2009704.note: A physical injury caused by exposure of the body to extremely low ambient temperatures that may lead to loss of body parts, or in extreme cases, death. Examples of cold injury are FROSTBITE and CHILBLAINS.

2009707.name: War-Related Injuries
2009707.note: WOUNDS and INJURIES and PSYCHOLOGICAL TRAUMA sustained during WAR.

2009720.name: Prescription Drug Overuse
2009720.note: The use of a medication in an amount more than as prescribed.

2009737.name: Specific Learning Disorder
2009737.note: Diagnosed when there are specific deficits in an individual’s ability to perceive or process information efficiently and accurately. This disorder first manifests during the years of formal schooling and is characterized by persistent and impairing difficulties with learning foundational academic sk

2009739.name: Late Onset Disorders
2009739.note: Pathological conditions (Disorder, SYNDROME, or DISEASE) whose SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS manifest late in the life of an individual.

2009827.name: Compassion Fatigue
2009827.note: Emotional distress caused by repeated or prolonged expression of compassion or empathy. It may occur in individuals working in care giving professions.

2009920.name: Fractures, Multiple
2009920.note: Injuries involving the breaking of either several bones or one bone in two or more places.

2009937.name: Drug Resistant Epilepsy
2009937.note: Epileptic condition in which adequate trials of two tolerated and appropriately chosen and used ANTIEPILEPTIC DRUGS schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom failed.

2009939.name: Autoimmune Hypophysitis
2009939.note: Immune-mediated inflammation of the PITUITARY GLAND often associated with other autoimmune diseases (e.g., HASHIMOTO DISEASE; GRAVES DISEASE; and ADDISON DISEASE).

2009940.name: Canaliculitis
2009940.note: Inflammation and infection of the lacrimal canaliculus area in the LACRIMAL APPARATUS.

2009947.name: Incisional Hernia
2009947.note: Protrusion of tissue at or near the site of an incision from a previous surgery.

2009949.name: Plasmablastic Lymphoma
syn: Plasmablastic Diffuse Large B cell Lymphoma
Plasmablasts Diffuse Large B cell Lymphoma
2009949.note: Malignant lymphoma composed of large B lymphoid cells which have the immunophenotype of plasma cells and a predilection for the ORAL CAVITY.

2009951.name: Mammary Analogue Secretory Carcinoma
2009951.note: A malignant neoplasm of epithelial cells of the SALIVARY GLANDS, with microcystic architecture, low-grade nuclei, and granular vacuolated cytoplasm.

2009953.name: Acne Conglobata
2009953.note: Severe and chronic form of acne characterized by large, burrowing abscesses associated with disfigurement.

2009988.name: Long Term Adverse Effects
2009988.note: Persistent detrimental effects from treatment for a condition. Included are effects from surgery such as POSTOPERATIVE COMPLICATIONS, and from DRUG THERAPY, such as CHEMICALLY INDUCED DISORDERS, or other THERAPEUTICS. Failure to attain a desired outcome from treatment for the condition is not consid

2010025.name: Infectious Encephalitis
2010025.note: Brain inflammation caused by an infectious agent.

2010039.name: Waterborne Diseases
2010039.note: Illnesses due to micro-organisms and chemicals in drinking water, those caused by organisms having part of their lifecycle in water or those with water-related vectors, and others spread by aerosols containing pathogens.

2010045.name: Unilateral Breast Neoplasms
2010045.note: Tumors or cancer found specifically in one human BREAST, but not in both.

2011257.name: Zika Virus Infection
2011257.note: A viral disease transmitted by the bite of AEDES mosquitoes infected with ZIKA VIRUS. Its mild DENGUE-like symptoms include fever, rash, headaches and ARTHRALGIA. The viral infection during pregnancy, in rare cases, is associated with congenital brain and ocular abnormalities, called Congenital Zika

2016182.name: Degloving Injuries
2016182.note: Avulsions of the superficial tissues of SKIN and SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE from the underlying FASCIA.

2016183.name: Staghorn Calculi
2016183.note: Renal calculi with a characteristic shape like antlers of a deer, formed as it extends into multiple calices of the RENAL PELVIS. A large number of staghorn calculi as well as other URINARY CALCULI are composed of STRUVITE.

2016269.name: Talipes
2016269.note: Deformity in which the foot is misaligned with respect to the TALUS in the ANKLE JOINT. While mostly congenital, as in CLUBFOOT, acquired deformities are included. Acquired talipedes are often associated with other foot deformities such as SYNDACTYLY and POLYDACTYLY.

2016278.name: Talipes Cavus
2016278.note: A foot deformity in which the arch of the foot is high and often the heel adducted.

2016280.name: Metatarsal Valgus
2016280.note: A foot anomaly in which the forefoot is angled outward relative to the hindfoot.

2016281.name: Metatarsus Varus
2016281.note: A foot anomaly in which the forefoot (METATARSUS) is angled inward relative to the heel.

2016284.name: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries
2016284.note: Sprain or tear injuries to the ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT of the knee.

2016285.name: Shoulder Injuries
syn: Superior Labrum from Anterior to Posterior Injuries
2016285.note: Injuries involving the SHOULDERS and SHOULDER JOINT.

2016286.name: Tibial Meniscus Injuries
2016286.note: Injuries to the TIBIAL MENISCUS of the leg.

2016289.name: Coxa Magna
2016289.note: Deformity of the hip characterized by enlargement and deformation of the FEMUR HEAD and FEMUR NECK, often with associated changes in the ACETABULUM. These changes may be secondary to other diseases (e.g. LEGG-PERTHES DISEASE; ARTHRITIS; HIP DISLOCATION, CONGENITAL) or TRAUMA.

2016290.name: Tarsal Coalition
2016290.note: Congenital, complete or partial fusion of the TARSAL BONES of the foot. PES PLANUS is usually a feature.

2016292.name: Morton Neuroma
2016292.note: A nerve inflammation in the foot caused by chronic compression of the plantar nerve between the METATARSAL BONES.

2016295.name: Microtrauma, Physical
2016295.note: Small injuries caused by external force applied to the body including bones, muscles, nerves and tendons.

2016297.name: Brain Contusion
2016297.note: A bruise of the brain from an impact of the skull.

2016298.name: Brain Injuries, Diffuse
2016298.note: Brain injuries occurring over a wide area instead of specific focal area.

2016299.name: Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy
2016299.note: Degenerative brain disease linked to repetitive brain trauma. Progressive symptoms may include MEMORY LOSS; AGGRESSION; or DEPRESSION.

2016302.name: Diastasis, Bone
2016302.note: Abnormal separation of bones, often from a LIGAMENT.

2016307.name: Rotator Cuff Injuries
2016307.note: Injuries to the ROTATOR CUFF of the shoulder joint.

2016310.name: Elbow Tendinopathy
2016310.note: Inflammation (tendinitis) or degeneration (tendinosis) of the tendons of the elbow.

2016311.name: Brain Injuries, Traumatic
2016311.note: A form of acquired brain injury which occurs when a sudden trauma causes damage to the brain.

2016312.name: Rotator Cuff Tear Arthropathy
2016312.note: Rapidly destructive shoulder joint and bone disease found mainly in elderly, and predominantly in women. It is characterized by SHOULDER PAIN; JOINT INSTABILITY; and the presence of crystalline CALCIUM PHOSPHATES in the SYNOVIAL FLUID. It is associated with ROTATOR CUFF INJURIES.

2016313.name: Crystal Arthropathies
2016313.note: Joint disorders that are characterized by accumulation of microcrystals in and around the joint including in the SYNOVIAL FLUID. They are classified according to the chemical nature of the crystals such as CALCIUM PYROPHOSPHATE; basic CALCIUM PHOSPHATES; and monosodium urate (see URIC ACID).

2016317.name: Enthesopathy
2016317.note: A disorder occurring at the site of insertion of TENDONS or LIGAMENTS into bones or JOINT CAPSULES.

2016324.name: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath
syn: Localized Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath
2016324.note: A tumor arising in the SYNOVIAL MEMBRANE; SYNOVIAL BURSA; or TENDON sheath. It is characterized by OSTEOCLAST-like GIANT CELLS; FOAM CELLS; pigmented HEMOSIDERIN-laden MACROPHAGES and inflammatory infiltrate. It is classified either as diffuse or localized tenosynovitis.

2016343.name: Bankart Lesions
2016343.note: An anterior capsulolabral injury associated with a tear of the anteroinferior GLENOID LABRUM.

2016352.name: Hyperekplexia
2016352.note: A neurological disorder characterized by an excessive startle reaction with ABNORMAL REFLEX; MYOCLONIC JERKS; and MUSCLE HYPERTONIA.

2016362.name: Anorectal Malformations
2016362.note: Congenital defects in the anus and the rectum often involving the urinary and genital tracts.

2016363.name: Tardive Dyskinesia
2016363.note: Drug-related movement disorder characterized by uncontrollable movements in certain muscles. It is associated with a long-term exposure to certain neuroleptic medications (e.g., METOCLOPRAMIDE).

2016370.name: Alert Fatigue, Health Personnel
2016370.note: Mental fatigue experienced by health care providers who encounter numerous alerts and reminders from the use of CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS. As the numbers of alerts and reminders designed to provide meaningful assistance to the patient care process increases, many health personnel may ignore

2016373.name: Pneumonia, Necrotizing
2016373.note: Severe complication of pneumonia characterized by liquefaction of lung tissue.

2016375.name: Multiple Chronic Conditions
2016375.note: Two or more concurrent chronic physical, mental, or behavioral health problems in an individual.

2016376.name: Familial Multiple Lipomatosis
2016376.note: A rare autosomal disorder characterized by numerous encapsulated lipomas on the trunk and extremities. The lipomas are usually not painful but can cause pain when growing. In rare cases, one lipoma can become painful and progress to multiple painful lipomas; it is then referred to as Dercum's Diseas

2016377.name: Microaneurysm
2016377.note: Aneurysm of the MICROVASCULATURE. Charcot–Bouchard aneurysms are aneurysms of the brain vasculature which is a common cause of CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE. Retinal microaneurysm is an early diagnostic sign of DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.

2016378.name: Acute Febrile Encephalopathy
2016378.note: Acute onset of fever accompanied by seizures, cerebral inflammation and a change in mental status (e.g., confusion, disorientation, and coma).

2016379.name: Neonatal Sepsis
2016379.note: Blood infection that occurs in an infant younger than 90 days old. Early-onset sepsis is seen in the first week of life and most often appears within 24 hours of birth. Late-onset occurs after 1 week and before 3 months of age.

2016380.name: Small Fiber Neuropathy
2016380.note: Disorder of the peripheral nerves that primarily impair small nerve fibers. The affected small nerve fibers include myelinated A-delta fibers (see A FIBERS) and unmyelinated C FIBERS. Because these small fibers innervate skin and help control autonomic function, their neuropathy presents with neurop

2016453.name: Emergence Delirium
2016453.note: A form of DELIRIUM which occurs after GENERAL ANESTHESIA.

2016457.name: Acute Retroviral Syndrome
2016457.note: Early stage of HIV infection. Symptoms resemble INFLUENZA or INFECTIOUS MONONUCLEOSIS.

2016458.name: Body Remains
2016458.note: The physical entity of a deceased human or animal.

2016464.name: Bunion
2016464.note: Abnormal swelling of the inner aspect of the first metatarsal head affecting the first METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT.

2016465.name: Fibromatosis, Plantar
2016465.note: A fibromatosis of the plantar fascia characterized by thickening of the fibrous bands on the plantar aponeurosis in the sole of the foot and toes.

2016514.name: Fractures, Avulsion
2016514.note: Tearing away of the CORTICAL BONE fragment at the location of a strong ligament or tendon attachment. The bone fragment detachment site often occurs near a soft site (e.g., GROWTH PLATE) at the base where LIGAMENTS; TENDONS; or JOINT CAPSULES attach. In younger patients it is most often caused by a

2016515.name: Crush Injuries
2016515.note: Excessive compression of parts of the body that causes muscle swelling, fracture, and/or neurological disturbances in the affected areas. Crush injury with systemic manifestations is referred to as CRUSH SYNDROME.

2016529.name: Cellulite
2016529.note: Skin lumpiness or skin surface dimpling often seen on the thighs, buttocks and abdomen. It is due to protrusion of SUBCUTANEOUS FAT into the DERMIS layer of skin.

2016530.name: Latent Autoimmune Diabetes in Adults
syn: LADA, Latent Autoimmune Diabetes in Adults
2016530.note: Autoimmune diabetes in adults with slowly progressive PANCREATIC BETA CELL failure and the presence of circulating autoantibodies to PANCREATIC ISLETS cell antigens.

2016531.name: Bilateral Vestibulopathy
2016531.note: Impairment of the vestibular function of both inner ears which can cause difficulties with balance, gait, VERTIGO, and visual blurring.

2016532.name: Cone-Rod Dystrophies
2016532.note: Genetically heterogeneous and sometimes syndromic (e.g., BARDET BIEDL SYNDROME; and SPINOCEREBELLAR ATAXIA TYPE 7) retinopathies with initial RETINAL CONE involvement. They are characterized by decreased VISUAL ACUITY; COLOR VISION DEFECTS; progressive loss of peripheral vision and night blindness.

2016568.name: Medically Unexplained Symptoms
2016568.note: Persistent health symptoms which remain unexplained after a complete medical evaluation. A cluster of symptoms that consistently appear together but without a known cause are referred to as a MEDICALLY UNEXPLAINED SYNDROME (MUS).

2016576.name: Myocardial Contusions
2016576.note: Bruise to the heart muscle due to blunt thoracic trauma.

2016578.name: Breast Carcinoma In Situ
2016578.note: A condition in which abnormal cells have not spread outside the duct, lobule, or nipple to other tissues of the breast. There are 3 types of breast carcinoma in situ: DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU; LOBULAR CARCINOMA IN SITU; and PAGET DISEASE OF THE NIPPLE.

2016591.name: Fracture Dislocation
2016591.note: Fracture of a bone near an articulation with concomitant dislocation of that joint.

2016676.name: Lymphadenopathy
2016676.note: Disease of LYMPH NODES which are abnormal in size, number or consistency.

2016753.name: Breast Cancer Lymphedema
2016753.note: Abnormal accumulation of lymph in the arm, shoulder and breast area associated with surgical treatment (e.g., MASTECTOMY) or radiation treatment of breast cancer.

2016754.name: ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction
2016754.note: A clinical syndrome defined by MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA symptoms; persistent elevation in the ST segments of the ELECTROCARDIOGRAM; and release of BIOMARKERS of myocardial NECROSIS (e.g., elevated TROPONIN levels). ST segment elevation in the ECG is often used in determining the treatment protocol (see a

2016755.name: Non-ST Elevated Myocardial Infarction
2016755.note: A myocardial infarction that does not produce elevations in the ST segments of the ELECTROCARDIOGRAM. ST segment elevation of the ECG is often used in determining the treatment protocol (see also ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction).

2016757.name: Teratozoospermia
2016757.note: Conditions in which sperm show abnormal morphology.

2016758.name: Ciliopathies
2016758.note: Genetic disorders caused by defects in genes related to the primary CILIUM; BASAL BODY; or CENTROSOME. Primary features may include obesity, SKELETAL DYSPLASIA; POLYDACTYLY and malformations that primarily involve the liver, eye or kidneys.

2016759.name: Margins of Excision
2016759.note: The edges of tissue removed in a surgery for assessment of the effectiveness of a surgical procedure in achieving the local control of a neoplasm and the adequacy of tumor removal. When the margin is negative or not involved by tumor (e.g., CANCER) it suggests all of the tumor has been removed by th

2016760.name: Spontaneous Perforation
2016760.note: A pathological hole in an organ, blood vessel or other soft part of the body, occurring in the absence of external force.

2016767.name: Ankyloglossia
2016767.note: A severe congenital restriction of TONGUE movement, resulting from fusion or adherence of the tongue to the floor of the mouth. In partial ankyloglossia (tongue-tie) the LINGUAL FRENUM is abnormally short, or is attached too close to the tip of the tongue. OMIM: 106280

2016773.name: Cancer Pain
2016773.note: Pain that may be caused by or related to cellular, tissue, and systemic changes that occur during NEOPLASM growth, tissue invasion, and METASTASIS.

2016774.name: Tertiary Lymphoid Structures
2016774.note: Aggregates of immune cells formed near the sites of chronically inflamed, infected, or tumorous tissues.

2016775.name: Propofol Infusion Syndrome
2016775.note: Rare and often fatal drug complication which affects patients undergoing long-term treatment with high doses of PROPOFOL. It is characterized by METABOLIC ACIDOSIS; HYPERLIPIDEMIA; RHABDOMYOLYSIS; cardiovascular CIRCULATORY COLLAPSE; CARDIAC FAILURE; and KIDNEY FAILURE.

2016781.name: Invasive Fungal Infections
2016781.note: Mycoses which manifest as infections of deep tissue or blood.

2016794.name: Surgical Wound
2016794.note: An incision made during a surgical procedure.

2016795.name: Chromothripsis
2016795.note: Massive number of chromosomal rearrangements and shattering that occurs in cancer cells. The breakpoints are located within one chromosome or chromosome arm.

2023103.name: Noncommunicable Diseases
2023103.note: Diseases which are typically non-infectious in origin and do not transmit from an affected individual to others. The four main types of noncommunicable diseases are CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES (e.g., heart attacks and stroke), CANCER, chronic respiratory diseases (e.g., CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DIS

2023112.name: Epileptic Syndromes
2023112.note: EPILEPTIC SEIZURES that are of similar type and age of onset and have other similar features (e.g., clinical course, EEG findings, genetic association and neuropathology).

2023114.name: Occupational Stress
2023114.note: Adverse psychological and behavioral reactions caused by the pressures and demands of employers or clients or other factors, such as the physical environment of the workplace, WORKPLACE VIOLENCE; or WORKPLACE BULLYING.

2023118.name: Microvascular Rarefaction
2023118.note: The reduction in density of the MICROVASCULATURE.

2023122.name: Frailty
2023122.note: A state of increased vulnerability to stressors, following declines in function and reserves across multiple physiologic systems, characterized by MUSCLE WEAKNESS; FATIGUE; slowed motor performance; low physical activity; and unintentional weight loss.

2023145.name: Spotted Fever Group Rickettsiosis
2023145.note: A group of arthropod-borne diseases caused by spotted fever bio-group members of RICKETTSIA. They are characterized by fever, headache, and petechial (spotted) rash.

2023146.name: Transfusion-Related Acute Lung Injury
2023146.note: A rare but serious transfusion-related reaction in which fluid builds up in the lungs unrelated to excessively high infusion rate and/or volume (TRANSFUSION-ASSOCIATED CIRCULATORY OVERLOAD). Signs of Transfusion-Related Acute Lung Injury include pulmonary secretions; hypotension; fever; DYSPNEA; TAC

2023147.name: Varicella Zoster Virus Infection
2023147.note: Infection caused by HUMAN HERPES VIRUS 3 (e.g., CHICKENPOX and HERPES ZOSTER).

2023166.name: Procedural Pain
2023166.note: Pain associated with examination, treatment or procedures.

2023169.name: Trisomy 13 Syndrome
2023169.note: A chromosome disorder associated with TRISOMY of all or part of CHROMOSOME 13. Clinical manifestations include CONGENITAL HEART DEFECTS (e.g., PATENT DUCTUS ARTERIOSUS), facial malformations (e.g., CLEFT LIP; CLEFT PALATE; COLOBOMA; MICROPHTHALMIA); HYPOTONIA, digit malformations (e.g., POLYDACTYLY

2023171.name: Trisomy 18 Syndrome
2023171.note: A chromosome disorder associated with TRISOMY of all or part of CHROMOSOME 18. Clinical manifestations include INTRAUTERINE GROWTH RETARDATION; CLEFT PALATE; CONGENITAL HEART DEFECTS; MICROCEPHALY; MICROGNATHIA and clenched fists with overlapping fingers. Most affected fetuses do not survive to birt

2023185.name: Vascular Ring
syn: Right Aortic Arch with Left Ligamentum Arteriosum
2023185.note: Congenital vascular malformation in which the AORTA arch and its branches encircle the TRACHEA and ESOPHAGUS. Signs and symptoms include DYSPNEA; RESPIRATORY SOUNDS, especially with eating, DYSPHAGIA, persistent cough, and GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX or may be asymptomatic. Two most common types are dou

2023203.name: Food Intolerance
2023203.note: Digestive system disorder where a particular food irritates the digestive tract or cannot be properly digested (i.e., due to a lack of a digestive enzyme). It differs from FOOD HYPERSENSITIVITY which is an immune system disorder, usually due to specific proteins in food. http://my.clevelandclinic.or

2023221.name: Tubular Sweat Gland Adenomas
2023221.note: Various tubular forms of benign tumors of the SWEAT GLAND with glandular differentiation. Common types include syringocystadenoma papilliferum of the head and neck, and hidradenoma papilliferum of the vulva area. Hidradenoma papilliferum may be derived from mammary-like glands of the vulva.

2023227.name: Interatrial Block
2023227.note: Impaired or delayed impulse conduction between the right and left HEART ATRIA. Advanced interatrial blocks are often associated with arrhythmias (e.g., ATRIAL FLUTTER; and ATRIAL FIBRILLATION), direct conduction block via the Bachmann's bundle and concomitant left atrial enlargement. Syndrome of adv

2023235.name: Cerebral Intraventricular Hemorrhage
2023235.note: Bleeding within the CEREBRAL VENTRICLES. It is associated with intraventricular trauma, aneurysm, vascular malformations, hypertension and in VERY LOW BIRTH WEIGHT infants.

2023246.name: Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Diseases
2023246.note: Diseases that exhibit signs and symptoms suggestive of a connective tissue disease that do not fulfill clinical or diagnostic criteria for any one defined disease but overlap with criteria of multiple such diseases. Commonly overlapping diseases include systemic autoimmune connective tissue diseases

2023282.name: Meconium Ileus
2023282.note: Intestinal obstruction caused by congealed MECONIUM in the distal ILEUM and CECUM. It presents shortly after birth as a failure to pass meconium and frequently occurs in infants with CYSTIC FIBROSIS.

2023349.name: Opium Dependence
2023349.note: Strong physiological and emotional dependence on OPIUM.

2023367.name: Oncogene Addiction
2023367.note: The dependence of tumor cells on a single oncogenic pathway or protein for their continued proliferation and survival.

2023368.name: Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome
syn: Celiac Artery Stenosis from Compression by Median Arcuate Ligament of Diaphragm
2023368.note: Compression of the CELIAC ARTERY by the median arcuate ligament, a fibrous band of the DIAPHRAGM, causing abdominal pain after eating and weight loss. OMIM: 116870

2023391.name: Nut and Peanut Hypersensitivity
2023391.note: Allergic reaction to tree nuts and peanuts, including other LEGUMES, that is triggered by the immune system. It includes co-sensitization to other food (e.g., sesame seed).

2023392.name: Kounis Syndrome
2023392.note: A disorder of cardiac function secondary to hypersensitivity reactions. It is characterized by coexistence of acute coronary syndromes and cardiac MAST CELL and PLATELET ACTIVATION. It may be induced by exposure to drugs (e.g., antibiotics, anesthetics, contrast media), food, and environmental trigg

2023404.name: Substance Abuse, Oral
2023404.note: Abuse, overuse, or misuse of a substance by ingestion.

2023407.name: Smoldering Multiple Myeloma
2023407.note: An asymptomatic and slow-growing PLASMA CELL dyscrasia characterized by presence of MYELOMA PROTEINS and clonal bone marrow plasma cells without end-organ damage (e.g., renal impairment). It is distinguished from MONOCLONAL GAMMOPATHY OF UNDETERMINED SIGNIFICANCE by a much higher risk of progression

2023415.name: Essential Hypertension
2023415.note: Hypertension that occurs without known cause, or preexisting renal disease. Associated polymorphisms for a number of genes have been identified, including AGT, GNB3, and ECE1. OMIM: 145500

2023417.name: Cardiac Conduction System Disease
2023417.note: Diseases characterized by pathological irregularities in the HEART CONDUCTION SYSTEM. They may be associated with other heart diseases and syndromes (e.g., BRUGADA SYNDROME; NEUROMUSCULAR DISEASE, HEART BLOCKS), isolated or may result from injuries. You can have a conduction disorder without having

2023422.name: Hypoadrenocorticism, Familial
syn: Adrenal Hypoplasia, Congenital, with Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism
2023422.note: Genetic or familial occurrence of ADDISONS DISEASE characterized by insufficient production of cortisol, aldosterone, and/or other hormones made in the adrenal cortex.

2023425.name: Heavy Metal Poisoning
2023425.note: Poisoning that results from chronic or acute ingestion, injection, inhalation, or skin absorption of HEAVY METALS. Acute and chronic exposures can cause ANEMIA; KIDNEY and LIVER damage; PULMONARY EDEMA; MEMORY LOSS and behavioral changes; bone deformities in children; and MISCARRIAGE or PREMATURE LA

2023428.name: Immunoglobulin Light-chain Amyloidosis
2023428.note: A nonproliferative disorder of PLASMA CELLS characterized by excessive production and misfolding of IMMUNOGLOBULIN LIGHT CHAINS that form insoluble amyloid fibrils (see AMYLOID DEPOSITS) in various tissues. Clinical features include LIVER FAILURE; MULTIPLE MYELOMA; NEPHROTIC SYNDROME; RESTRICTIVE CA

2023453.name: Solitary Kidney
2023453.note: Either a single or a single functioning kidney due to NEPHRECTOMY, birth defects or other kidney diseases.

2023456.name: Charles Bonnet Syndrome
2023456.note: Repetitive visual hallucinations experienced mostly by elderly with diminished visual acuity or visual field loss, with awareness of the fictional nature of their hallucinations. It is not associated with delusions and other sensory hallucinations.

2023459.name: Injection Site Reaction
2023459.note: Adverse reactions that occur initially at the site of injection or infusion. Milder type is confined to a local allergic flare reaction. A more severe reaction is caused by extravasation of VESICANTS from the blood vessel at the site of injection and can cause damage to the surrounding tissue. In tu

2023486.name: Clinical Deterioration
2023486.note: A critical disease progression, often measured by a set of clinical parameters, which activates HOSPITAL RAPID RESPONSE TEAM.

2023500.name: Alcoholic Korsakoff Syndrome
2023500.note: A neurological disorder characterized by inattentiveness and the inability to form short term memories. It is caused by THIAMINE DEFICIENCY due to chronic ALCOHOLISM.

2023501.name: Drug Misuse
2023501.note: Use of a drug for a purpose not consistent with legal or medical guidelines.

2023540.name: Communicable Diseases, Imported
2023540.note: Infectious diseases originating in one geographically delineated ecosystem that are carried (by travel or immigration) to another geographically delineated ecosystem by an infected individual, animal, or disease vector.

2023547.name: Diverticular Diseases
2023547.note: Diseases of the DIVERTICULUM often due to infection and/or inflammation (DIVERTICULITIS).

2027885.name: Neonatal Brachial Plexus Palsy
2027885.note: Perinatal nerve injury involving the BRACHIAL PLEXUS involving a weak or paralyzed upper extremity.

2027917.name: Neurolymphomatosis
2027917.note: Infiltration of the nervous system by malignant lymphoma cells.

2027923.name: Adenocarcinoma of Lung
2027923.note: A carcinoma originating in the lung and the most common lung cancer type in never-smokers. Malignant cells exhibit distinct features such as glandular epithelial, or tubular morphology. Mutations in KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, and ERBB2 genes are associated with this cancer.

2027925.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Head and Neck
syn: Head And Neck Squamous Cell Carcinomas
Carcinoma, Squamous Cell of Head and Neck
Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck
Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Head And Neck
Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Mouth
Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Larynx
Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Nasal Cavity
2027925.note: The most common type of head and neck carcinoma that originates from cells on the surface of the NASAL CAVITY; MOUTH; PARANASAL SINUSES, SALIVARY GLANDS, and LARYNX. Mutations in TNFRSF10B, PTEN, and ING1 genes are associated with this cancer.

2027931.name: Chondrosarcoma, Clear Cell
2027931.note: A chondrosarcoma of adolescence to old age of the proximal EPIPHYSES of long bones. It has variably clear cytoplasm of the mostly neoplastic CHONDROCYTES with little intervening matrix.

2027940.name: Carcinoma, Ovarian Epithelial
2027940.note: A malignant neoplasm that originates in cells on the surface EPITHELIUM of the ovary and is the most common form of ovarian cancer. There are five histologic subtypes: papillary serous, endometrioid, mucinous, clear cell, and transitional cell. Mutations in BRCA1, OPCML, PRKN, PIK3CA, AKT1, CTNNB1,

2027965.name: Thyroid Cancer, Papillary
2027965.note: An ADENOCARCINOMA that originates from follicular cells of the THYROID GLAND and accounts for the majority of THYROID CANCER cases. Cells exhibit enlarged, oval, or elongated morphologies with clear, round, nuclei. Fusions of RET, NTRK1, TPM3, and PCM1 genes are associated with this cancer.

2027966.name: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
2027966.note: A carcinoma that originates in the EPITHELIUM of the NASOPHARYNX and includes four subtypes: keratinizing squamous cell, non-keratinizing, basaloid squamous cell, and PAPILLARY ADENOCARCINOMA. It is most prevalent in Southeast Asian populations and is associated with EPSTEIN-BARR VIRUS INFECTIONS. S

2027967.name: Craniofacial Fibrous Dysplasia
2027967.note: Mostly benign fibro-osseous proliferation of the facial bones and skull. It can be either monostotic (localized to a single bone) or polyostotic (localized to more than one bone) type.

2027969.name: Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
2027969.note: A carcinoma that originates usually from cells on the surface of the middle and lower third of the ESOPHAGUS. Tumor cells exhibit typical squamous morphology and form large polypoid lesions. Mutations in RNF6, LZTS1, TGFBR2, DEC1, and WWOX1 genes are associated with this cancer.

2027984.name: Urinary Bladder, Underactive
2027984.note: Symptom of underactive detrusor muscle of the URINARY BLADDER that contracts with abnormally reduced strength or duration resulting in an incomplete and/or prolonged bladder emptying.

2027988.name: Healthcare-Associated Pneumonia
2027988.note: Infection of the lung often accompanied by inflammation that is acquired through an interaction within a healthcare institution often through a therapeutic experience (e.g., use of catheters or ventilators).

2028015.name: Post-Lyme Disease Syndrome
2028015.note: A condition caused by long-lasting and ongoing infection with the spirochete Borrelia burgdorferi resulting in progressive inflammatory neurologic, neuromuscular, and dermatologic manifestations including ENCEPHALITIS; MYELITIS; acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans; and ARTHRITIS.

2028033.name: GATA2 Deficiency
2028033.note: A rare disorder of the immune system with wide-ranging effects which include GATA2 Transcription Factor dysfunction, immunodeficiency, myelodysplastic syndrome (ineffective blood cell production), lung disease, and problems of the vascular and lymphatic system.

2028110.name: Cauda Equina Syndrome
2028110.note: Compressive lesion affecting the nerve roots of the CAUDA EQUINA (e.g., compression, herniation, inflammation, rupture, or stenosis), which controls the function of the bladder and bowel. Symptoms may include neurological dysfunction of bladder or bowels, loss of sexual sensation and altered sensati

2028127.name: Immunoglobulin G4-Related Disease
2028127.note: A spectrum of systemic autoimmune diseases in which IMMUNOGLOBULIN G4 plays a pathophysiologic role. It can affect multiple organs in highly variable presentations, characterized by inflammatory lesions composed of IgG4-positive PLASMA CELLS, further infiltrated by T helper cells (T-LYMPHOCYTES, HEL

2028134.name: Cone Dystrophy
2028134.note: A general term which describes a group of rare eye disorders that affect the cone cells of the RETINA. Cone dystrophy can cause a variety of symptoms including decreased visual clarity or acuity when looking straight ahead (central vision), a reduced ability to see colors, and an increased sensitivi

2028143.name: Myopericytoma
2028143.note: Rare myofibroma-like perivascular soft tissue tumor, usually benign, characterized by concentric perivascular proliferation.

2028144.name: Pancreatic Intraductal Neoplasms
syn: Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasms of the Pancreas
2028144.note: EPITHELIAL NEOPLASMS with pancreatic ductal differentiation that arise from the EXOCRINE PANCREAS and grow mostly within the PANCREATIC DUCTS. They are characterized by the presence of intraductal masses with mostly papillary growth pattern. Overt production of MUCIN within the pancreatic duct is as

2028164.name: Body-Weight Trajectory
2028164.note: A general pattern of body weight gain or loss over many years. Weight change trajectory is influenced by several determinants in children and adults.

2028170.name: Gestational Weight Gain
2028170.note: Increase in body weight of the mother during the course of her PREGNANCY.

2030840.name: Pregnancy in Obesity
2030840.note: BODY MASS INDEX in PREGNANT PEOPLE that is excessively above the recommended cut-off.

2030841.name: Vaccine-Preventable Diseases
2030841.note: Diseases for which vaccines exist that can confer partial or complete protection. (World Health Organization vaccine-safety-training.org)

2030854.name: Vector Borne Diseases
2030854.note: Infectious diseases transmitted by DISEASE VECTORS.

2030857.name: Narcotic-Related Disorders
2030857.note: Disorders related to or resulting from abuse or misuse of NARCOTICS.

2030862.name: Rumination Syndrome
2030862.note: A gastrointestinal disorder characterized by repetitive and effortless regurgitation of ingested food from the stomach to the oral cavity in the early POSTPRANDIAL PERIOD. It is associated with functional gastrointestinal pathology (e.g., increased intra-gastric pressure) and psychiatric disorders (

2030875.name: Opioid-Induced Constipation
2030875.note: CONSTIPATION associated with the use of OPIOIDS.

2030876.name: Postoperative Cognitive Complications
2030876.note: COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT or functional decline after a surgical procedure.

2030883.name: Extranodal Extension
2030883.note: A penetration of LYMPH NODE metastatic cells through the nodal capsule into the perinodal fatty tissue used in a TUMOR STAGING system (the TNM staging system).

2030898.name: Anomalous Left Coronary Artery
2030898.note: Malformations of left CORONARY ARTERY where it is connected to the PULMONARY ARTERY instead of the AORTA.

2030899.name: Univentricular Heart
2030899.note: Rare congenital heart malformation with a single ventricle (HEART VENTRICLES) instead of the usual two.

2030900.name: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
syn: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Vessels
2030900.note: A rare heart defect that occurs when the HEART VENTRICLES and attached valves, the MITRAL VALVE and the TRICUSPID VALVE are reversed so that the AORTA and the PULMONARY ARTERY are connected to the wrong ventricle. Although the heart valves and the two great arteries, the PULMONARY ARTERY and the AOR

2030926.name: Hamman-Rich Syndrome
2030926.note: Acute idiopathic interstitial pneumonitis characterized by diffuse PULMONARY ALVEOLI damage with uniform edematous connective tissue proliferation. It is often associated with extensive fibroblastic distortion of the lung parenchyma and leads to ADULT RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME in later stages.

2030927.name: Pancreaticobiliary Maljunction
2030927.note: A group of anatomical variations in which the COMMON BILE DUCT and MAIN PANCREATIC DUCT are joined outside the duodenal wall often with abnormally long common channel rather than at the SPHINCTER OF ODDI.

2030928.name: Chronic Urticaria
2030928.note: Wheals (urticaria) and/or angioedema presented with daily symptoms lasting for more than 6 weeks. It may be classified into chronic spontaneous and chronic inducible urticaria depending on whether a specific trigger can be linked to the development of vascular reaction.

2030938.name: Synesthesia
2030938.note: The experience of involuntary sensory cross activation where the presentation of a particular stimulus elicits a secondary sensory-perceptual experience. It most commonly occurs in the association of color with linguistic stimuli such as letters, numbers, words, or music, but can also occur between

2030939.name: Cyclodialysis Clefts
2030939.note: Finding of a separation of the CILIARY BODY in the SCLERAL SPUR region, creating aqueous outflow from the ANTERIOR CHAMBER into suprachoroidal space between the CHOROID and the SCLERA. Persistent cyclodialysis clefts may be associated with OCULAR HYPOTENSION and OPTIC DISC EDEMA.

2030940.name: Uveal Effusion Syndrome
2030940.note: Rare disease characterized by suprachoroidal fluid accumulation between the CHOROID and the SCLERA, annular detachment of the CHOROID, often with secondary RETINAL DETACHMENT; OPTIC DISK EDEMA, and minimal signs of UVEITIS and INTRAOCULAR PRESSURE changes.

2030941.name: Choroidal Effusions
2030941.note: Finding of fluid accumulation between the CHOROID and the SCLERA.

2030942.name: Meibomian Gland Dysfunction
2030942.note: A chronic dysfunction of MEIBOMIAN GLANDS characterized by altered tear film stability and function due to a decrease or alteration in lipid quality/content in meibum. It is often associated with evaporative-type DRY EYE SYNDROME.

2030943.name: Optic Nerve Hypoplasia
2030943.note: A group of rare genetic disorders characterized by underdeveloped OPTIC NERVES, resulting in increased incidences of vision impairment, CONGENITAL NYSTAGMUS and STRABISMUS. It may be syndromic, and is often associated with CNS malformations.

2030944.name: Familial Exudative Vitreoretinopathies
2030944.note: A group of inherited disorders characterized by incomplete development of the retinal vasculature. Its severity can vary from complete blindness in infancy, to mild or no visual problems, where small areas of vascular defects are observable only by FLUORESCEIN ANGIOGRAPHY. Exudative vitreoretinopath

2030945.name: Retinal Arterial Macroaneurysm
2030945.note: An acquired dilation of the retinal artery often associated with systemic HYPERTENSION.

2030946.name: Stargardt Disease
2030946.note: A juvenile-onset macular dystrophy characterized by progressive loss of VISUAL ACUITY with normal acuity in peripheral VISUAL FIELDS. Other associated clinical features may include LIPOFUSCIN fundus autofluorescence, atrophy of the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM, loss of color vision, PHOTOPHOBIA and PA

2030947.name: White Dot Syndromes
syn: Acute Idiopathic Blind Spot Enlargement Syndrome
Acute Posterior Multifocal Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy
2030947.note: A group of idiopathic multifocal posterior uveitis syndromes involving the CHOROID; RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM; and RETINA. They are characterized by multiple lesions of hypoautofluorescent dots in the FUNDUS OCULI and reduced VISUAL ACUITY. Several entities including BIRDSHOT CHORIORETINOPATHY are

2030948.name: Multifocal Choroiditis
2030948.note: A multifocal uveitis syndrome involving the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM and capillary layer of the CHOROID. It is characterized by chronic UVEITIS and multiple CHOROID lesions referred to as white dots, blurry vision, floaters, sensitivity to light, blind spots, and eye discomfort.

2030949.name: Birdshot Chorioretinopathy
2030949.note: A form of chorioretinitis characterized by multiple small, cream-colored LESIONS, symmetrically scattered mainly around the OPTIC DISK. These lesions are the most distinctive sign and often appear at the level of the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM but, on occasion, suggest an even deeper infiltration an

2030954.name: Locked-In Syndrome
2030954.note: Acquired neuromuscular disorder characterized by complete paralysis of voluntary muscles and lower CRANIAL NERVES except for limited voluntary eye movements. It is due to various cerebrospinal disconnections at or near the PONS and the POSTERIOR CRANIAL FOSSA, typically secondary to pontine hemorrha

2030956.name: Cytokine Release Syndrome
2030956.note: A severe immune reaction characterized by excessive release of CYTOKINES. Symptoms include DYSPNEA; FEVER; HEADACHE; HYPOTENSION; NAUSEA; RASH; TACHYCARDIA; HYPOXIA; HYPERFERRITINEMIA, and MULTIPLE ORGAN FAILURE. It is associated with viral infections, SEPSIS; AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES and a variety of fa

2030958.name: Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma
2030958.note: A rare, aggressive brain tumor that forms in the GLIAL CELLS in the PONS.

2030960.name: Asthma-Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Overlap Syndrome
syn: Asthma Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Overlap Syndrome
2030960.note: Syndrome with clinical features of both ASTHMA and COPD.

2030965.name: Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy
2030965.note: Sudden death in a patient with EPILEPSY associated with SEIZURES and seizure-related symptoms (e.g., APNEA; HYPOXEMIA) without other identifiable accidental causes (e.g., DROWNING; WOUNDS AND INJURIES).

2031003.name: Undiagnosed Diseases
2031003.note: Rare and common diseases lacking a diagnosis.

2031016.name: Synucleinopathies
2031016.note: Neurodegenerative disorders involving deposition of abnormal ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN in dopaminergic neurons and glial cells in the brain. Pathological aggregations of alpha-synuclein proteins results in LEWY BODIES and Lewy neurites; melanin granules in the SUBSTANTIA NIGRA and LOCUS COERULEUS; and glial c

2031018.name: Shoulder Dystocia
2031018.note: Obstetric complication during OBSTETRIC DELIVERY in which exit of the fetus is delayed due to physical obstruction involving fetal shoulder(s).

2031022.name: Specific Language Disorder
2031022.note: Language disorder that delays the mastery of oral language skills or in children who have no hearing loss or other developmental delays.

2031025.name: Mandibular Nerve Injuries
2031025.note: Traumatic injuries to the MANDIBULAR NERVE and its branches. Note that marginal mandibular nerve injury is a type of FACIAL NERVE INJURIES. Injuries to LINGUAL NERVE branch of mandibular nerve is LINGUAL NERVE INJURIES.

2031036.name: Post-Cardiac Arrest Syndrome
2031036.note: A reperfusion syndrome characterized by various pathophysiological processes after CARDIAC ARREST. It may include post-cardiac arrest brain injury (HYPOXIA-ISCHEMIA, BRAIN), cardiocirculatory dysfunction, (e.g., systemic ISCHEMIA), HYPERGLYCEMIA; MULTIPLE ORGAN FAILURE and delayed death.

2031040.name: Bone Marrow Failure Disorders
2031040.note: Inherited or acquired diseases characterized by insufficient and/or dysplastic blood cells.

2031041.name: Congenital Bone Marrow Failure Syndromes
2031041.note: Inherited syndromes characterized by deficiency or absence of various blood cells due to mutations that affect HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS development and proliferation.

2031043.name: Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome
syn: Pancreatic Insufficiency and Bone Marrow Dysfunction
2031043.note: An inherited syndrome characterized by EXOCRINE PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY; hematologic abnormalities (e.g., bone marrow hypoplasia), and skeletal abnormalities (e.g., metaphyseal chondroplasia). GERMLINE MUTATIONS in the SBDS gene are associated with Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome.

2031050.name: Hepatic Infarction
2031050.note: Formation of infarct resulting from obstruction of HEPATIC ARTERY and/or PORTAL VEIN most often after LIVER TRANSPLANTATION or hepatobiliary surgery.

2031051.name: Autoimmune Pancreatitis
2031051.note: Chronic pancreatitis associated with autoimmune diseases.

2031054.name: Ototoxicity
2031054.note: Damage to the EAR or its function secondary to exposure to toxic substances such as drugs used in CHEMOTHERAPY; IMMUNOTHERAPY; or RADIATION.

2031059.name: Toxic Optic Neuropathy
2031059.note: Damage to the eye or its function (e.g., VISUAL IMPAIRMENT) due to OPTIC NERVE damage secondary to toxic substances such as drugs used in CHEMOTHERAPY; IMMUNOTHERAPY; or RADIATION.

2031060.name: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
2031060.note: A progressive rare pulmonary disease characterized by high blood pressure in the PULMONARY ARTERY.

2031061.name: Myotoxicity
2031061.note: Damage to the muscle or its function secondary to toxic substances such as drugs used in CHEMOTHERAPY; IMMUNOTHERAPY; or RADIATION.

2031063.name: Pancreatitis, Acute Hemorrhagic
2031063.note: An acute INFLAMMATION of the PANCREAS in which the initial edematous pancreatitis evolved into necrosis accompanied by HEMORRHAGE.

2031070.name: Accidental Injuries
2031070.note: Injuries resulting from events or circumstances that are unforeseen, unplanned, unanticipated, and without premeditation.

2031084.name: Primary Immunodeficiency Diseases
2031084.note: Genetic immunologic deficiency diseases and syndromes due to mutations in genes involved in IMMUNITY generally characterized by an increased susceptibility to infectious diseases. They are often associated with AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE manifestations.

2031085.name: Hereditary Complement Deficiency Diseases
2031085.note: Genetic disorders due to mutations in genes involved in COMPLEMENT SYSTEM PROTEINS. They are often classified into distinct pathway of complement activation where causative mutations are found (e.g., classical pathway, lectin pathway, alternative pathway, and terminal complement pathway).

2031119.name: Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions
syn: LSIL, Low Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion
LSIL, Low Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions
HSIL, High Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion
2031119.note: A cytological test finding that shows abnormal lesions of SQUAMOUS EPITHELIAL cells.

2051966.name: Internal Hernia
2051966.note: A protrusion of an internal abdominal organ through a hole in an anatomical structure such as a muscle or a membrane. For instance, in paraduodenal hernia the SMALL INTESTINE herniates through an opening in the MESENTERIES. It includes intra-abdominal and diaphragmatic hernias. In abdominal hernia a

2051967.name: Paraduodenal Hernia
2051967.note: A protrusion of the SMALL INTESTINE through an opening in the MESENTERY.

2051972.name: Kimura Disease
2051972.note: A chronic inflammatory disease characterized by benign enlargement of cervical LYMPH NODE and SALIVARY GLANDS with increased levels of IMMUNOGLOBULIN E. Unlike ANGIOLYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA WITH EOSINOPHILIA it involves eosinophil infiltrates in lymph node and salivary glands and mostly found in Asian m

2051985.name: Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip
2051985.note: Dislocation of the HIP JOINT from an abnormal FEMORAL HEAD to the ACETABULUM relationship. It is most often due to ligamentous laxity, abnormal positioning of the joint and various other developmental, congenital factors, and method of delivery (e.g., OLIGOHYDRAMNIOS). When dislocation is diagnosed

2051999.name: Warburg Effect, Oncologic
2051999.note: An observation in neoplastic cellular transformation, characterized by an increased glucose uptake via glycolytic activities resulting in an increased LACTATE production under aerobic microenvironment.

2052000.name: Ovarian Torsion
2052000.note: A condition that occurs when an ovary twists around the ligaments that hold it in place. This twisting can cut off blood flow. It usually affects only one ovary.

2052001.name: Aortic Valve Disease
2052001.note: Diseases involving the AORTIC VALVE functionality. Aortic valve disease often results in a backward and/or regurgitated blood flow into the LEFT VENTRICLE or a decreased blood flow from the heart. It includes congenital (e.g., bicuspid aortic valve), syndromic, and acquired (e.g., age-related, infec

2052002.name: Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease
2052002.note: Congenital heart valve defects where the AORTIC VALVE has two instead of normal three cusps. It is often associated with AORTIC REGURGITATION and AORTIC INSUFFICIENCY.

2052003.name: Quadricuspid Aortic Valve
2052003.note: Congenital malformation where the AORTIC VALVE has four instead of three cusps. It is often associated with AORTIC REGURGITATION and AORTIC VALVE STENOSIS.

2052004.name: Aortico-Ventricular Tunnel
2052004.note: Congenital anomaly characterized by an extra-cardiac channel connecting the AORTA either to the right or left HEART VENTRICLE.

2052009.name: Colitis-Associated Neoplasms
2052009.note: Colonic neoplasms associated with chronic inflammation conditions such as ULCERATIVE COLITIS and CROHN DISEASE.

2052012.name: Popliteal Artery Entrapment Syndrome
2052012.note: Entrapment of the POPLITEAL ARTERY in the LEG due to an abnormal course of the artery often associated with onset of development and/or overuse of the gastrocnemius or popliteus muscles on the back of the leg. It is most often associated with runners and other athletes with enlarged calf muscle that

2052013.name: Laminopathies
2052013.note: Congenital neuromuscular and muscular dystrophy diseases associated with mutations in the LAMIN TYPE A (Lamin A/C or LMNA gene). It includes CARDIOMYOPATHY, DILATED, 1A; CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, type 2B1; EMERY-DREIFUSS MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY, types 2 and 3; HUTCHINSON-GILFORD PROGERIA SYNDROME; LIP

2052014.name: Reinjuries
2052014.note: Damage inflicted on the same body part as a previous injury.

2052016.name: X-Linked Emery-Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy
syn: X Linked Emery Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy
Benign Scapuloperoneal Muscular Dystrophy with Early Contractures
Myopathy, X-Linked, With Postural Muscle Atrophy
Emery Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy 6, X Linked
2052016.note: Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy associated with mutations on emerin (EMD gene) or four and a half LIM domains 1 (FHL1 gene) both located on X chromosome.

2052017.name: Autosomal Emery-Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy
syn: Autosomal Dominant Emery Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy
Muscular Dystrophy With Early Contractures And Cardiomyopathy, Autosomal Dominant
Emery Dreifuss Muscular Dystrophy, Autosomal Dominant
2052017.note: Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy associated with mutations on LAMINS (LMNA gene).

2052019.name: Chronic Exertional Compartment Syndrome
2052019.note: Compartment syndrome characterized by pain in muscle groups with elevated compartment pressures due most often exercise training in athletes. Most often encountered chronic exertional compartment syndrome is in the anterior or deep posterior compartments of the lower leg in athletes in training simi

2052021.name: Ischemic Stroke
2052021.note: Stroke due to BRAIN ISCHEMIA resulting in interruption or reduction of blood flow to a part of the brain. When obstruction is due to a BLOOD CLOT formed within in a cerebral blood vessel it is a thrombotic stroke. When obstruction is formed elsewhere and moved to block a cerebral blood vessel (see C

2052022.name: Thrombotic Stroke
2052022.note: A type of ischemic stroke resulting from obstruction due to a BLOOD CLOT formed within in a CEREBRAL ARTERY often associated with ATHEROSCLEROSIS. A stroke due to a blood clot in a cerebral vein is a venous infarction (see VENOUS INFARCTION, BRAIN).

2052023.name: Embolic Stroke
2052023.note: An ischemic stroke due to a blood clot, emboli or other types of blockage which forms somewhere other than the brain and subsequently travels near and restricts blood flow to the brain. Most often the origin of the clot is from the heart and is referred to as cardioembolic stroke.

2052025.name: Hemorrhagic Stroke
2052025.note: Stroke due to rupture of a weakened blood vessel in the brain (e.g., CEREBRAL HEMISPHERES; CEREBELLUM; SUBARACHNOID SPACE).

2052029.name: Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava
2052029.note: Finding of the SUPERIOR VENA CAVA on the left instead of the usual right side of the ASCENDING AORTA. In bilateral superior vena cava it is found on both sides.

2052044.name: Opiate Overdose
2052044.note: Accidental or deliberate use of an OPIOID in excess of normal dosage. It includes overdose for prescription and illicit opioids.

2052053.name: Tinea Cruris
2052053.note: Fungal infection of the groin. The main causative fungus is TRICHOPHYTON.

2052055.name: Reinfection
2052055.note: Infection by the same infectious agent following a recovery. Reinfection may be by a different strain or the same strain.

2052057.name: Cardiac Papillary Fibroelastoma
2052057.note: Primary tumors, predominantly of the CARDIAC VALVES, characterized by multiple papillary frond structures. Although histologically benign, they may result in complications (e.g., valve dysfunction, EMBOLISM; STROKE; and SUDDEN DEATH).

2052060.name: Chemotherapy-Related Cognitive Impairment
2052060.note: The diminished or impaired mental and/or intellectual function associated with the chemical treatment of cancer.

2052064.name: Semicircular Canal Dehiscence
syn: Dehiscence of the Superior Semicircular Canal
Dehiscence of the Posterior Semicircular Canal
Dehiscence of the Lateral Semicircular Canal
2052064.note: A vestibular disorder caused by a pathologic third window into the BONY LABYRINTH (in contrast to the normal ROUND WINDOW OF EAR and the OVAL WINDOW OF EAR). It can present with autophony, sound- or pressure-induced VERTIGO, and chronic disequilibrium among other vestibulocochlear symptoms.(From: Se

2052074.name: Hyperthermia
2052074.note: An abnormal elevation of body temperature, usually as a result of inability to regulate core body temperature due to non-pathologic factors.

2052075.name: Phytoplasma Disease
2052075.note: Plant diseases caused by PHYTOPLASMA bacteria.

2052076.name: Plant Necrosis and Chlorosis
2052076.note: Plant diseases affecting mostly leaves where either plant cells or tissues are dead and/or collapsed (necrosis) or yellowed due to loss of CHLOROPHYLL (chlorosis).

2052122.name: Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome
syn: Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Bunyavirus Infection
2052122.note: A tick-borne infection with SEVERE FEVER WITH THROMBOCYTOPENIA SYNDROME BUNYAVIRUS of the genus Phlebovirus. It is associated with fever, THROMBOCYTOPENIA; LEUKOCYTOPENIA, and multiorgan dysfunction. It is found in parts of Asia including China, Japan, Korea and Vietnam and can be transmitted from i

2052131.name: Latent Infection
2052131.note: Delayed infection of the host by a dormant or inactive pathogen.

2052135.name: Hyperferritinemia
2052135.note: A finding of elevated serum level of FERRITIN. It is often associated with IRON OVERLOAD, repeated blood transfusions, malignancy, iron metabolic syndromes, virus infection, liver injury or dysfunction, and renal failure. Hyperferritinemia in iron metabolic syndromes (e.g., Still's diseases, and HEM

2052155.name: Mesothelioma, Malignant
2052155.note: A type of mesothelioma with a tendency to metastasize. Most tumors originate from either the PLEURA or PERITONEUM, tumors may also originate in the PERICARDIUM or testicular tissue. It is associated with ASBESTOS exposure. Somatic mutations identified in WT1, BCL10, CDKN2A, NF2, and BAP1 genes are a

2052179.name: COVID-19
2052179.note: A viral disorder generally characterized by high FEVER; COUGH; DYSPNEA; CHILLS; PERSISTENT TREMOR; MUSCLE PAIN; HEADACHE; SORE THROAT; a new loss of taste and/or smell (see AGEUSIA and ANOSMIA) and other symptoms of a VIRAL PNEUMONIA. A coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2 VIRUS, in the genus BETACORONAVIRUS is

2052189.name: Anosmia
2052189.note: Complete or severe loss of the subjective sense of smell. Loss of smell may be caused by many factors such as a cold, allergy, OLFACTORY NERVE DISEASES, viral RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (e.g., COVID-19), aging and various neurological disorders (e.g., ALZHEIMER DISEASE).

2052207.name: Viral Zoonoses
2052207.note: Viral infections that may be transmitted between non-human animals and HUMANS.

2052208.name: Bacterial Zoonoses
2052208.note: Bacterial infections that may be transmitted between non-human animals and HUMANS.

2052212.name: Blood-Borne Infections
2052212.note: Diseases due to or propagated by body fluids from hosts whose BLOOD has been contaminated with pathogens.

2052217.name: Mania
2052217.note: A state of elevated excitement with over-activity sometimes accompanied with psychotic symptoms (e.g., PSYCHOMOTOR AGITATION, inflated SELF ESTEEM and flight of ideas). It is often associated with mental disorders (e.g., CYCLOTHYMIC DISORDER; and BIPOLAR DISEASES).

2101040.name: Diaschisis
2101040.note: Loss or decreased brain function within intact region of the brain distant from the site of the lesion.

2101048.name: Radiation Fibrosis Syndrome
2101048.note: Radiation-induced fibrosis due to increased production of FIBRIN. Its symptoms include CERVICAL DYSTONIA, difficulty with speech and swallowing, swelling in the radiation field and TRISMUS.

2101076.name: Corticobasal Degeneration
2101076.note: Rare progressive neurological disorder characterized by Parkinsonism, cortical atrophy of multiple areas of the brain including the cerebral cortex and the basal ganglia, cognitive dysfunction and eye movement abnormalities.

2101078.name: Vascular Depression
2101078.note: Late-life depression associated with clinical or MRI defined cerebrovascular pathology.

2101083.name: MINOCA
syn: Myocardial Infarction and Non-obstructed Coronary Arteries
Myocardial Infarction and Non obstructed Coronary Arteries
Myocardial Infarction and Nonobstructed Coronary Arteries
Myocardial Infarction with Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries
Myocardial Infarction with Non obstructive Coronary Arteries
Myocardial Infarction with Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries
2101083.note: Myocardial infarction in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. CORONARY CIRCULATION disruption is due to various other factors such as ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUE and CORONARY VASOSPASM.

2101091.name: Persistent Infection
2101091.note: Infection which lasts for a long period with continuous display of clinical features. Persistent infection arises due to inability of host cells to clear primary infections completely. When persistent infections are cleared so that infection symptoms are under control they are often referred to as c

2101118.name: Body Odor
2101118.note: Strong or unusual odor related to the body. Occasional abnormal body odor may be a temporary effect of a metabolic change.

2101123.name: Axial Spondyloarthritis
2101123.note: A spectrum of chronic inflammatory conditions affecting the axial joints (e.g., SPINE), characterized by pain, stiffness of joints (ANKYLOSIS), reduced mobility and inflammation. When joint inflammation and damage are visible on regular X-rays it is called ANKYLOSING SPONDYLITIS; otherwise it is ref

2101124.name: Non-Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis
2101124.note: Chronic inflammatory conditions affecting the axial joints which cannot be detectable on x-rays. It is characterized by pain, stiffness of joints and inflammation. Non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis can have symptoms onset before the age of 45 and progress to more severe ANKYLOSING SPONDYLITIS

2101140.name: Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
2101140.note: A severe form of peripheral artery disease in which a hypoperfusion of the BLOOD through an organ or tissue is caused by occlusion of peripheral arterial vessels. It is associated with the presence of chronic ischemic rest pain, ulceration or GANGRENE.

2101156.name: Erythema Ab Igne
2101156.note: A cutaneous finding caused by prolonged heat exposure (e.g., space heater) and local heat injury (e.g., caused by LASER THERAPY). It is characterized by epidermal atrophy, reticular hyperpigmentation, and telangiectatic dermatosis.

2101161.name: Ambulatory Care Sensitive Conditions
2101161.note: Various health conditions in OUTPATIENT CARE settings for which adequate management, treatment and interventions delivered in the ambulatory care setting could potentially prevent HOSPITALIZATION.

2101175.name: Livedoid Vasculopathy
2101175.note: A rare cutaneous thrombotic disease due to occlusion of dermal vessels. It is characterized by purpuric maculae and ulcerations especially during summer which form scars called atrophie blanche. It is more associated with other syndromes (e.g., PROTEIN C DEFICIENCY; HYPERHOMOCYSTEINEMIA). Livedo ret

2101177.name: Intestinal Failure
2101177.note: Various intestinal diseases functionally defined as having reduced intestine function requiring PARENTERAL NUTRITION.

2101194.name: Mast Cell Activation Syndrome
syn: Non Clonal Mast Cell Activation Syndrome
Non Clonal Mast Cell Activation Disorder
2101194.note: A clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of mast cell disorders in which there is aberrant release of mast cell mediators with little to no accompanying proliferation of MAST CELLS.

2101196.name: Focal Facial Dermal Dysplasias
syn: Hereditary Symmetrical Aplastic Nevi of Temples
Focal Facial Dermal Dysplasia, Type II
2101196.note: A heterogenous group of genetic disorders characterized by scar-like atrophic lesions on the temple region of the head including preauricular area. Location of skin defects is likely related to defects in fusion of embryonic facial prominences during development of the face. Focal facial dermal dysp

2101201.name: Mast Cell Activation Disorders
2101201.note: A spectrum of primary, secondary, and idiopathic disorders involving MAST CELLS and characterized by an aberrant release of mast cell mediators which result in multiple and variable inflammatory and allergic symptoms. These disorders are associated with various mutations in tyrosine kinase KIT (PROT

2101206.name: Iron Deficiencies
2101206.note: Deficient amounts of iron in the body as a result of blood loss, diets deficient in iron, or an iron uptake or storage disorder.

2101211.name: Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia
2101211.note: A rare inherited genetic disorder, one form of HYPERLIPOPROTEINEMIA TYPE II, characterized by high level of LOW-DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN (LDL) which if not treated could elevate the chance of heart attack at an early age.

2101228.name: Neuroinflammatory Diseases
2101228.note: Diseases characterized by inflammation of the nervous tissue.

2101229.name: Thromboinflammation
2101229.note: Thrombosis with associated inflammation due to crosstalk between HEMOSTASIS and INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSES modulated by PLATELETS. It is associated with many diseases such as COVID-19; SICKLE CELL ANEMIA; and THROMBOPHLEBITIS.

2101267.name: Psychogenic Nonepileptic Seizures
2101267.note: Seizures caused by psychological factors without electrophysiological epileptic changes.

2101298.name: Weight Cycling
2101298.note: Repeated cycles of weight loss followed by weight gain.

2101299.name: Urogenital Diseases
2101299.note: Pathological processes of the URINARY TRACT and the reproductive system (GENITALIA).

2101300.name: Genital Diseases
2101300.note: Pathological processes involving the reproductive tract (GENITALIA).

2103143.name: Bronchiolitis Obliterans Syndrome
2103143.note: Bronchiolitis obliterans complication from allogenic HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION and LUNG TRANSPLANTATION.

2103144.name: Organizing Pneumonia
2103144.note: Any obstructive lung disease characterized by consolidated formation of GRANULATION TISSUE polyps within ALVEOLAR DUCTS AND ALVEOLI. It is classified as either primary (cryptogenic organizing pneumonia) or secondary organizing pneumonia. Secondary organizing pneumonia after transplantation is called

2103146.name: Platypnea Orthodeoxia Syndrome
2103146.note: Orthostatic dyspnea and fall of oxygen blood saturation when standing up which regress by assuming lying position.

2103147.name: Urticaria, Solar
2103147.note: Chromophore-dependent photodermatosis triggered by UV and visible light.

2103148.name: Pancreas Divisum
2103148.note: Anatomic variants in PANCREATIC DUCTS characterized by failure of fusion of the ventral and dorsal endodermal buds. Pancreas divisum results in inadequate or no communication between dorsal and ventral ducts. While most cases are asymptomatic, it may be associated with recurrent PANCREATITIS.

2103149.name: Crystalluria
2103149.note: Crystals in the URINE found in urinary sediment analysis. Urinary crystalline may be formed from various metabolites (e.g. CALCIUM OXALATES; CALCIUM PHOSPHATES; URATES) and drugs (e.g., SULPHADIAZINE; ACYCLOVIR; and TRIAMTERENE).

2103150.name: Tympanosclerosis
2103150.note: Calcification of the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE and MIDDLE EAR most often associated with chronic OTITIS MEDIA.

2103153.name: Calcinosis Cutis
2103153.note: Pathological deposition of calcium in the skin and subcutaneous tissue. Excessive calcification of the skin may be associated with underlying diseases that cause tissue damage (e.g. EHLERS-DANLOS SYNDROME; PSEUDOXANTHOMA ELASTICUM; ROTHMUND-THOMSON SYNDROME; and WERNER SYNDROME) or that cause abnorm

2103154.name: Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
2103154.note: A hypertrophic cardiomyopathy characterized by apical hypertrophy, typically LEFT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY (described as ace of spades sign), and deep T-wave inversions in EKG. Clinical symptoms include minor symptoms such as CHEST PAIN; DYSPNEA; and SYNCOPE to more complex symptoms such as ATRIAL FI

2103156.name: Exercise-Induced Allergies
2103156.note: Allergic reactions following a period of exercise. Elevated serum HISTAMINE and TRYPTASE levels and cutaneous MAST CELL degranulation are often associated with post-exertional allergic reactions which sometimes are triggered only in combination with prior consumption of a specific food such as wheat

2103157.name: Focal Cortical Dysplasia
2103157.note: Abnormal, non-neoplastic cell proliferation of the CEREBRAL CORTEX confined to an area in any lobe. Focal cortical dysplasia in the temporal lobe is associated with TEMPORAL LOBE EPILEPSY.

2103158.name: Hippocampal Sclerosis
2103158.note: Neuronal loss in the hippocampal regions of CA1 and CA4 and less severely CA2 and CA3. Additional loss of hippocampal stratum radiatum, hippocampal atrophy and ASTROGLIOSIS are common. Hippocampal sclerosis is associated with intractable TEMPORAL LOBE EPILEPSY.

2103160.name: Tuberculosis, Extrapulmonary
2103160.note: MYCOBACTERIUM infections of organs other than the lung.

2103161.name: Ventricular Outflow Obstruction, Left
syn: Dynamic Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction
2103161.note: Occlusion of the outflow tract in the LEFT VENTRICLE of the heart.

2103162.name: Ventricular Outflow Obstruction, Right
syn: Dynamic Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction
2103162.note: Occlusion of the outflow tract in the RIGHT VENTRICLE of the heart.

2103163.name: Isolated Systolic Hypertension
2103163.note: Hypertension with elevated systolic and normal diastolic blood pressure. It is the most common subtype in the elderly and is related to VASCULAR STIFFNESS and ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUE buildup.

2103165.name: Multiple Amputations, Traumatic
2103165.note: The loss of part of, or all of, more than one limb, or other appendages of the body due to injury or disease.

2103168.name: Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy
2103168.note: A CHOROID neovascularization characterized by serosanguineous retinal pigment epithelial detachment and leakage of serous exudate sometimes associated with aneurysmal polypoidal lesions.

2103170.name: Venom Hypersensitivity
2103170.note: Allergic reaction to venoms in insect bites and stings that is triggered by the immune system (i.e., HISTAMINE RELEASE).

2103171.name: Limbal Stem Cell Deficiency
2103171.note: Loss or disturbance of limbal STEM CELL function in the CORNEAL LIMBUS resulting in inability to self-renew CORNEAL EPITHELIUM and conjunctivalized corneal surface.

2103173.name: Knee Fractures
2103173.note: Fractures of bones at the KNEE and the KNEE JOINT.

2103175.name: Tibial Plateau Fractures
2103175.note: Fractures in the proximal portion of the TIBIA which acts as articular surface in the KNEE. They are often associated with knee ligament injuries (e.g., ACL TEARS).

2103176.name: Elbow Injuries
2103176.note: Injuries involving the ELBOW and ELBOW JOINT.

2103177.name: Radial Head and Neck Fractures
2103177.note: Fractures of the proximal head and/or neck of the RADIUS bone near the ELBOW JOINT.

2103179.name: Olecranon Fracture
2103179.note: Fractures of the OLECRANON PROCESS at the ELBOW JOINT.

2103180.name: Elbow Fractures
2103180.note: Fractures of the distal HUMERUS and the proximal ULNA and the RADIUS at the ELBOW JOINT, including the head, anatomic and surgical necks, and tuberosities.

2103181.name: Humeral Fractures, Distal
syn: Lateral Epicondyle Fractures of the Elbow
2103181.note: Fractures of the distal HUMERUS at the ELBOW JOINT.

2103183.name: Wrist Fractures
2103183.note: Fractures of the CARPAL BONES, the distal ULNA and/or RADIUS at the WRIST.

2103186.name: Femoral Fractures, Distal
2103186.note: Fractures of the distal FEMUR from the articular surface in the KNEE to the condylar region of the femur. A subset with a coronal-plane fracture of the distal femur condyle(s) is Hoffa Fracture.

2103187.name: Hoffa Fracture
2103187.note: Coronal plane fractures of the FEMUR condyle at the KNEE.

2103188.name: Proximal Femoral Fractures
2103188.note: Fractures of the proximal FEMUR at the HIP.

2103189.name: Dust Mite Allergy
2103189.note: Allergic rhinitis due to HOUSE DUST MITE ALLERGENS (e.g., Der p 1 of HOUSE DUST MITES) that is triggered by the immune system.

2103190.name: Allergic Fungal Sinusitis
2103190.note: Fungal infection in the PARANASAL SINUSES characterized by common allergy respiratory symptoms, recurrent NASAL POLYPS and/or ASTHMA with buildup of allergic MUCIN.

2103197.name: Chronic Kidney Diseases of Uncertain Etiology
syn: Chronic Kidney Disease of Nontraditional Etiology
CINAC Chronic Interstitial Nephritis in Agricultural Communities
Chronic Kidney Disease of Unknown Etiology
Chronic Kidney Disease of Unknown or Uncertain Etiology
CKDu Chronic Kidney Disease of Unknown Etiology
Chronic Interstitial Nephritis of Agricultural Communities
Kidney Disease of Unknown Cause in Agricultural Laborers
CKDu Chronic Kidney Diseases of Uncertain Etiology
Chronic Kidney Disease of Uncertain Etiology
2103197.note: Chronic kidney diseases not associated with traditional RISK FACTORS, e.g., TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS and HYPERTENSION, but rather with infectious diseases, exposure to environmental toxins, or other unknown factors. They are most prevalent in agricultural communities of DEVELOPING COUNTRIES.

2103225.name: Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Neoplasms
2103225.note: A urothelial carcinoma found in the tissue that lines the inner surface of the bladder. The bladder muscle is not involved.

2103237.name: Uterine Didelphys
2103237.note: An abnormality in which the MULLERIAN DUCTS do not properly join to form a single uterus during embryological development instead resulting in complete duplication of uterine horns and duplication of the cervix. Double uterus is associated with double cervix and vagina and sometimes renal agenesis.

2103238.name: Uterine Duplication Anomalies
2103238.note: A group of anomalies in which the UTERUS is duplicated due to abnormal fusion of the MULLERIAN DUCT during embryonic development.

2103239.name: Bicornuate Uterus
syn: Double Uterus and Longitudinal Vaginal Septum
2103239.note: A congenital uterine anomaly in which the UTERUS is divided into two uterine horns with a significant cleft at the uterine fundus due to partial fusion of the MULLERIAN DUCTS. Bicornuate uterus is sometimes associated with a longitudinal vaginal septum and abnormal development of renal tracts.

2103240.name: Septate Uterus
2103240.note: A congenital duplication of the UTERUS in which a septum is formed separating the uterus. The partitioning septum can also separate the CERVIX and VAGINA.

2103244.name: Breakthrough Infections
2103244.note: Infections by the same infectious agent (e.g., virus, fungus) occurring during exposure to prophylaxis, vaccine and treatment.

2103258.name: Mixed Dementias
2103258.note: Dementias caused by multiple etiologies, e.g., ALZHEIMER DISEASE, and VASCULAR DEMENTIA and/or LEWY BODY DISEASE.

2103259.name: Congenital Cranial Dysinnervation Disorders
2103259.note: Congenital neurodevelopmental diseases characterized by abnormal eye, eyelid, and facial movements. Congenital cranial dysinnervation disorders (CCDDs) are caused by abnormal innervation of CRANIAL NERVES (e.g., CNs III, IV and VI) resulting in aplasia or hypoplasia of the ocular and facial musculat

2103261.name: Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome
syn: PASC Post Acute Sequelae of COVID-19
2103261.note: Post acute stage of COVID-19 virus infection including signs, symptoms, and conditions that continue or develop after acute COVID-19 infection. Persistent symptoms may include FATIGUE; DYSPNEA; and MEMORY LOSS.

2103262.name: Post-Infectious Disorders
syn: Post Active Phase of Infection Syndrome
2103262.note: Debilitating disorder characterized by fatigue and other symptoms related to cognitive, autonomous, and immune dysfunction experienced in the aftermath of infections.

2103266.name: Low Anterior Resection Syndrome
2103266.note: Postoperative complication after removal of the RECTUM (low anterior resection surgery or resection surgery to the lower part of the COLON). It includes disordered rectum function, e.g., frequent BOWEL MOVEMENT; FECAL INCONTINENCE; and CONSTIPATION.

2103272.name: Dropped Head Syndrome
2103272.note: Condition characterized by sagging of the head due to severe NECK MUSCLES weakness in the back of the neck. It may result in severe cervical KYPHOSIS called chin-on-chest deformity. Dropped head syndrome is most often associated with other diseases, e.g., PARKINSON'S DISEASE; STROKES; HEAD AND NECK

2103301.name: Chronic Inducible Urticaria
2103301.note: Chronic urticaria with identified triggering factor which is either physical, e.g., vibratory urticaria, or non-physical, e.g., aquagenic urticaria.

2103313.name: Developmental Defects of Enamel
2103313.note: Defects in normal AMELOGENESIS caused by any local, systemic, environmental, or genetic factors. Enamel defects resulting from demineralization of normally developed DENTAL ENAMEL is referred to as TOOTH DEMINERALIZATION.

2103314.name: Dental Enamel Hypomineralization
2103314.note: Reduced mineralization disorder of the DENTAL ENAMEL during development resulting in qualitative defects, e.g., discolored or chalky (soft) enamel.

2103315.name: Molar Hypomineralization
2103315.note: A type of developmental disturbance of AMELOGENESIS involving MOLARS of any type (obligatory) plus other teeth sometimes. It is characterized by demarcated enamel opacities with unknown systemic causation (idiopathic).

2103316.name: Popliteal Artery Aneurysm
2103316.note: An abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the POPLITEAL ARTERY located behind the KNEE JOINT.

2103317.name: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, Type IV
syn: Ehlers Danlos Syndrome, Sack Barabas Type
Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, Type IV, Autosomal Dominant
Ehlers Danlos Syndrome Type 4, Autosomal Dominant
2103317.note: A subtype of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) characterized by vascular pathologies, e.g., AORTIC DISSECTION in addition to common EDS findings, e.g., hyperextensible skin and joints, skin fragility and reduced wound healing capability. It is associated with mutations in collagen type III alpha 1 chain

2103318.name: Aortic Aneurysm, Thoracoabdominal
2103318.note: An abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of ABDOMINAL AORTA at the aortic hiatus.

2103319.name: Aneurysm, Ascending Aorta
2103319.note: An abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the ASCENDING AORTA.

2103320.name: Aneurysm, Aortic Arch
2103320.note: An abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the AORTIC ARCH.

2103321.name: Descending Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm
2103321.note: An abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the DESCENDING THORACIC AORTA.

2103322.name: Aortic Root Aneurysm
2103322.note: An abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the AORTIC ROOT.

2103323.name: Dissection, Thoracic Aorta
2103323.note: Dissection or a tear of the THORACIC AORTA. It includes aortic root dissection, ascending aortic dissection, aortic arch dissection and descending thoracic aortic dissection.

2103325.name: Dissection, Abdominal Aorta
2103325.note: Dissection or a tear of the ABDOMINAL AORTA. It includes thoracoabdominal aortic dissection at the aortic hiatus.

2103329.name: Dissection, Blood Vessel
2103329.note: A tear or separation of the layers by a blood vessel typically involving vessels under pressure, i.e., ARTERIES, e.g., AORTA. Tearing of the TUNICA INTIMA layer of a blood vessel may lead to interstitial HEMORRHAGE. Dissection between the tunica intima and TUNICA MEDIA causes luminal occlusion. Diss

2103330.name: Aortic Intramural Hematoma
2103330.note: An atypical form of AORTIC DISSECTION in which subintimal dissection of the aortic TUNICA MEDIA without initial laceration of the aortic TUNICA INTIMA. It may begin from a rupture of the VASA VASORUM feeding aortic media.

2103331.name: Penetrating Atherosclerotic Ulcer
2103331.note: Ulceration of the AORTA by an ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUE by penetrating through and disrupting the internal elastic lamina of the TUNICA INTIMA.

2103333.name: Acute Aortic Syndrome
2103333.note: A group of aortic diseases presented with acute chest pain. It commonly includes AORTIC DISSECTION; AORTIC INTRAMURAL HEMATOMA; PENETRATING ATHEROSCLEROTIC ULCER and sometimes aortic aneurysms.

2103338.name: Sinistral Portal Hypertension
2103338.note: Portal hypertension of the SPLENIC VEIN due to occlusion caused by pancreatic pathology such as PANCREATIC PSEUDOCYST and PANCRATIC CANCER. Sinistral portal hypertension is associated with GASTRIC VARICES and acute HEMATEMESIS.

2103339.name: Idiopathic Noncirrhotic Portal Hypertension
2103339.note: Portal hypertension without known risk factors for hypertension, e.g., HEPATIC CIRRHOSIS and SCHISTOSOMIASIS. Idiopathic Noncirrhotic Portal Hypertension is most often associated with pathology in the PORTAL SYSTEM vasculature.

2103382.name: Overtraining Syndrome
