2103382.note: An accumulation of training and/or non-training stress resulting in short-term decrement in performance capacity with or without related physiological and psychological signs and symptoms of maladaptation in which restoration of performance capacity may take from several weeks to several months.(fro

2106378.name: Pathologic Complete Response
2106378.note: The disappearance of all signs of a disease upon REMISSION INDUCTION as supported by pathological examination.

2106396.name: Cytopenia
2106396.note: A deficiency in or reduction of the number of blood cells.

2106412.name: Olivary Degeneration
2106412.note: Degeneration of the OLIVARY NUCLEUS typically involving INFERIOR OLIVARY COMPLEX. It is associated with various syndromes and neurodegenerative disorders including hypertrophic olivary degeneration secondary to a Guillain-Mollaret triangle lesion.

2106427.name: Hypertensive Crisis
2106427.note: A severe, acute increase in BLOOD PRESSURE that may result in STROKE or MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA.

2106437.name: Cutaneous Malignant Melanoma
2106437.note: A primary melanoma that originates from atypical skin MELANOCYTES, especially from acquired and congenital MELANOCYTIC NEVI, and DYSPLASTIC NEVI.

2106459.name: Genetic Risk Score
2106459.note: Estimate of an individual's genetic liability to a trait or disease, calculated according to their genotype profile and relevant genome-wide association study data. (from Tutorial: a guide to performing polygenic risk score analyses. Nat Protoc. 2020 Sep;15(9):2759.)

2106472.name: Non-Erosive Reflux Disease
2106472.note: A type of gastroesophageal reflux disease with acid reflux-related symptoms, but that does not affect the integrity of the ESOPHAGEAL MUCOSA.

2106474.name: Aflatoxin Poisoning
2106474.note: Poisoning by AFLATOXINS most often associated with NAUSEA, abdominal pain, hepatotoxicity, immunosuppression, HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA and sometimes death.

2106475.name: Cold Urticaria
2106475.note: Various skin flares developing after exposure to cold temperature. While most are characterized by a limited episodic cutaneous condition characterized by URTICARIAL WHEALS, such as in allergic urticaria, other types are more severe and generalized and rarely familial, e.g., cryopyrin-associated per

2106476.name: Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome
2106476.note: Recurrent vomiting accompanied by nausea, abdominal pain and sometimes compulsive hot bathing behavior in chronic CANNABIS abuse.

2106478.name: Cystitis, Hemorrhagic
2106478.note: A diffuse inflammation of the URINARY BLADDER characterized by HEMATURIA due to bleeding from the bladder mucosa. Hemorrhagic cystitis is most often associated with infections, e.g., HUMAN ADENOVIRUS INFECIONS, but may also be due to other noninfectious etiologies: CHEMOTHERAPY with certain drugs, e

2106480.name: Mosquito-Borne Diseases
2106480.note: Infectious diseases transmitted by mosquito vectors. Mosquito-borne human viral diseases include Chikungunya, Dengue, viral encephalitis (e.g., Japanese and St. Louis types), West Nile, Yellow fever, Zika virus infections. Mosquito-borne human parasitic diseases include malaria and lymphatic filaria

2106483.name: Ross River Virus Infection
2106483.note: Virus diseases caused by Ross River virus of the ALPHAVIRUS genus. It is the most common endemic arboviral infection in Australia.

2106491.name: Imprinting Disorders
2106491.note: Disorders caused by transcriptional silencing of one parental gene allele (imprinted gene). Imprinted genes show genetic expression from only one parent of the gene pair through epigenetic processes with no change in the DNA sequence.

2106492.name: Chronic Cough
2106492.note: Cough lasting for greater than 8 weeks in adults potentially impacting HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE. Chronic cough generally is associated with eosinophilic airway inflammation (e.g., asthma (COUGH-VARIANT ASTHMA) and non-asthmatic BRONCHITIS, upper airway disorders, GERD and cough hypersensitivit

2106493.name: Cough-Variant Asthma
2106493.note: Asthma which is characterized by CHRONIC COUGH that is nonproductive without other asthmatic symptoms, e.g., WHEEZING, and PAROXYSMAL DYSPNEA. Cough-variant asthma is accompanied by AIRWAY HYPERSENSITIVITY and may progress to classical asthma without treatment.

2106494.name: Rhinosinusitis
2106494.note: Obstruction of sinus drainage into the NASAL CAVITY and inflammation of the NASAL MUCOSA in the PARANASAL SINUSES.

2106495.name: Cavernous Sinus Syndromes
2106495.note: Disease processes of the CAVERNOUS SINUS.

2106561.name: Hemosiderosis, Pulmonary
2106561.note: Iron deposition within the lung. Primary pulmonary hemosiderosis is characterized by HEMOPTYSIS; IRON-DEFICIENCY ANEMIA, and diffuse pulmonary hemorrhage as seen as transient pulmonary infiltrates on RADIOGRAPHY. Even though large amounts of iron are laid down in the lung, with normal or increased t

2106609.name: Patient-Ventilator Asynchrony
2106609.note: A time mismatch between patient's inspiratory effort and MECHANICAL VENTILATOR's inspiratory time.

2106647.name: Emotional Exhaustion
2106647.note: A state of feeling emotionally overextended and drained.

2106674.name: Retrograde Ejaculation
2106674.note: The flow of SEMINAL FLUID, from the posterior URETHRA, backwards into the BLADDER. Causes include injuries such as from SPINAL CORD INJURIES; DIABETIC NEUROPATHIES; surgeries in adjacent tissues such as AORTIC ANEURYSM surgeries and transurethral bladder neck incisions; or drug side effects.

2106676.name: Ejaculatory Dysfunction
2106676.note: The inability in males to ejaculate, or to have a normal time to EJACULATION.

2106682.name: Hearing Loss, Hidden
2106682.note: Hearing loss that is difficult to diagnose by standard hearing tests as it most often pertains to difficulties in hearing only in certain situations such as in noisy environments.

2108117.name: Coccidioidal Meningitis
2108117.note: Meningitis caused by a fungus of the genus COCCIDIOIDES, endemic to the SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES, south-central Washington State, and parts of Mexico and Central and South America.

2108118.name: Congenital Portosystemic Shunt
2108118.note: Congenital vascular malformation where the portal venous system blood (PORTAL SYSTEM) bypasses the liver sinusoids and drains into the systemic vein through a shunt.

2108119.name: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease
syn: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody Associated Disease
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Autoantibody Associated Disease
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein-Immunoglobulin G Associated Disorder
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Immunoglobulin G Associated Disorder
2108119.note: A disease in which serum antibodies are directed against MYELIN-OLIGODENDROCYTE GLYCOPROTEIN. MOGAD is typically associated with ACUTE DISSEMINATED ENCEPHALOMYELITIS; NEUROMYELITIS OPTICA; or TRANSVERSE MYELITIS.

2108143.name: Vaso-Occlusive Crises
2108143.note: A common complication of SICKLE CELL DISEASE arises when MICROVESSELS become obstructed by sickled red blood cells, leading to tissue and organ oxygen deprivation, resulting in acute episodes of pain.

2108145.name: Guttate Psoriasis
2108145.note: A skin condition, typically emerges suddenly and frequently occurs after an infection such as STREPTOCOCCAL INFECTION. While prevalent among children, it can also manifest in young adults. Its defining feature is the eruption of small, red, scaly patches that typically appear on the arms, legs, and

2108146.name: Nociplastic Pain
2108146.note: Pain originating from the disrupted function of pain-related sensory pathways in both the peripheral and central nervous system (CNS), leading to heightened sensitivity.

2108166.name: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease
2108166.note: Concept that the origins of lifestyle-related disease is formed at the time of fertilization, embryonic, fetal, and neonatal stages by the interrelation between genes and the environments (nutrition, stress, or environmental chemicals). (J Cardiol 2020 Jul;76(1):14-17)...

2108169.name: Polymorphic Catecholaminergic Ventricular Tachycardia
2108169.note: An arrhythmogenic disorder of the heart characterized by irregular heart rhythms in response to physical activity, stress, or catecholamine infusion, often transitioning into VENTRICULAR FIBRILLATION.

2108175.name: Cronkhite-Canada Syndrome
2108175.note: A nonfamilial polyposis syndrome that is characterized by the presence of diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis, skin hyperpigmentation, ALOPECIA; DIARRHEA, and PROTEIN-LOSING ENTEROPATHY. It was first reported by Cronkhite and Canada in 1955.

2108186.name: Uveal Melanoma
2108186.note: A rare, malignant MELANOMA arising from the melanocytes of the UVEA.

2108192.name: Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome
2108192.note: Disease that affects linguistic, VISUAL SPATIAL PROCESSING; EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, and MOOD regulation. Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome is associated with acquired lesions in the CEREBELLUM particularly in the posterior lobe and the vermis.

2108193.name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
2108193.note: Infection of the lungs in a patient who is not hospitalized or who has not resided in a long-term care facility for 14 days prior to the onset of symptoms. It is associated with some signs and symptoms of acute infection and is accompanied by the presence of an acute infiltrate on chest radiograph.(

2108197.name: Emphysematous Pyelonephritis
2108197.note: Acute often necrotizing pyelonephritis characterized by accumulation of gas within and around renal parenchyma. Emphysematous pyelonephritis is typically associated with bacterial infection in DIABETES MELLITUS and IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PATIENT.

2108199.name: Fetus-in-Fetu
2108199.note: Rare abnormality where a fetal part of an identical twin that stopped developing during gestation is found within a normally developing fetus. It is considered a TWIN PREGNANCY complication.

2108202.name: Cloacal Exstrophy
2108202.note: A rare congenital malformation that affects the development of the urinary, digestive, and REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEMS due to CLOACA malformations. In this condition, the large intestine develops outside the abdominal cavity, with the bladder connected to it. Due to this abnormal connection between the col

2108220.name: OEIS Complex
syn: Omphalocele Exstrophy Imperforate Anus Spinal Defects Complex
Omphalocele, Exstrophy Of The Bladder, Imperforate Anus, Spinal Abnormalities
Omphalocele, Exstrophy Of The Cloaca, Imperforate Anus, and Spinal Defects
2108220.note: A combination of defects comprising OMPHALOCELE, exstrophy of the cloaca, ANUS IMPERFORATE, and spinal defects. This rare complex is thought to represent the most severe end of a spectrum of birth defects, the exstrophy-epispadias sequence, which, in order of increasing severity, includes phallic se

2108222.name: Atrophic Maxilla
2108222.note: Loss of the MAXILLA bone mass and/or height due to natural edentulous maxilla (JAW, EDENTULOUS) or previous dental extractions. It may require a reconstruction via BONE TRANSPLANTATION and/or ALVEOLOPLASTY prior to a DENTAL IMPLANTATION.

2108223.name: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
syn: Agranular CD4+ CD56+ Hematodermic Neoplasm Tumor
Agranular CD4+ Natural Killer Cell Leukemia
2108223.note: A rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy derived from the precursors of PLASMACYTOID DENDRITIC CELLS. Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasms affect bone marrow and blood in addition to the lymph nodes, spleen, central nervous system, and skin.

2108224.name: Foveomacular Retinitis
2108224.note: A photochemical injury to retina tissues, usually at the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. It is commonly associated with sungazing, eclipse viewing, welding, or using a laser pointer without proper eye protection resulting in subjective visual disturbances (e.g., floaters) and reduced VISUAL ACUITY.

2108225.name: Oral Allergy Syndrome
2108225.note: Allergic reaction to certain foods, including fresh fruits, vegetables and nuts which share CROSS REACTIONS to allergens from trees, grass or pollens. Oral allergy syndrome is limited to itchy lips, mouth, and throat without severe ANAPHYLAXIS and is often associated with chronic EOSINOPHILIC ESOPHA

2108227.name: Diabesity
2108227.note: Co-occurrence of DIABETES MELLITUS and OBESITY largely due to diabetic complication from HYPERGLYCEMIA. Diabesity is also associated with faster deterioration of diabetic symptoms and complications.

2108239.name: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy
2108239.note: A rare form of dilated cardiomyopathy which causes heart enlargement and weakness during the last month of pregnancy or within five months of delivery.

2108908.name: Vestibular Migraine
2108908.note: Vertigo or major dizziness associated with abnormal brain activity in migraine affecting the VESTIBULAR SYSTEM.

2108911.name: Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness
2108911.note: A chronic functional disorder with vertigo, dizziness and unsteadiness triggered by vestibular episode and psychological stress. Unlike in BENIGN PAROXYSMAL POSITIONAL VERTIGO, the otoliths on the OTOLITHIC MEMBRANE are not involved in pathology of persistent postural-perceptual dizziness.

2108912.name: Perilymphatic Fistula
2108912.note: An abnormal connection between inner ear and the surrounding structures, resulting in a leakage of the PERILYMPH. It is most common in a whiplash-type head trauma injury. Perilymph or labyrinthine fistulas may result in dizziness and/or intermittent hearing loss.

2108913.name: Autoimmune Inner Ear Disease
2108913.note: Inner ear diseases caused by autoimmune reaction, characterized by audiovestibular dysfunction including TINNITUS; VERTIGO and progressive SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS. Autoimmune inner ear disease may coexist with other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., COGAN SYNDROME).

2108914.name: Cervical Dizziness
2108914.note: Presence of vestibular symptoms such as light-headedness, dizziness or unsteadiness associated with injuries and pathologies of the CERVICAL VERTEBRAE. Cervicogenic dizziness are often associated with a whiplash-type injury and neck pain.

2108932.name: Carotid Webs
2108932.note: The presence of one or more thin flap-like membranes arising from the posterior wall of the INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY bulb. While carotid webs can be asymptomatic, they may also be associated with TRANSIENT ISCHEMIC ATTACKS, and STROKE.

2108940.name: Autoimmune-Inflammatory Syndrome Induced by Adjuvants
syn: Autoimmune Inflammatory Syndrome Induced by Adjuvants
2108940.note: An immune disease that is triggered by a variety of ADJUVANTS. It results in a spectrum of autoimmune and inflammatory responses that lead to significant health challenges.

2109019.name: Pseudobulbar Affect
2109019.note: A condition that is characterized by episodes of sudden uncontrollable and inappropriate laughing or crying. It can result from certain neurological conditions or injuries that may impact the way the brain controls emotions.

2109020.name: Omphalocele
2109020.note: A congenital defect with major fissure in the ABDOMINAL WALL at the UMBILICUS resulting in the extrusion of VISCERA through the UMBILICUS. Unlike GASTROSCHISIS, omphalocele is covered with PERITONEUM but without overlying SKIN.

2109039.name: Pseudothrombocytopenia
2109039.note: A laboratory phenomenon where a low platelet count is observed due to the action of ANTICOAGULANTS such as EDTA causing platelet AGGLUTINATION.

2109053.name: Tuberculosis Disease
2109053.note: An advanced form of TUBERCULOSIS that is not being controlled by the IMMUNE SYSTEM. It requires prompt and effective treatment to prevent medical complications and transmission of the disease to other people.

2109061.name: Non-Melanoma Skin Neoplasms
2109061.note: Skin neoplasms that are not MELANOMA.

2109062.name: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma
syn: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Skin
2109062.note: A non-melanoma skin neoplasm that is one of the three principal types of skin cancer. It often presents as a hard lump or ulcer and is more likely to metastasize than BASAL CELL CARCINOMA.

68000006.name: Abdomen, Acute
68000006.note: A clinical syndrome with acute abdominal pain that is severe, localized, and rapid in onset. Acute abdomen may be caused by a variety of disorders, injuries, or diseases.

68000007.name: Abdominal Injuries
68000007.note: General or unspecified injuries involving organs in the abdominal cavity.

68000008.name: Abdominal Neoplasms
68000008.note: New abnormal growth of tissue in the ABDOMEN.

68000012.name: Abetalipoproteinemia
syn: Microsomal Triglyceride Transfer Protein Deficiency Disease
68000012.note: An autosomal recessive disorder of lipid metabolism. It is caused by mutation of the microsomal triglyceride transfer protein that catalyzes the transport of lipids (TRIGLYCERIDES; CHOLESTEROL ESTERS; PHOSPHOLIPIDS) and is required in the secretion of BETA-LIPOPROTEINS (low density lipoproteins or L

68000013.name: Congenital Abnormalities
68000013.note: Malformations of organs or body parts during development in utero.

68000014.name: Abnormalities, Drug-Induced
68000014.note: Congenital abnormalities caused by medicinal substances or drugs of abuse given to or taken by the mother, or to which she is inadvertently exposed during the manufacture of such substances. The concept excludes abnormalities resulting from exposure to non-medicinal chemicals in the environment.

68000015.name: Abnormalities, Multiple
68000015.note: Congenital abnormalities that affect more than one organ or body structure.

68000016.name: Abnormalities, Radiation-Induced
68000016.note: Congenital changes in the morphology of organs produced by exposure to ionizing or non-ionizing radiation.

68000022.name: Abortion, Spontaneous
68000022.note: Expulsion of the product of FERTILIZATION before completing the term of GESTATION and without deliberate interference.

68000026.name: Abortion, Habitual
68000026.note: Three or more consecutive spontaneous abortions.

68000027.name: Abortion, Incomplete
68000027.note: Premature loss of PREGNANCY in which not all the products of CONCEPTION have been expelled.

68000030.name: Abortion, Missed
68000030.note: The retention in the UTERUS of a dead FETUS two months or more after its DEATH.

68000031.name: Abortion, Septic
68000031.note: Any type of abortion, induced or spontaneous, that is associated with infection of the UTERUS and its appendages. It is characterized by FEVER, uterine tenderness, and foul discharge.

68000033.name: Abortion, Threatened
68000033.note: UTERINE BLEEDING from a GESTATION of less than 20 weeks without any CERVICAL DILATATION. It is characterized by vaginal bleeding, lower back discomfort, or midline pelvic cramping and a risk factor for MISCARRIAGE.

68000034.name: Abortion, Veterinary
68000034.note: Premature expulsion of the FETUS in animals.

68000037.name: Abruptio Placentae
68000037.note: Premature separation of the normally implanted PLACENTA from the UTERUS. Signs of varying degree of severity include UTERINE BLEEDING, uterine MUSCLE HYPERTONIA, and FETAL DISTRESS or FETAL DEATH.

68000038.name: Abscess
68000038.note: Accumulation of purulent material in tissues, organs, or circumscribed spaces, usually associated with signs of infection.

68000039.name: Peritonsillar Abscess
68000039.note: An accumulation of purulent material in the area between the PALATINE TONSIL and its capsule.

68000051.name: Acantholysis
68000051.note: Separation of the prickle cells of the stratum spinosum of the epidermis, resulting in atrophy of the prickle cell layer. It is seen in diseases such as pemphigus vulgaris (see PEMPHIGUS) and DARIER DISEASE.

68000052.name: Acanthosis Nigricans
68000052.note: A circumscribed melanosis consisting of a brown-pigmented, velvety verrucosity or fine papillomatosis appearing in the axillae and other body folds. It occurs in association with endocrine disorders, underlying malignancy, administration of certain drugs, or as in inherited disorder.

68000126.name: Achlorhydria
68000126.note: A lack of HYDROCHLORIC ACID in GASTRIC JUICE despite stimulation of gastric secretion.

68000130.name: Achondroplasia
syn: Achondroplasia, Severe, With Developmental Delay And Acanthosis Nigricans
Severe Achondroplasia with Developmental Delay and Acanthosis Nigricans
68000130.note: An autosomal dominant disorder that is the most frequent form of short-limb dwarfism. Affected individuals exhibit short stature caused by rhizomelic shortening of the limbs, characteristic facies with frontal bossing and mid-face hypoplasia, exaggerated lumbar lordosis, limitation of elbow extensio

68000137.name: Acid-Base Imbalance
68000137.note: Disturbances in the ACID-BASE EQUILIBRIUM of the body.

68000138.name: Acidosis
68000138.note: A pathologic condition of acid accumulation or depletion of base in the body. The two main types are RESPIRATORY ACIDOSIS and metabolic acidosis, due to metabolic acid build up.

68000140.name: Acidosis, Lactic
68000140.note: Acidosis caused by accumulation of lactic acid more rapidly than it can be metabolized. It may occur spontaneously or in association with diseases such as DIABETES MELLITUS; LEUKEMIA; or LIVER FAILURE.

68000141.name: Acidosis, Renal Tubular
syn: Renal Tubular Acidosis, Distal, Autosomal Dominant
Autosomal Dominant Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis
68000141.note: A group of genetic disorders of the KIDNEY TUBULES characterized by the accumulation of metabolically produced acids with elevated plasma chloride, hyperchloremic metabolic ACIDOSIS. Defective renal acidification of URINE (proximal tubules) or low renal acid excretion (distal tubules) can lead to co

68000142.name: Acidosis, Respiratory
68000142.note: Respiratory retention of carbon dioxide. It may be chronic or acute.

68000151.name: Acinetobacter Infections
68000151.note: Infections with bacteria of the genus ACINETOBACTER.

68000152.name: Acne Vulgaris
68000152.note: A chronic disorder of the pilosebaceous apparatus associated with an increase in sebum secretion. It is characterized by open comedones (blackheads), closed comedones (whiteheads), and pustular nodules. The cause is unknown, but heredity and age are predisposing factors.

68000153.name: Acne Keloid
68000153.note: A type of acneiform disorder in which secondary pyogenic infection in and around pilosebaceous structures ends in keloidal scarring. It manifests as persistent folliculitis of the back of the neck associated with occlusion of the follicular orifices. It is most often encountered in black or Asian me

68000160.name: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Diseases
68000160.note: Pathological processes of the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE, including the branches of COCHLEAR NERVE and VESTIBULAR NERVE. Common examples are VESTIBULAR NEURITIS, cochlear neuritis, and ACOUSTIC NEUROMA. Clinical signs are varying degree of HEARING LOSS; VERTIGO; and TINNITUS.

68000163.name: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
68000163.note: An acquired defect of cellular immunity associated with infection by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), a CD4-positive T-lymphocyte count under 200 cells/microliter or less than 14% of total lymphocytes, and increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections and malignant neoplasms. Clinical

68000168.name: Acrocephalosyndactylia
syn: Acrocephaly, Skull Asymmetry, and Mild Syndactyly

68000169.name: Acrodermatitis
68000169.note: Inflammation involving the skin of the extremities, especially the hands and feet. Several forms are known, some idiopathic and some hereditary. The infantile form is called Gianotti-Crosti syndrome.

68000170.name: Acrodynia
68000170.note: A condition seen primarily in childhood, most often resulting from chronic exposure to MERCURY COMPOUNDS which may result in encephalopathy and POLYNEUROPATHY. Clinical features include pain, swelling and pinkish discoloration of the fingers and toes, weakness in the extremities, extreme irritabilit

68000172.name: Acromegaly
68000172.note: A condition caused by prolonged exposure to excessive HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE in adults. It is characterized by bony enlargement of the FACE; lower jaw (PROGNATHISM); hands; FEET; HEAD; and THORAX. The most common etiology is a GROWTH HORMONE-SECRETING PITUITARY ADENOMA. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology

68000182.name: ACTH Syndrome, Ectopic
68000182.note: Symptom complex due to ACTH production by non-pituitary neoplasms.

68000187.name: Actinobacillosis
68000187.note: A disease characterized by suppurative and granulomatous lesions in the respiratory tract, upper alimentary tract, skin, kidneys, joints, and other tissues. Actinobacillus lignieresii infects cattle and sheep while A. equuli infects horses and pigs.

68000189.name: Actinobacillus Infections
68000189.note: Infections with bacteria of the genus ACTINOBACILLUS.

68000193.name: Actinomycetales Infections
68000193.note: Infections with bacteria of the order ACTINOMYCETALES.

68000196.name: Actinomycosis
68000196.note: Infections with bacteria of the genus ACTINOMYCES.

68000197.name: Actinomycosis, Cervicofacial
68000197.note: A form of ACTINOMYCOSIS characterized by slow-growing inflammatory lesions of the lymph nodes that drain the mouth (lumpy jaw), reddening of the overlying skin, and intraperitoneal abscesses.

68000208.name: Acute Disease
68000208.note: Disease having a short and relatively severe course.

68000210.name: Acute-Phase Reaction
68000210.note: An early local inflammatory reaction to insult or injury that consists of fever, an increase in inflammatory humoral factors, and an increased synthesis by hepatocytes of a number of proteins or glycoproteins usually found in the plasma.

68000219.name: Adams-Stokes Syndrome
68000219.note: A condition of fainting spells caused by heart block, often an atrioventricular block, that leads to BRADYCARDIA and drop in CARDIAC OUTPUT. When the cardiac output becomes too low, the patient faints (SYNCOPE). In some cases, the syncope attacks are transient and in others cases repetitive and pers

68000224.name: Addison Disease
68000224.note: An adrenal disease characterized by the progressive destruction of the ADRENAL CORTEX, resulting in insufficient production of ALDOSTERONE and HYDROCORTISONE. Clinical symptoms include ANOREXIA; NAUSEA; WEIGHT LOSS; MUSCLE WEAKNESS; and HYPERPIGMENTATION of the SKIN due to increase in circulating le

68000230.name: Adenocarcinoma
68000230.note: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

68000231.name: Adenocarcinoma, Papillary
68000231.note: An adenocarcinoma containing finger-like processes of vascular connective tissue covered by neoplastic epithelium, projecting into cysts or the cavity of glands or follicles. It occurs most frequently in the ovary and thyroid gland. (Stedman, 25th ed)

68000232.name: Adenofibroma
68000232.note: A benign neoplasm composed of glandular and fibrous tissues, with a relatively large proportion of glands. (Stedman, 25th ed)

68000235.name: Adenolymphoma
68000235.note: A benign tumor characterized histologically by tall columnar epithelium within a lymphoid tissue stroma. It is usually found in the salivary glands, especially the parotid.

68000236.name: Adenoma
68000236.note: A benign epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

68000237.name: Adenoma, Basophil
68000237.note: A small tumor of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland whose cells stain with basic dyes. It may give rise to excessive secretion of ACTH, resulting in CUSHING SYNDROME. (Dorland, 27th ed)

68000238.name: Adenoma, Chromophobe
68000238.note: A benign tumor of the anterior pituitary in which the cells do not stain with acidic or basic dyes.

68000239.name: Adenoma, Acidophil
68000239.note: A benign tumor, usually found in the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland, whose cells stain with acid dyes. Such pituitary tumors may give rise to excessive secretion of growth hormone, resulting in gigantism or acromegaly. A specific type of acidophil adenoma may give rise to nonpuerperal galactor

68000257.name: Adenoviridae Infections
68000257.note: Virus diseases caused by the ADENOVIRIDAE.

68000258.name: Adenovirus Infections, Human
68000258.note: Respiratory and conjunctival infections caused by 33 identified serotypes of human adenoviruses.

68000267.name: Tissue Adhesions
68000267.note: Pathological processes consisting of the union of the opposing surfaces of a wound.

68000270.name: Adie Syndrome
68000270.note: A syndrome characterized by a TONIC PUPIL that occurs in combination with decreased lower extremity reflexes. The affected pupil will respond more briskly to accommodation than to light (light-near dissociation) and is supersensitive to dilute pilocarpine eye drops, which induce pupillary constricti

68000274.name: Adiposis Dolorosa
68000274.note: A rare disease characterized by multiple tumor-like fatty deposits that press on nerves in various sites causing pain and weakness. Often these lipoma-like structures are located on the trunk and limbs but not on the face and hands.

68000291.name: Adnexal Diseases
68000291.note: Diseases of the uterine appendages (ADNEXA UTERI) including diseases involving the OVARY, the FALLOPIAN TUBES, and ligaments of the uterus (BROAD LIGAMENT; ROUND LIGAMENT).

68000292.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
68000292.note: A spectrum of inflammation involving the female upper genital tract and the supporting tissues. It is usually caused by an ascending infection of organisms from the endocervix. Infection may be confined to the uterus (ENDOMETRITIS), the FALLOPIAN TUBES; (SALPINGITIS); the ovaries (OOPHORITIS), the s

68000303.name: Adrenal Cortex Diseases
68000303.note: Pathological processes of the ADRENAL CORTEX.

68000306.name: Adrenal Cortex Neoplasms
68000306.note: Tumors or cancers of the ADRENAL CORTEX.

68000307.name: Adrenal Gland Diseases
68000307.note: Pathological processes of the ADRENAL GLANDS.

68000308.name: Adrenocortical Hyperfunction
68000308.note: Excess production of ADRENAL CORTEX HORMONES such as ALDOSTERONE; HYDROCORTISONE; DEHYDROEPIANDROSTERONE; and/or ANDROSTENEDIONE. Hyperadrenal syndromes include CUSHING SYNDROME; HYPERALDOSTERONISM; and VIRILISM.

68000309.name: Adrenal Insufficiency
68000309.note: Conditions in which the production of adrenal CORTICOSTEROIDS falls below the requirement of the body. Adrenal insufficiency can be caused by defects in the ADRENAL GLANDS, the PITUITARY GLAND, or the HYPOTHALAMUS.

68000310.name: Adrenal Gland Neoplasms
68000310.note: Tumors or cancer of the ADRENAL GLANDS.

68000312.name: Adrenal Hyperplasia, Congenital
68000312.note: A group of inherited disorders of the ADRENAL GLANDS, caused by enzyme defects in the synthesis of cortisol (HYDROCORTISONE) and/or ALDOSTERONE leading to accumulation of precursors for ANDROGENS. Depending on the hormone imbalance, congenital adrenal hyperplasia can be classified as salt-wasting, h

68000314.name: Adrenal Rest Tumor
68000314.note: Neoplasm derived from displaced cells (rest cells) of the primordial ADRENAL GLANDS, generally in patients with CONGENITAL ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA. Adrenal rest tumors have been identified in TESTES; LIVER; and other tissues. They are dependent on ADRENOCORTICOTROPIN for growth and adrenal steroid secre

68000326.name: Adrenoleukodystrophy
68000326.note: An X-linked recessive disorder characterized by the accumulation of saturated very long chain fatty acids in the LYSOSOMES of ADRENAL CORTEX and the white matter of CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. This disease occurs almost exclusively in the males. Clinical features include the childhood onset of ATAXIA; N

68000343.name: Afferent Loop Syndrome
68000343.note: A complication of gastrojejunostomy (BILLROTH II PROCEDURE), a reconstructive GASTROENTEROSTOMY. It is caused by acute (complete) or chronic (intermittent) obstruction of the afferent jejunal loop due to HERNIA, intussusception, kinking, VOLVULUS, etc. It is characterized by PAIN and VOMITING of BIL

68000347.name: Afibrinogenemia
68000347.note: A deficiency or absence of FIBRINOGEN in the blood.

68000355.name: African Horse Sickness
68000355.note: An insect-borne reovirus infection of horses, mules and donkeys in Africa and the Middle East; characterized by pulmonary edema, cardiac involvement, and edema of the head and neck.

68000357.name: African Swine Fever
68000357.note: A sometimes fatal ASFIVIRUS infection of pigs, characterized by fever, cough, diarrhea, hemorrhagic lymph nodes, and edema of the gallbladder. It is transmitted between domestic swine by direct contact, ingestion of infected meat, or fomites, or mechanically by biting flies or soft ticks (genus Orni

68000361.name: Agammaglobulinemia
68000361.note: An immunologic deficiency state characterized by an extremely low level of generally all classes of gamma-globulin in the blood.

68000370.name: Ageusia
68000370.note: Complete or severe loss of the subjective sense of taste, frequently accompanied by OLFACTION DISORDERS.

68000377.name: Agnosia
68000377.note: Loss of the ability to comprehend the meaning or recognize the importance of various forms of stimulation that cannot be attributed to impairment of a primary sensory modality. Tactile agnosia is characterized by an inability to perceive the shape and nature of an object by touch alone, despite unim

68000380.name: Agranulocytosis
68000380.note: A decrease in the number of GRANULOCYTES; (BASOPHILS; EOSINOPHILS; and NEUTROPHILS).

68000381.name: Agraphia
68000381.note: Loss or impairment of the ability to write (letters, syllables, words, or phrases) due to an injury to a specific cerebral area or occasionally due to emotional factors. This condition rarely occurs in isolation, and often accompanies APHASIA. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p48

68000382.name: Agricultural Workers' Diseases
68000382.note: Diseases in persons engaged in cultivating and tilling soil, growing plants, harvesting crops, raising livestock, or otherwise engaged in husbandry and farming. The diseases are not restricted to farmers in the sense of those who perform conventional farm chores: the heading applies also to those en

68000386.name: AIDS-Related Complex
68000386.note: A prodromal phase of infection with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Laboratory criteria separating AIDS-related complex (ARC) from AIDS include elevated or hyperactive B-cell humoral immune responses, compared to depressed or normal antibody reactivity in AIDS; follicular or mixed hyperplasi

68000387.name: Ainhum
68000387.note: Spontaneous autoamputation of the fourth or fifth toe.

68000402.name: Airway Obstruction
68000402.note: Any hindrance to the passage of air into and out of the lungs.

68000405.name: Akinetic Mutism
68000405.note: A syndrome characterized by a silent and inert state without voluntary motor activity despite preserved sensorimotor pathways and vigilance. Bilateral FRONTAL LOBE dysfunction involving the anterior cingulate gyrus and related brain injuries are associated with this condition. This may result in imp

68000417.name: Albinism
68000417.note: General term for a number of inherited defects of amino acid metabolism in which there is a deficiency or absence of pigment in the eyes, skin, or hair.

68000419.name: Albuminuria
68000419.note: The presence of albumin in the urine, an indicator of KIDNEY DISEASES.

68000425.name: Alcohol Amnestic Disorder
68000425.note: A mental disorder associated with chronic ethanol abuse (ALCOHOLISM) and nutritional deficiencies characterized by short term memory loss, confabulations, and disturbances of attention. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1139)

68000430.name: Alcohol Withdrawal Delirium
68000430.note: An acute organic mental disorder induced by cessation or reduction in chronic alcohol consumption. Clinical characteristics include CONFUSION; DELUSIONS; vivid HALLUCINATIONS; TREMOR; agitation; insomnia; and signs of autonomic hyperactivity (e.g., elevated blood pressure and heart rate, dilated pup

68000435.name: Alcoholic Intoxication
68000435.note: An acute brain syndrome which results from the excessive ingestion of ETHANOL or ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES.

68000437.name: Alcoholism
68000437.note: A primary, chronic disease with genetic, psychosocial, and environmental factors influencing its development and manifestations. The disease is often progressive and fatal. It is characterized by impaired control over drinking, preoccupation with the drug alcohol, use of alcohol despite adverse cons

68000453.name: Aleutian Mink Disease
68000453.note: A slow progressive disease of mink caused by the ALEUTIAN MINK DISEASE VIRUS. It is characterized by poor reproduction, weight loss, autoimmunity, hypergammaglobulinemia, increased susceptibility to bacterial infections, and death from renal failure. The disease occurs in all color types, but mink w

68000471.name: Alkalosis
68000471.note: A pathological condition that removes acid or adds base to the body fluids.

68000472.name: Alkalosis, Respiratory
68000472.note: A state due to excess loss of carbon dioxide from the body. (Dorland, 27th ed)

68000474.name: Alkaptonuria
68000474.note: An inborn error of amino acid metabolism resulting from a defect in the enzyme HOMOGENTISATE 1,2-DIOXYGENASE, an enzyme involved in the breakdown of PHENYLALANINE and TYROSINE. It is characterized by accumulation of HOMOGENTISIC ACID in the urine, OCHRONOSIS in various tissues, and ARTHRITIS.

68000505.name: Alopecia
68000505.note: Absence of hair from areas where it is normally present.

68000506.name: Alopecia Areata
68000506.note: Loss of scalp and body hair involving microscopically inflammatory patchy areas.

68000507.name: Mucinosis, Follicular
68000507.note: A disease of the pilosebaceous unit, presenting clinically as grouped follicular papules or plaques with associated hair loss. It is caused by mucinous infiltration of tissues, and usually involving the scalp, face, and neck. It may be primary (idiopathic) or secondary to mycosis fungoides or reticu

68000532.name: Altitude Sickness
68000532.note: Multiple symptoms associated with reduced oxygen at high ALTITUDE.

68000542.name: Alveolitis, Extrinsic Allergic
68000542.note: A common interstitial lung disease caused by hypersensitivity reactions of PULMONARY ALVEOLI after inhalation of and sensitization to environmental antigens of microbial, animal, or chemical sources. The disease is characterized by lymphocytic alveolitis and granulomatous pneumonitis.

68000544.name: Alzheimer Disease
68000544.note: A degenerative disease of the BRAIN characterized by the insidious onset of DEMENTIA. Impairment of MEMORY, judgment, attention span, and problem solving skills are followed by severe APRAXIAS and a global loss of cognitive abilities. The condition primarily occurs after age 60, and is marked pathol

68000550.name: Amblyopia
68000550.note: A nonspecific term referring to impaired vision. Major subcategories include stimulus deprivation-induced amblyopia and toxic amblyopia. Stimulus deprivation-induced amblyopia is a developmental disorder of the visual cortex. A discrepancy between visual information received by the visual cortex fro

68000562.name: Amebiasis
68000562.note: Infection with any of various amebae. It is an asymptomatic carrier state in most individuals, but diseases ranging from chronic, mild diarrhea to fulminant dysentery may occur.

68000564.name: Ameloblastoma
68000564.note: An immature epithelial tumor of the JAW originating from the epithelial rests of Malassez or from other epithelial remnants of the ENAMEL from the developmental period. It is a slowly growing tumor, usually benign, but displays a marked propensity for invasive growth.

68000567.name: Amelogenesis Imperfecta
68000567.note: A clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of hereditary conditions characterized by malformed DENTAL ENAMEL, usually involving DENTAL ENAMEL HYPOPLASIA and/or TOOTH HYPOMINERALIZATION.

68000592.name: Amino Acid Metabolism, Inborn Errors
syn: Inherited Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism
68000592.note: Disorders affecting amino acid metabolism. The majority of these disorders are inherited and present in the neonatal period with metabolic disturbances (e.g., ACIDOSIS) and neurologic manifestations. They are present at birth, although they may not become symptomatic until later in life.

68000608.name: Renal Aminoacidurias
68000608.note: A group of inherited kidney disorders characterized by the abnormally elevated levels of AMINO ACIDS in URINE. Genetic mutations of transport proteins result in the defective reabsorption of free amino acids at the PROXIMAL RENAL TUBULES. Renal aminoaciduria are classified by the specific amino acid

68000647.name: Amnesia
68000647.note: Pathologic partial or complete loss of the ability to recall past experiences (AMNESIA, RETROGRADE) or to form new memories (AMNESIA, ANTEROGRADE). This condition may be of organic or psychologic origin. Organic forms of amnesia are usually associated with dysfunction of the DIENCEPHALON or HIPPOCAM

68000648.name: Amnesia, Retrograde
68000648.note: Loss of the ability to recall information that had been previously encoded in memory prior to a specified or approximate point in time. This process may be organic or psychogenic in origin. Organic forms may be associated with CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA; CEREBROVASCULAR ACCIDENTS; SEIZURES; DEMENTIA; and

68000652.name: Amniotic Band Syndrome
68000652.note: A disorder present in the newborn infant in which constriction rings or bands, causing soft tissue depressions, encircle digits, extremities, or limbs and sometimes the neck, thorax, or abdomen. They may be associated with intrauterine amputations.

68000673.name: Amputation, Traumatic
68000673.note: Loss of a limb or other bodily appendage by accidental injury.

68000686.name: Amyloidosis
68000686.note: A group of sporadic, familial and/or inherited, degenerative, and infectious disease processes, linked by the common theme of abnormal protein folding and deposition of AMYLOID. As the amyloid deposits enlarge they displace normal tissue structures, causing disruption of function. Various signs and

68000690.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
syn: Motor Neuron Disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
68000690.note: A degenerative disorder affecting upper MOTOR NEURONS in the brain and lower motor neurons in the brain stem and SPINAL CORD. Disease onset is usually after the age of 50 and the process is usually fatal within 3 to 6 years. Clinical manifestations include progressive weakness, atrophy, FASCICULATIO

68000694.name: Anal Gland Neoplasms
68000694.note: Tumors or cancer of the anal gland.

68000699.name: Pain Insensitivity, Congenital
68000699.note: A syndrome characterized by indifference to PAIN despite the ability to distinguish noxious from non-noxious stimuli. Absent corneal reflexes and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY may be associated. Familial forms with autosomal recessive and autosomal dominant patterns of inheritance have been described. (Ad

68000707.name: Anaphylaxis
68000707.note: An acute hypersensitivity reaction due to exposure to a previously encountered ANTIGEN. The reaction may include rapidly progressing URTICARIA, respiratory distress, vascular collapse, systemic SHOCK, and death.

68000708.name: Anaplasia
68000708.note: Loss of structural differentiation and useful function of neoplastic cells.

68000711.name: Anaplasmataceae Infections
68000711.note: Infections with bacteria of the family ANAPLASMATACEAE.

68000712.name: Anaplasmosis
68000712.note: A disease usually in cattle caused by parasitization of the red blood cells by bacteria of the genus ANAPLASMA.

68000724.name: Ancylostomiasis
68000724.note: Infection of humans or animals with hookworms of the genus ANCYLOSTOMA. Characteristics include anemia, dyspepsia, eosinophilia, and abdominal swelling.

68000740.name: Anemia
68000740.note: A reduction in the number of circulating ERYTHROCYTES or in the quantity of HEMOGLOBIN.

68000741.name: Anemia, Aplastic
68000741.note: A form of anemia in which the bone marrow fails to produce adequate numbers of peripheral blood elements.

68000742.name: Anemia, Dyserythropoietic, Congenital
syn: Hereditary Erythroblast Multinuclearity with Positive Acidified Serum
Hereditary Erythroblastic Multinuclearity with Positive Acidified-Serum Test
68000742.note: A familial disorder characterized by ANEMIA with multinuclear ERYTHROBLASTS, karyorrhexis, asynchrony of nuclear and cytoplasmic maturation, and various nuclear abnormalities of bone marrow erythrocyte precursors (ERYTHROID PRECURSOR CELLS). Type II is the most common of the 3 types; it is often ref

68000743.name: Anemia, Hemolytic
68000743.note: A condition of inadequate circulating red blood cells (ANEMIA) or insufficient HEMOGLOBIN due to premature destruction of red blood cells (ERYTHROCYTES).

68000744.name: Anemia, Hemolytic, Autoimmune
68000744.note: Acquired hemolytic anemia due to the presence of AUTOANTIBODIES which agglutinate or lyse the patient's own RED BLOOD CELLS.

68000745.name: Anemia, Hemolytic, Congenital
68000745.note: Hemolytic anemia due to various intrinsic defects of the erythrocyte.

68000746.name: Anemia, Hemolytic, Congenital Nonspherocytic
68000746.note: Any one of a group of congenital hemolytic anemias in which there is no abnormal hemoglobin or spherocytosis and in which there is a defect of glycolysis in the erythrocyte. Common causes include deficiencies in GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE ISOMERASE; PYRUVATE KINASE; and GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE DEHYDROGENASE.

68000747.name: Anemia, Hypochromic
68000747.note: Anemia characterized by a decrease in the ratio of the weight of hemoglobin to the volume of the erythrocyte, i.e., the mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration is less than normal. The individual cells contain less hemoglobin than they could have under optimal conditions. Hypochromic anemia may be

68000748.name: Anemia, Macrocytic
68000748.note: Anemia characterized by larger than normal erythrocytes, increased mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH).

68000749.name: Anemia, Megaloblastic
68000749.note: A disorder characterized by the presence of ANEMIA, abnormally large red blood cells (megalocytes or macrocytes), and MEGALOBLASTS.

68000750.name: Anemia, Myelophthisic
68000750.note: Anemia characterized by appearance of immature myeloid and nucleated erythrocytes in the peripheral blood, resulting from infiltration of the bone marrow by foreign or abnormal tissue.

68000751.name: Anemia, Neonatal
68000751.note: The mildest form of erythroblastosis fetalis in which anemia is the chief manifestation.

68000752.name: Anemia, Pernicious
68000752.note: A megaloblastic anemia occurring in children but more commonly in later life, characterized by histamine-fast achlorhydria, in which the laboratory and clinical manifestations are based on malabsorption of vitamin B 12 due to a failure of the gastric mucosa to secrete adequate and potent intrinsic f

68000753.name: Anemia, Refractory
68000753.note: A severe sometimes chronic anemia, usually macrocytic in type, that does not respond to ordinary antianemic therapy.

68000754.name: Anemia, Refractory, with Excess of Blasts
syn: Refractory Anemia with Excess of Blasts
68000754.note: Chronic refractory anemia with granulocytopenia, and/or thrombocytopenia. Myeloblasts and progranulocytes constitute 5 to 40 percent of the nucleated marrow cells.

68000755.name: Anemia, Sickle Cell
syn: Sickling Disorder Due to Hemoglobin S
68000755.note: A disease characterized by chronic hemolytic anemia, episodic painful crises, and pathologic involvement of many organs. It is the clinical expression of homozygosity for hemoglobin S.

68000756.name: Anemia, Sideroblastic
68000756.note: Anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts containing excessive deposits of iron in the marrow.

68000757.name: Anencephaly
68000757.note: A malformation of the nervous system caused by failure of the anterior neuropore to close. Infants are born with intact spinal cords, cerebellums, and brainstems, but lack formation of neural structures above this level. The skull is only partially formed but the eyes are usually normal. This condit

68000782.name: Aneuploidy
68000782.note: The chromosomal constitution of cells which deviate from the normal by the addition or subtraction of CHROMOSOMES, chromosome pairs, or chromosome fragments. In a normally diploid cell (DIPLOIDY) the loss of a chromosome pair is termed nullisomy (symbol: 2N-2), the loss of a single chromosome is MON

68000783.name: Aneurysm
68000783.note: Pathological outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of any blood vessel (ARTERIES or VEINS) or the heart (HEART ANEURYSM). It indicates a thin and weakened area in the wall which may later rupture. Aneurysms are classified by location, etiology, or other characteristics.

68000784.name: Aortic Dissection
68000784.note: A tear in the inner layer of the AORTA leading to interstitial HEMORRHAGE, and splitting (dissecting) of the aortic TUNICA MEDIA layer. It typically begins with a tear in the TUNICA INTIMA layer.

68000785.name: Aneurysm, Infected
68000785.note: Aneurysm due to growth of microorganisms in the arterial wall, or infection arising within preexisting arteriosclerotic aneurysms.

68000787.name: Angina Pectoris
68000787.note: The symptom of paroxysmal pain consequent to MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA usually of distinctive character, location and radiation. It is thought to be provoked by a transient stressful situation during which the oxygen requirements of the MYOCARDIUM exceed that supplied by the CORONARY CIRCULATION.

68000788.name: Angina Pectoris, Variant
68000788.note: A clinical syndrome characterized by the development of CHEST PAIN at rest with concomitant transient ST segment elevation in the ELECTROCARDIOGRAM, but with preserved exercise capacity.

68000789.name: Angina, Unstable
68000789.note: Precordial pain at rest, which may precede a MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION.

68000793.name: Angioid Streaks
68000793.note: Small breaks in the elastin-filled tissue of the retina.

68000794.name: Angiokeratoma
68000794.note: A vascular, horny neoplasm of the skin characterized by TELANGIECTASIS and secondary epithelial changes including acanthosis and hyperkeratosis.

68000795.name: Fabry Disease
68000795.note: An X-linked inherited metabolic disease caused by a deficiency of lysosomal ALPHA-GALACTOSIDASE A. It is characterized by intralysosomal accumulation of globotriaosylceramide and other GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS in blood vessels throughout the body leading to multi-system complications including renal, card

68000796.name: Angiolymphoid Hyperplasia with Eosinophilia
68000796.note: Solitary or multiple benign cutaneous nodules comprised of immature and mature vascular structures intermingled with endothelial cells and a varied infiltrate of eosinophils, histiocytes, lymphocytes, and mast cells.

68000798.name: Angiomatosis
68000798.note: A condition with multiple tumor-like lesions caused either by congenital or developmental malformations of BLOOD VESSELS, or reactive vascular proliferations, such as in bacillary angiomatosis. Angiomatosis is considered non-neoplastic.

68000799.name: Angioedema
68000799.note: Swelling involving the deep DERMIS, subcutaneous, or submucosal tissues, representing localized EDEMA. Angioedema often occurs in the face, lips, tongue, and larynx.

68000820.name: Animal Diseases
68000820.note: Diseases that occur in VERTEBRATE animals.

68000839.name: Aniseikonia
68000839.note: A condition in which the ocular image of an object as seen by one eye differs in size and shape from that seen by the other.

68000844.name: Ankylosis
68000844.note: Fixation and immobility of a joint.

68000848.name: Anodontia
68000848.note: Congenital absence of the teeth. It may involve all (total anodontia) or only some of the teeth (partial anodontia, hypodontia), or six or more of the teeth (oligodontia) and both the deciduous and the permanent dentition, or only teeth of the permanent dentition.

68000849.name: Anomia
68000849.note: A language dysfunction characterized by the inability to name people and objects that are correctly perceived. The individual is able to describe the object in question, but cannot provide the name. This condition is associated with lesions of the dominant hemisphere involving the language areas, in

68000853.name: Anophthalmos
68000853.note: Congenital absence of the eye or eyes.

68000855.name: Anorexia
68000855.note: The lack or loss of APPETITE accompanied by an aversion to food and the inability to eat. It is the defining characteristic of the disorder ANOREXIA NERVOSA.

68000857.name: Olfaction Disorders
68000857.note: Impaired ability to smell. This may be caused by OLFACTORY NERVE DISEASES; PARANASAL SINUS DISEASES; viral RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS; CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA; SMOKING; and other conditions.

68000858.name: Anovulation
68000858.note: Suspension or cessation of OVULATION in animals or humans with follicle-containing ovaries (OVARIAN FOLLICLE). Depending on the etiology, OVULATION may be induced with appropriate therapy.

68000860.name: Hypoxia
68000860.note: Sub-optimal OXYGEN levels in the ambient air of living organisms.

68000868.name: Anterior Compartment Syndrome
68000868.note: Rapid swelling, increased tension, pain, and ischemic necrosis of the muscles of the anterior tibial compartment of the leg, often following excessive PHYSICAL EXERTION.

68000874.name: Anthracosilicosis
68000874.note: A form of pneumoconiosis caused by inhalation of dust that contains both CARBON and crystalline SILICON DIOXIDE. These foreign matters induce fibrous nodule formation in the lung.

68000881.name: Anthrax
68000881.note: An acute infection caused by the spore-forming bacteria BACILLUS ANTHRACIS. It commonly affects hoofed animals such as sheep and goats. Infection in humans often involves the skin (cutaneous anthrax), the lungs (inhalation anthrax), or the gastrointestinal tract. Anthrax is not contagious and can be

68001002.name: Anuria
68001002.note: Absence of urine formation. It is usually associated with complete bilateral ureteral (URETER) obstruction, complete lower urinary tract obstruction, or unilateral ureteral obstruction when a solitary kidney is present.

68001005.name: Anus Neoplasms
68001005.note: Tumors or cancer of the ANAL CANAL.

68001006.name: Anus, Imperforate
68001006.note: A congenital abnormality characterized by the persistence of the anal membrane, resulting in a thin membrane covering the normal ANAL CANAL. Imperforation is not always complete and is treated by surgery in infancy. This defect is often associated with NEURAL TUBE DEFECTS; MENTAL RETARDATION; and DO

68001014.name: Aortic Aneurysm
68001014.note: An abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of AORTA.

68001015.name: Aortic Arch Syndromes
68001015.note: Conditions resulting from abnormalities in the arteries branching from the ASCENDING AORTA, the curved portion of the aorta. These syndromes are results of occlusion or abnormal blood flow to the head-neck or arm region leading to neurological defects and weakness in an arm. These syndromes are asso

68001017.name: Aortic Coarctation
68001017.note: A birth defect characterized by the narrowing of the AORTA that can be of varying degree and at any point from the transverse arch to the iliac bifurcation. Aortic coarctation causes arterial HYPERTENSION before the point of narrowing and arterial HYPOTENSION beyond the narrowed portion.

68001018.name: Aortic Diseases
68001018.note: Pathological processes involving any part of the AORTA.

68001019.name: Aortic Rupture
68001019.note: The tearing or bursting of the wall along any portion of the AORTA, such as thoracic or abdominal. It may result from the rupture of an aneurysm or it may be due to TRAUMA.

68001020.name: Aortic Stenosis, Subvalvular
68001020.note: A pathological constriction occurring in the region below the AORTIC VALVE. It is characterized by restricted outflow from the LEFT VENTRICLE into the AORTA.

68001022.name: Aortic Valve Insufficiency
68001022.note: Pathological condition characterized by the backflow of blood from the ASCENDING AORTA back into the LEFT VENTRICLE, leading to regurgitation. It is caused by diseases of the AORTIC VALVE or its surrounding tissue (aortic root).

68001023.name: Aortic Valve Prolapse
68001023.note: The downward displacement of the cuspal or pointed end of the trileaflet AORTIC VALVE causing misalignment of the cusps. Severe valve distortion can cause leakage and allow the backflow of blood from the ASCENDING AORTA back into the LEFT VENTRICLE, leading to aortic regurgitation.

68001024.name: Aortic Valve Stenosis
68001024.note: A pathological constriction that can occur above (supravalvular stenosis), below (subvalvular stenosis), or at the AORTIC VALVE. It is characterized by restricted outflow from the LEFT VENTRICLE into the AORTA.

68001025.name: Aortitis
68001025.note: Inflammation of the wall of the AORTA.

68001028.name: Aortopulmonary Septal Defect
68001028.note: A developmental abnormality in which the spiral (aortopulmonary) septum failed to completely divide the TRUNCUS ARTERIOSUS into ASCENDING AORTA and PULMONARY ARTERY. This abnormal communication between the two major vessels usually lies above their respective valves (AORTIC VALVE; PULMONARY VALVE).

68001035.name: Aphakia
68001035.note: Absence of crystalline lens totally or partially from field of vision, from any cause except after cataract extraction. Aphakia is mainly congenital or as result of LENS DISLOCATION AND SUBLUXATION.

68001036.name: Aphakia, Postcataract
68001036.note: Absence of the crystalline lens resulting from cataract extraction.

68001037.name: Aphasia
68001037.note: A cognitive disorder marked by an impaired ability to comprehend or express language in its written or spoken form. This condition is caused by diseases which affect the language areas of the dominant hemisphere. Clinical features are used to classify the various subtypes of this condition. General

68001039.name: Aphasia, Broca
68001039.note: An aphasia characterized by impairment of expressive LANGUAGE (speech, writing, signs) and relative preservation of receptive language abilities (i.e., comprehension). This condition is caused by lesions of the motor association cortex in the FRONTAL LOBE (BROCA AREA and adjacent cortical and white

68001041.name: Aphasia, Wernicke
68001041.note: Impairment in the comprehension of speech and meaning of words, both spoken and written, and of the meanings conveyed by their grammatical relationships in sentences. It is caused by lesions that primarily affect Wernicke's area, which lies in the posterior perisylvian region of the temporal lobe of

68001044.name: Aphonia
68001044.note: Complete loss of phonation due to organic disease of the larynx or to nonorganic (i.e., psychogenic) causes.

68001049.name: Apnea
68001049.note: A transient absence of spontaneous respiration.

68001063.name: Appendiceal Neoplasms
68001063.note: Tumors or cancer of the APPENDIX.

68001064.name: Appendicitis
68001064.note: Acute inflammation of the APPENDIX. Acute appendicitis is classified as simple, gangrenous, or perforated.

68001068.name: Feeding and Eating Disorders
68001068.note: A group of disorders characterized by physiological and/or psychological disturbances in appetite or food intake.

68001072.name: Apraxias
68001072.note: A group of cognitive disorders characterized by the inability to perform previously learned skills that cannot be attributed to deficits of motor or sensory function. The two major subtypes of this condition are ideomotor (see APRAXIA, IDEOMOTOR) and ideational apraxia, which refers to loss of the a

68001079.name: Apudoma
68001079.note: A general term collectively applied to tumors associated with the APUD CELLS series, irrespective of their specific identification.

68001098.name: Spider Bites
68001098.note: The effects, both local and systemic, caused by the bites of SPIDERS.

68001100.name: Arachnoiditis
68001100.note: Acute or chronic inflammation of the arachnoid membrane of the meninges most often involving the spinal cord or base of the brain. This term generally refers to a persistent inflammatory process characterized by thickening of the ARACHNOID membrane and dural adhesions. Associated conditions include

68001102.name: Arbovirus Infections
68001102.note: Infections caused by arthropod-borne viruses, general or unspecified.

68001112.name: Arcus Senilis
68001112.note: A corneal disease in which there is a deposition of phospholipid and cholesterol in the corneal stroma and anterior sclera.

68001117.name: Arenaviridae Infections
68001117.note: Virus diseases caused by the ARENAVIRIDAE.

68001129.name: Argyria
68001129.note: A permanent ashen-gray discoloration of the skin, conjunctiva, and internal organs resulting from long-continued use of silver salts. (Dorland, 27th ed)

68001134.name: Arm Injuries
68001134.note: General or unspecified injuries involving the UPPER ARM and the FOREARM.

68001139.name: Arnold-Chiari Malformation
68001139.note: A group of congenital malformations involving the brainstem, cerebellum, upper spinal cord, and surrounding bony structures. Type II is the most common, and features compression of the medulla and cerebellar tonsils into the upper cervical spinal canal and an associated MENINGOMYELOCELE. Type I feat

68001145.name: Arrhythmias, Cardiac
68001145.note: Any disturbances of the normal rhythmic beating of the heart or MYOCARDIAL CONTRACTION. Cardiac arrhythmias can be classified by the abnormalities in HEART RATE, disorders of electrical impulse generation, or impulse conduction.

68001146.name: Arrhythmia, Sinus
68001146.note: Irregular HEART RATE caused by abnormal function of the SINOATRIAL NODE. It is characterized by a greater than 10% change between the maximum and the minimum sinus cycle length or 120 milliseconds.

68001157.name: Arterial Occlusive Diseases
68001157.note: Pathological processes which result in the partial or complete obstruction of ARTERIES. They are characterized by greatly reduced or absence of blood flow through these vessels. They are also known as arterial insufficiency.

68001159.name: Arterio-Arterial Fistula
68001159.note: Abnormal communication between two ARTERIES that may result from injury or occur as a congenital abnormality.

68001161.name: Arteriosclerosis
68001161.note: Thickening and loss of elasticity of the walls of ARTERIES of all sizes. There are many forms classified by the types of lesions and arteries involved, such as ATHEROSCLEROSIS with fatty lesions in the ARTERIAL INTIMA of medium and large muscular arteries.

68001162.name: Arteriosclerosis Obliterans
68001162.note: Common occlusive arterial disease which is caused by ATHEROSCLEROSIS. It is characterized by lesions in the innermost layer (ARTERIAL INTIMA) of arteries including the AORTA and its branches to the extremities. Risk factors include smoking, HYPERLIPIDEMIA, and HYPERTENSION.

68001164.name: Arteriovenous Fistula
68001164.note: An abnormal direct communication between an artery and a vein without passing through the CAPILLARIES. An A-V fistula usually leads to the formation of a dilated sac-like connection, arteriovenous aneurysm. The locations and size of the shunts determine the degree of effects on the cardiovascular fu

68001165.name: Arteriovenous Malformations
68001165.note: Abnormal formation of blood vessels that shunt arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the CAPILLARIES. They usually are crooked, dilated, and with thick vessel walls. A common type is the congenital arteriovenous fistula. The lack of blood flow and oxygen in the capillaries can l

68001168.name: Arthritis
68001168.note: Acute or chronic inflammation of JOINTS.

68001169.name: Arthritis, Experimental
68001169.note: ARTHRITIS that is induced in experimental animals. Immunological methods and infectious agents can be used to develop experimental arthritis models. These methods include injections of stimulators of the immune response, such as an adjuvant (ADJUVANTS, IMMUNOLOGIC) or COLLAGEN.

68001170.name: Arthritis, Infectious
68001170.note: Arthritis caused by BACTERIA; RICKETTSIA; MYCOPLASMA; VIRUSES; FUNGI; or PARASITES.

68001171.name: Arthritis, Juvenile
68001171.note: Arthritis in children, with onset before 16 years of age. The terms juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (JRA) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) refer to classification systems for chronic arthritis in children. Only one subtype of juvenile arthritis (polyarticular-onset, rheumatoid factor-positive)

68001172.name: Arthritis, Rheumatoid
68001172.note: A chronic systemic disease, primarily of the joints, marked by inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures, widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, and by atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures. Etiology is unknown, but autoimm

68001176.name: Arthrogryposis
68001176.note: Persistent flexure or contracture of a joint.

68001177.name: Arthropathy, Neurogenic
68001177.note: Chronic progressive degeneration of the stress-bearing portion of a joint, with bizarre hypertrophic changes at the periphery. It is probably a complication of a variety of neurologic disorders, particularly TABES DORSALIS, involving loss of sensation, which leads to relaxation of supporting structu

68001183.name: Arthus Reaction
68001183.note: A dermal inflammatory reaction produced under conditions of antibody excess, when a second injection of antigen produces intravascular antigen-antibody complexes which bind complement, causing cell clumping, endothelial damage, and vascular necrosis.

68001184.name: Articulation Disorders
68001184.note: Disorders of the quality of speech characterized by the substitution, omission, distortion, and addition of phonemes.

68001195.name: Asbestosis
syn: Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonitis - from Asbestos Exposure
68001195.note: A form of pneumoconiosis caused by inhalation of asbestos fibers which elicit potent inflammatory responses in the parenchyma of the lung. The disease is characterized by interstitial fibrosis of the lung, varying from scattered sites to extensive scarring of the alveolar interstitium.

68001196.name: Ascariasis
68001196.note: Infection by nematodes of the genus ASCARIS. Ingestion of infective eggs causes diarrhea and pneumonitis. Its distribution is more prevalent in areas of poor sanitation and where human feces are used for fertilizer.

68001198.name: Ascaridiasis
68001198.note: Infection with nematodes of the genus ASCARIDIA. This condition usually occurs in fowl, often manifesting diarrhea.

68001201.name: Ascites
68001201.note: Accumulation or retention of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity.

68001206.name: Ascorbic Acid Deficiency
68001206.note: A condition due to a dietary deficiency of ascorbic acid (vitamin C), characterized by malaise, lethargy, and weakness. As the disease progresses, joints, muscles, and subcutaneous tissues may become the sites of hemorrhage. Ascorbic acid deficiency frequently develops into SCURVY in young children

68001228.name: Aspergillosis
68001228.note: Infections with fungi of the genus ASPERGILLUS.

68001229.name: Aspergillosis, Allergic Bronchopulmonary
68001229.note: Hypersensitivity reaction (ALLERGIC REACTION) to fungus ASPERGILLUS in an individual with long-standing BRONCHIAL ASTHMA. It is characterized by pulmonary infiltrates, EOSINOPHILIA, elevated serum IMMUNOGLOBULIN E, and skin reactivity to Aspergillus antigen.

68001237.name: Asphyxia
68001237.note: A pathological condition caused by lack of oxygen, manifested in impending or actual cessation of life.

68001238.name: Asphyxia Neonatorum
68001238.note: Respiratory failure in the newborn. (Dorland, 27th ed)

68001247.name: Asthenia
68001247.note: Clinical sign or symptom manifested as debility, or lack or loss of strength and energy.

68001248.name: Asthenopia
68001248.note: Term generally used to describe complaints related to refractive error, ocular muscle imbalance, including pain or aching around the eyes, burning and itchiness of the eyelids, ocular fatigue, and headaches.

68001249.name: Asthma
68001249.note: A form of bronchial disorder with three distinct components: airway hyper-responsiveness (RESPIRATORY HYPERSENSITIVITY), airway INFLAMMATION, and intermittent AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION. It is characterized by spasmodic contraction of airway smooth muscle, WHEEZING, and dyspnea (DYSPNEA, PAROXYSMAL).

68001250.name: Asthma, Exercise-Induced
68001250.note: Asthma attacks following a period of exercise. Usually the induced attack is short-lived and regresses spontaneously. The magnitude of postexertional airway obstruction is strongly influenced by the environment in which exercise is performed (i.e. inhalation of cold air during physical exertion mark

68001251.name: Astigmatism
68001251.note: Unequal or irregular curvature of the CORNEA (Corneal astigmatism) and/or the EYE LENS (Lenticular astigmatism) resulting in REFRACTIVE ERROR.

68001254.name: Astrocytoma
68001254.note: Neoplasms of the brain and spinal cord derived from glial cells which vary from histologically benign forms to highly anaplastic and malignant tumors. Fibrillary astrocytomas are the most common type and may be classified in order of increasing malignancy (grades I through IV). In the first two deca

68001259.name: Ataxia
68001259.note: Impairment of the ability to perform smoothly coordinated voluntary movements. This condition may affect the limbs, trunk, eyes, pharynx, larynx, and other structures. Ataxia may result from impaired sensory or motor function. Sensory ataxia may result from posterior column injury or PERIPHERAL NERV

68001260.name: Ataxia Telangiectasia
68001260.note: An autosomal recessive inherited disorder characterized by choreoathetosis beginning in childhood, progressive CEREBELLAR ATAXIA; TELANGIECTASIS of CONJUNCTIVA and SKIN; DYSARTHRIA; B- and T-cell immunodeficiency, and RADIOSENSITIVITY to IONIZING RADIATION. Affected individuals are prone to recurren

68001261.name: Pulmonary Atelectasis
68001261.note: Absence of air in the entire or part of a lung, such as an incompletely inflated neonate lung or a collapsed adult lung. Pulmonary atelectasis can be caused by airway obstruction, lung compression, fibrotic contraction, or other factors.

68001264.name: Athetosis
68001264.note: A dyskinesia characterized by an inability to maintain the fingers, toes, tongue, or other body parts in a stable position, resulting in continuous slow, sinusoidal, and flowing involuntary movements. This condition is frequently accompanied by CHOREA, where it is referred to as choreoathetosis. Ath

68001265.name: Athletic Injuries
68001265.note: Injuries incurred during participation in competitive or non-competitive sports.

68001281.name: Atrial Fibrillation
68001281.note: Abnormal cardiac rhythm that is characterized by rapid, uncoordinated firing of electrical impulses in the upper chambers of the heart (HEART ATRIA). In such case, blood cannot be effectively pumped into the lower chambers of the heart (HEART VENTRICLES). It is caused by abnormal impulse generation.

68001282.name: Atrial Flutter
68001282.note: Rapid, irregular atrial contractions caused by a block of electrical impulse conduction in the right atrium and a reentrant wave front traveling up the inter-atrial septum and down the right atrial free wall or vice versa. Unlike ATRIAL FIBRILLATION which is caused by abnormal impulse generation, ty

68001284.name: Atrophy
68001284.note: Decrease in the size of a cell, tissue, organ, or multiple organs, associated with a variety of pathological conditions such as abnormal cellular changes, ischemia, malnutrition, or hormonal changes.

68001304.name: Auditory Diseases, Central
68001304.note: Disorders of hearing or auditory perception due to pathological processes of the AUDITORY PATHWAYS in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. These include CENTRAL HEARING LOSS and AUDITORY PERCEPTUAL DISORDERS.

68001308.name: Auditory Perceptual Disorders
68001308.note: Acquired or developmental cognitive disorders of AUDITORY PERCEPTION characterized by a reduced ability to perceive information contained in auditory stimuli despite intact auditory pathways. Affected individuals have difficulty with speech perception, sound localization, and comprehending the meani

68001327.name: Autoimmune Diseases
68001327.note: Disorders that are characterized by the production of antibodies that react with host tissues or immune effector cells that are autoreactive to endogenous peptides.

68001329.name: Autolysis
68001329.note: The spontaneous disintegration of tissues or cells by the action of their own autogenous enzymes.

68001342.name: Autonomic Nervous System Diseases
syn: Disorders of the Autonomic Nervous System
68001342.note: Diseases of the AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM, including sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric nervous systems.

68001353.name: Avian Leukosis
68001353.note: A group of transmissible viral diseases of chickens and turkeys. Liver tumors are found in most forms, but tumors can be found elsewhere.

68001357.name: Sarcoma, Avian
68001357.note: Connective tissue tumors, affecting primarily fowl, that are usually caused by avian sarcoma viruses.

68001361.name: Avitaminosis
68001361.note: A condition due to a deficiency of one or more essential vitamins. (Dorland, 27th ed)

68001404.name: Babesiosis
68001404.note: A group of tick-borne diseases of mammals including ZOONOSES in humans. They are caused by protozoa of the genus BABESIA, which parasitize erythrocytes, producing hemolysis. In the U.S., the organism's natural host is mice and transmission is by the deer tick IXODES SCAPULARIS.

68001416.name: Back Pain
68001416.note: Acute or chronic pain located in the posterior regions of the THORAX; LUMBOSACRAL REGION; or the adjacent regions.

68001423.name: Bacterial Infections and Mycoses
68001423.note: Infections caused by bacteria and fungi, general, specified, or unspecified.

68001424.name: Bacterial Infections
68001424.note: Infections by bacteria, general or unspecified.

68001437.name: Bacteriuria
68001437.note: The presence of bacteria in the urine which is normally bacteria-free. These bacteria are from the URINARY TRACT and are not contaminants of the surrounding tissues. Bacteriuria can be symptomatic or asymptomatic. Significant bacteriuria is an indicator of urinary tract infection.

68001442.name: Bacteroides Infections
68001442.note: Infections with bacteria of the genus BACTEROIDES.

68001446.name: Balanitis
68001446.note: Inflammation of the head of the PENIS, glans penis.

68001447.name: Balantidiasis
68001447.note: Infection by parasites of the genus BALANTIDIUM. The presence of Balantidium in the LARGE INTESTINE leads to DIARRHEA; DYSENTERY; and occasionally ULCER.

68001449.name: Balkan Nephropathy
68001449.note: A form of chronic interstitial nephritis that is endemic to limited areas of BULGARIA, the former YUGOSLAVIA, and ROMANIA. It is characterized by a progressive shrinking of the KIDNEYS that is often associated with uroepithelial tumors.

68001469.name: Barotrauma
68001469.note: Injury following pressure changes; includes injury to the eustachian tube, ear drum, lung and stomach.

68001471.name: Barrett Esophagus
68001471.note: A condition with damage to the lining of the lower ESOPHAGUS resulting from chronic acid reflux (ESOPHAGITIS, REFLUX). Through the process of metaplasia, the squamous cells are replaced by a columnar epithelium with cells resembling those of the INTESTINE or the salmon-pink mucosa of the STOMACH. Ba

68001474.name: Bartonella Infections
68001474.note: Infections by the genus BARTONELLA. Bartonella bacilliformis can cause acute febrile anemia, designated Oroya fever, and a benign skin eruption, called verruga peruana. BARTONELLA QUINTANA causes TRENCH FEVER, while BARTONELLA HENSELAE is the etiologic agent of bacillary angiomatosis (ANGIOMATOSIS,

68001476.name: Bartonellaceae Infections
68001476.note: Infections with bacteria of the family BARTONELLACEAE.

68001477.name: Bartter Syndrome
syn: Aldosteronism with Hyperplasia of the Adrenal Cortex
68001477.note: A group of disorders caused by defective salt reabsorption in the ascending LOOP OF HENLE. It is characterized by severe salt-wasting, HYPOKALEMIA; HYPERCALCIURIA; metabolic ALKALOSIS, and hyper-reninemic HYPERALDOSTERONISM without HYPERTENSION. There are several subtypes including ones due to mutat

68001478.name: Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome
syn: Multiple Basal Cell Nevi, Odontogenic Keratocysts, and Skeletal Anomalies
68001478.note: Hereditary disorder consisting of multiple basal cell carcinomas, odontogenic keratocysts, and multiple skeletal defects, e.g., frontal and temporoparietal bossing, bifurcated and splayed ribs, kyphoscoliosis, fusion of vertebrae, and cervicothoracic spina bifida. Genetic transmission is autosomal d

68001480.name: Basal Ganglia Diseases
68001480.note: Diseases of the BASAL GANGLIA including the PUTAMEN; GLOBUS PALLIDUS; claustrum; AMYGDALA; and CAUDATE NUCLEUS. DYSKINESIAS (most notably involuntary movements and alterations of the rate of movement) represent the primary clinical manifestations of these disorders. Common etiologies include CEREBRO

68001506.name: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome
68001506.note: A syndrome of multiple defects characterized primarily by umbilical hernia (HERNIA, UMBILICAL); MACROGLOSSIA; and GIGANTISM; and secondarily by visceromegaly; HYPOGLYCEMIA; and ear abnormalities.

68001528.name: Behcet Syndrome
68001528.note: Rare chronic inflammatory disease involving the small blood vessels. It is of unknown etiology and characterized by mucocutaneous ulceration in the mouth and genital region and uveitis with hypopyon. The neuro-ocular form may cause blindness and death. SYNOVITIS; THROMBOPHLEBITIS; gastrointestinal u

68001602.name: Beriberi
68001602.note: A disease caused by a deficiency of thiamine (vitamin B1) and characterized by polyneuritis, cardiac pathology, and edema. The epidemic form is found primarily in areas in which white (polished) rice is the staple food, as in Japan, China, the Philippines, India, and other countries of southeast Asi

68001606.name: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome
68001606.note: A familial coagulation disorder characterized by a prolonged bleeding time, unusually large platelets, and impaired prothrombin consumption.

68001607.name: Berylliosis
68001607.note: A form of pneumoconiosis caused by inhaled rare metal BERYLLIUM or its soluble salts which are used in a wide variety of industry including alloys, ceramics, radiographic equipment, and vacuum tubes. Berylliosis is characterized by an acute inflammatory reaction in the upper airway leading to BRONCH

68001630.name: Bezoars
68001630.note: Concretions of swallowed hair, fruit or vegetable fibers, or similar substances found in the alimentary canal.

68001649.name: Bile Duct Diseases
68001649.note: Diseases in any part of the ductal system of the BILIARY TRACT from the smallest BILE CANALICULI to the largest COMMON BILE DUCT.

68001650.name: Bile Duct Neoplasms
68001650.note: Tumors or cancer of the BILE DUCTS.

68001651.name: Cholestasis, Extrahepatic
68001651.note: Impairment of bile flow in the large BILE DUCTS by mechanical obstruction or stricture due to benign or malignant processes.

68001655.name: Bile Reflux
68001655.note: Retrograde bile flow. Reflux of bile can be from the duodenum to the stomach (DUODENOGASTRIC REFLUX); to the esophagus (GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX); or to the PANCREAS.
