68020786.name: Hemangioma, Cavernous, Central Nervous System
68020786.note: A vascular anomaly composed of a collection of large, thin walled tortuous VEINS that can occur in any part of the central nervous system but lack intervening nervous tissue. Familial occurrence is common and has been associated with a number of genes mapped to 7q, 7p and 3q. Clinical features inclu

68020787.name: Central Nervous System Venous Angioma
68020787.note: A vascular anomaly characterized by a radial or wedge-shaped arrangement of dilated VEINS draining into a larger vein in the brain, spinal cord, or the meninges. Veins in a venous angioma are surrounded by normal nervous tissue, unlike a CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM CAVERNOUS HEMANGIOMA that lacks interve

68020788.name: Bardet-Biedl Syndrome
68020788.note: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA; POLYDACTYLY; OBESITY; MENTAL RETARDATION; hypogenitalism; renal dysplasia; and short stature. This syndrome has been distinguished as a separate entity from LAURENCE-MOON SYNDROME. (From J Med Genet 1997 Feb;34(2):92-8)

68020790.name: Diabetes Insipidus, Neurogenic
syn: Diabetes Insipidus Secondary To Vasopressin Deficiency
68020790.note: A genetic or acquired polyuric disorder caused by a deficiency of VASOPRESSINS secreted by the NEUROHYPOPHYSIS. Clinical signs include the excretion of large volumes of dilute URINE; HYPERNATREMIA; THIRST; and polydipsia. Etiologies include HEAD TRAUMA; surgeries and diseases involving the HYPOTHALA

68020792.name: Salivary Calculi
68020792.note: The presence of calculi in a salivary duct or gland.

68020795.name: Photophobia
68020795.note: Abnormal sensitivity to light. This may occur as a manifestation of EYE DISEASES; MIGRAINE; SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE; MENINGITIS; and other disorders. Photophobia may also occur in association with DEPRESSION and other MENTAL DISORDERS.

68020802.name: Epidural Abscess
68020802.note: Circumscribed collections of suppurative material occurring in the spinal or intracranial EPIDURAL SPACE. The majority of epidural abscesses occur in the spinal canal and are associated with OSTEOMYELITIS of a vertebral body; ANALGESIA, EPIDURAL; and other conditions. Clinical manifestations include

68020803.name: Encephalitis, Herpes Simplex
68020803.note: An acute (or rarely chronic) inflammatory process of the brain caused by SIMPLEXVIRUS infections which may be fatal. The majority of infections are caused by human herpesvirus 1 (HERPESVIRUS 1, HUMAN) and less often by human herpesvirus 2 (HERPESVIRUS 2, HUMAN). Clinical manifestations include FEVER

68020804.name: Encephalitis, Varicella Zoster
68020804.note: Inflammation of brain tissue caused by infection with the varicella-zoster virus (HERPESVIRUS 3, HUMAN). This condition is associated with immunocompromised states, including the ACQUIRED IMMUNODEFICIENCY SYNDROME. Pathologically, the virus tends to induce a vasculopathy and infect oligodendrocytes

68020805.name: Central Nervous System Viral Diseases
68020805.note: Viral infections of the brain, spinal cord, meninges, or perimeningeal spaces.

68020806.name: Central Nervous System Bacterial Infections
68020806.note: Bacterial infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges, including infections involving the perimeningeal spaces.

68020807.name: Central Nervous System Parasitic Infections
68020807.note: Infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges caused by parasites.

68020808.name: Central Nervous System Protozoal Infections
68020808.note: Infections of the brain, spinal cord, or meninges by single celled organisms of the former subkingdom known as protozoa. The central nervous system may be the primary or secondary site of protozoal infection. These diseases may occur as OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS or arise in immunocompetent hosts.

68020809.name: Central Nervous System Helminthiasis
68020809.note: Infections of the BRAIN; SPINAL CORD; or MENINGES caused by HELMINTHS (parasitic worms).

68020814.name: Meningitis, Escherichia coli
68020814.note: A form of gram-negative meningitis that tends to occur in neonates, in association with anatomical abnormalities (which feature communication between the meninges and cutaneous structures) or as OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS in association with IMMUNOLOGIC DEFICIENCY SYNDROMES. In premature neonates the

68020818.name: Neuroschistosomiasis
68020818.note: SCHISTOSOMIASIS of the brain, spinal cord, or meninges caused by infections with trematodes of the genus SCHISTOSOMA (primarily SCHISTOSOMA JAPONICUM; SCHISTOSOMA MANSONI; and SCHISTOSOMA HAEMATOBIUM in humans). S. japonicum infections of the nervous system may cause an acute meningoencephalitis or

68020819.name: Perimeningeal Infections
68020819.note: Infectious processes, including abscesses, effusions, and empyemas which occur in the epidural or subdural spaces surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

68020820.name: Dyskinesias
68020820.note: Abnormal involuntary movements which primarily affect the extremities, trunk, or jaw that occur as a manifestation of an underlying disease process. Conditions which feature recurrent or persistent episodes of dyskinesia as a primary manifestation of disease may be referred to as dyskinesia syndrome

68020821.name: Dystonic Disorders
68020821.note: Acquired and inherited conditions that feature DYSTONIA as a primary manifestation of disease. These disorders are generally divided into generalized dystonias (e.g., dystonia musculorum deformans) and focal dystonias (e.g., writer's cramp). They are also classified by patterns of inheritance and by

68020828.name: Pseudobulbar Palsy
68020828.note: A syndrome characterized by DYSARTHRIA, dysphagia, dysphonia, impairment of voluntary movements of tongue and facial muscles, and emotional lability. This condition is caused by diseases that affect the motor fibers that travel from the cerebral cortex to the lower BRAIN STEM (i.e., corticobulbar tr

68020833.name: Diffuse Axonal Injury
68020833.note: A relatively common sequela of blunt head injury, characterized by a global disruption of axons throughout the brain. Associated clinical features may include NEUROBEHAVIORAL MANIFESTATIONS; PERSISTENT VEGETATIVE STATE; DEMENTIA; and other disorders.

68020852.name: Lyme Neuroborreliosis
68020852.note: Nervous system infections caused by tick-borne spirochetes of the BORRELIA BURGDORFERI GROUP. The disease may affect elements of the central or peripheral nervous system in isolation or in combination. Common clinical manifestations include a lymphocytic meningitis, cranial neuropathy (most often a

68020857.name: Hallux Limitus
68020857.note: A bony proliferation and articular degeneration of the first METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT that is characterized by pain and a progressive decrease in the dorsiflexion range of motion.

68020859.name: Hallux Rigidus
68020859.note: A condition caused by degenerative arthritis (see OSTEOARTHRITIS) of the METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT of the great toe and characterized by pain and limited dorsiflexion, but relatively unrestricted plantar flexion.

68020863.name: Central Nervous System Cysts
68020863.note: Congenital or acquired cysts of the brain, spinal cord, or meninges which may remain stable in size or undergo progressive enlargement.

68020879.name: Neuromuscular Manifestations
68020879.note: Signs and symptoms associated with diseases of the muscle, neuromuscular junction, or peripheral nerves.

68020886.name: Somatosensory Disorders
68020886.note: Disorders of sensory information received from superficial and deep regions of the body. The somatosensory system conveys neural impulses which pertain to proprioception, tactile sensation, thermal sensation, pressure sensation, and pain. PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM DISEASES; SPINAL CORD DISEASES; and

68020896.name: Hypovolemia
68020896.note: An abnormally low volume of blood circulating through the body. It may result in hypovolemic shock (see SHOCK).

68020914.name: Myopathies, Structural, Congenital
68020914.note: A heterogeneous group of diseases characterized by the early onset of hypotonia, developmental delay of motor skills, non-progressive weakness. Each of these disorders is associated with a specific histologic muscle fiber abnormality.

68020915.name: Korsakoff Syndrome
68020915.note: An acquired cognitive disorder characterized by inattentiveness and the inability to form short term memories. This disorder is frequently associated with chronic ALCOHOLISM; but it may also result from dietary deficiencies; CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA; NEOPLASMS; CEREBROVASCULAR DISORDERS; ENCEPHALITIS;

68020918.name: Complex Regional Pain Syndromes
68020918.note: Conditions characterized by pain involving an extremity or other body region, HYPERESTHESIA, and localized autonomic dysfunction following injury to soft tissue or nerve. The pain is usually associated with ERYTHEMA; SKIN TEMPERATURE changes, abnormal sudomotor activity (i.e., changes in sweating du

68020919.name: Sleep Disorders, Intrinsic
68020919.note: Dyssomnias (i.e., insomnias or hypersomnias) associated with dysfunction of internal sleep mechanisms or secondary to a sleep-related medical disorder (e.g., sleep apnea, post-traumatic sleep disorders, etc.). (From Thorpy, Sleep Disorders Medicine, 1994, p187)

68020920.name: Dyssomnias
68020920.note: A broad category of sleep disorders characterized by either hypersomnolence or insomnia. The three major subcategories include intrinsic (i.e., arising from within the body) (SLEEP DISORDERS, INTRINSIC), extrinsic (secondary to environmental conditions or various pathologic conditions), and disturba

68020921.name: Sleep Arousal Disorders
68020921.note: Sleep disorders characterized by impaired arousal from the deeper stages of sleep (generally stage III or IV sleep).

68020922.name: Sleep-Wake Transition Disorders
68020922.note: Parasomnias characterized by behavioral abnormalities that occur during the transition between wakefulness and sleep (or between sleep and wakefulness).

68020923.name: REM Sleep Parasomnias
68020923.note: Abnormal behavioral or physiologic events that are associated with REM sleep, including REM SLEEP BEHAVIOR DISORDER.

68020924.name: Urological Manifestations
68020924.note: Clinical disturbances of the urinary system.

68020925.name: Hypoxia-Ischemia, Brain
68020925.note: A disorder characterized by a reduction of oxygen in the blood combined with reduced blood flow (ISCHEMIA) to the brain from a localized obstruction of a cerebral artery or from systemic hypoperfusion. Prolonged hypoxia-ischemia is associated with ISCHEMIC ATTACK, TRANSIENT; BRAIN INFARCTION; BRAIN

68020936.name: Epilepsy, Benign Neonatal
68020936.note: A condition marked by recurrent seizures that occur during the first 4-6 weeks of life despite an otherwise benign neonatal course. Autosomal dominant familial and sporadic forms have been identified. Seizures generally consist of brief episodes of tonic posturing and other movements, apnea, eye dev

68020937.name: Epilepsy, Partial, Sensory
68020937.note: A disorder characterized by recurrent focal onset seizures which have sensory (i.e., olfactory, visual, tactile, gustatory, or auditory) manifestations. Partial seizures that feature alterations of consciousness are referred to as complex partial seizures (EPILEPSY, COMPLEX PARTIAL).

68020938.name: Epilepsy, Partial, Motor
68020938.note: A disorder characterized by recurrent localized paroxysmal discharges of cerebral neurons that give rise to seizures that have motor manifestations. The majority of partial motor seizures originate in the FRONTAL LOBE (see also EPILEPSY, FRONTAL LOBE). Motor seizures may manifest as tonic or clonic

68020941.name: Myasthenia Gravis, Neonatal
68020941.note: A disorder of neuromuscular transmission that occurs in a minority of newborns born to women with myasthenia gravis. Clinical features are usually present at birth or develop in the first 3 days of life and consist of hypotonia and impaired respiratory, suck, and swallowing abilities. This condition

68020943.name: AIDS Arteritis, Central Nervous System
syn: HIV-Associated Vasculitis of the Central Nervous System
HIV Associated Vasculitis of the Central Nervous System
68020943.note: Inflammation of ARTERIES in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM that occurs in patients with ACQUIRED IMMUNODEFICIENCY SYNDROME or AIDS-RELATED OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS.

68020945.name: Lupus Vasculitis, Central Nervous System
syn: Central Nervous System Systemic Lupus Erythematosis
Systemic Lupus Erythematosis, Central Nervous System
68020945.note: Central nervous system vasculitis that is associated with SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS. Clinical manifestations may include DEMENTIA; SEIZURES; CRANIAL NERVE DISEASES; HEMIPARESIS; BLINDNESS; DYSPHASIA; and other neurological disorders.

68020953.name: Neuroaspergillosis
68020953.note: Infections of the nervous system caused by fungi of the genus ASPERGILLUS, most commonly ASPERGILLUS FUMIGATUS. Aspergillus infections may occur in immunocompetent hosts, but are more prevalent in individuals with IMMUNOLOGIC DEFICIENCY SYNDROMES. The organism may spread to the nervous system from f

68020955.name: Striatonigral Degeneration
68020955.note: A sporadic neurodegenerative disease with onset in middle-age characterized clinically by Parkinsonian features (e.g., MUSCLE RIGIDITY; HYPOKINESIA; stooped posture) and HYPOTENSION. This condition is considered a clinical variant of MULTIPLE SYSTEM ATROPHY. Pathologic features include a prominent l

68020961.name: Lewy Body Disease
68020961.note: A neurodegenerative disease characterized by dementia, mild parkinsonism, and fluctuations in attention and alertness. The neuropsychiatric manifestations tend to precede the onset of bradykinesia, MUSCLE RIGIDITY, and other extrapyramidal signs. DELUSIONS and visual HALLUCINATIONS are relatively fr

68020964.name: Embryo Loss
68020964.note: Early pregnancy loss during the EMBRYO, MAMMALIAN stage of development. In the human, this period comprises the second through eighth week after fertilization.

68020966.name: Muscular Disorders, Atrophic
68020966.note: Disorders characterized by an abnormal reduction in muscle volume due to a decrease in the size or number of muscle fibers. Atrophy may result from diseases intrinsic to muscle tissue (e.g., MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY) or secondary to PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM DISEASES that impair innervation to muscle tiss

68020967.name: Myotonic Disorders
68020967.note: Diseases characterized by MYOTONIA, which may be inherited or acquired. Myotonia may be restricted to certain muscles (e.g., intrinsic hand muscles) or occur as a generalized condition.

68020968.name: Brachial Plexus Neuritis
68020968.note: A syndrome associated with inflammation of the BRACHIAL PLEXUS. Clinical features include severe pain in the shoulder region which may be accompanied by MUSCLE WEAKNESS and loss of sensation in the upper extremity. This condition may be associated with VIRUS DISEASES; IMMUNIZATION; SURGERY; heroin u

68020969.name: Disease Attributes
68020969.note: Clinical characteristics of disease or illness.

68021081.name: Chronobiology Disorders
68021081.note: Disruptions of the rhythmic cycle of bodily functions or activities.

68021181.name: Egg Hypersensitivity
68021181.note: Allergic reaction to eggs that is triggered by the immune system.

68021182.name: Wheat Hypersensitivity
68021182.note: Allergic reaction to wheat that is triggered by the immune system.

68021183.name: Peanut Hypersensitivity
68021183.note: Allergic reaction to peanuts that is triggered by the immune system.

68021184.name: Nut Hypersensitivity
68021184.note: Allergic reaction to tree nuts that is triggered by the immune system.

68021441.name: Carcinoma, Pancreatic Ductal
syn: Duct Cell Carcinoma of the Pancreas
68021441.note: Carcinoma that arises from the PANCREATIC DUCTS. It accounts for the majority of cancers derived from the PANCREAS.

68021501.name: Flank Pain
68021501.note: Pain emanating from below the RIBS and above the ILIUM.

68021782.name: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney
68021782.note: A nongenetic defect due to malformation of the KIDNEY which appears as a bunch of grapes with multiple renal cysts but lacking the normal renal bean shape, and the collection drainage system. This condition can be detected in-utero with ULTRASONOGRAPHY.

68021821.name: Communicable Diseases, Emerging
68021821.note: Infectious diseases that are novel in their outbreak ranges (geographic and host) or transmission mode.

68021865.name: Isosporiasis
68021865.note: Infection with parasitic protozoa of the genus ISOSPORA, producing intestinal disease. It is caused by ingestion of oocysts and can produce tissue cysts.

68021866.name: Cyclosporiasis
68021866.note: Infection with parasitic protozoa of the genus CYCLOSPORA. It is distributed globally and causes a diarrheal illness. Transmission is waterborne.

68021921.name: Aortic Stenosis, Supravalvular
68021921.note: A pathological constriction occurring in the region above the AORTIC VALVE. It is characterized by restricted outflow from the LEFT VENTRICLE into the AORTA.

68021922.name: Discrete Subaortic Stenosis
68021922.note: A type of constriction that is caused by the presence of a fibrous ring (discrete type) below the AORTIC VALVE, anywhere between the aortic valve and the MITRAL VALVE. It is characterized by restricted outflow from the LEFT VENTRICLE into the AORTA.

68022124.name: Hyperammonemia
68022124.note: Elevated level of AMMONIA in the blood. It is a sign of defective CATABOLISM of AMINO ACIDS or ammonia to UREA.

68022861.name: Hermanski-Pudlak Syndrome
68022861.note: Syndrome characterized by the triad of oculocutaneous albinism (ALBINISM, OCULOCUTANEOUS); PLATELET STORAGE POOL DEFICIENCY; and lysosomal accumulation of ceroid lipofuscin.

68023341.name: Chills
68023341.note: The sudden sensation of being cold. It may be accompanied by SHIVERING.

68023521.name: Chlamydophila Infections
68023521.note: Infections with bacteria of the genus CHLAMYDOPHILA.

68023903.name: Coronary Restenosis
68023903.note: Recurrent narrowing or constriction of a coronary artery following surgical procedures performed to alleviate a prior obstruction.

68023921.name: Coronary Stenosis
68023921.note: Narrowing or constriction of a coronary artery.

68023961.name: Gonadal Dysgenesis, 46,XX
68023961.note: The 46,XX gonadal dysgenesis may be sporadic or familial. Familial XX gonadal dysgenesis is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait and its locus was mapped to chromosome 2. Mutation in the gene for the FSH receptor (RECEPTORS, FSH) was detected. Sporadic XX gonadal dysgenesis is heterogeneous a

68023981.name: Sarcoma, Myeloid
68023981.note: An extramedullary tumor of immature MYELOID CELLS or MYELOBLASTS. Granulocytic sarcoma usually occurs with or follows the onset of ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA.

68024182.name: Uniparental Disomy
68024182.note: The presence in a cell of two paired chromosomes from the same parent, with no chromosome of that pair from the other parent. This chromosome composition stems from non-disjunction (NONDISJUNCTION, GENETIC) events during MEIOSIS. The disomy may be composed of both homologous chromosomes from one par

68024343.name: Open Bite
68024343.note: A condition in which certain opposing teeth fail to establish occlusal contact when the jaws are closed.

68024741.name: Cardiomyopathy, Hypertrophic, Familial
68024741.note: An autosomal dominant inherited form of HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY. It results from any of more than 50 mutations involving genes encoding contractile proteins such as VENTRICULAR MYOSINS; cardiac TROPONIN T; ALPHA-TROPOMYOSIN.

68024801.name: Tauopathies
68024801.note: Neurodegenerative disorders involving deposition of abnormal tau protein isoforms (TAU PROTEINS) in neurons and glial cells in the brain. Pathological aggregations of tau proteins are associated with mutation of the tau gene on chromosome 17 in patients with ALZHEIMER DISEASE; DEMENTIA; PARKINSONIAN

68024821.name: Metabolic Syndrome
68024821.note: A cluster of symptoms that are risk factors for CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES and TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS. The major components of metabolic syndrome include ABDOMINAL OBESITY; atherogenic DYSLIPIDEMIA; HYPERTENSION; HYPERGLYCEMIA; INSULIN RESISTANCE; a proinflammatory state; and a prothrombotic (THROMBO

68025063.name: Chromosome Disorders
68025063.note: Clinical conditions caused by an abnormal chromosome constitution in which there is extra or missing chromosome material (either a whole chromosome or a chromosome segment). (from Thompson et al., Genetics in Medicine, 5th ed, p429)

68025064.name: Sex Chromosome Disorders
68025064.note: Clinical conditions caused by an abnormal sex chromosome constitution (SEX CHROMOSOME ABERRATIONS), in which there is extra or missing sex chromosome material (either a whole chromosome or a chromosome segment).

68025241.name: Spondylarthritis
68025241.note: Inflammation of the joints of the SPINE, the intervertebral articulations.

68025242.name: Spondylarthropathies
68025242.note: Heterogeneous group of arthritic diseases sharing clinical and radiologic features. They are associated with the HLA-B27 ANTIGEN and some with a triggering infection. Most involve the axial joints in the SPINE, particularly the SACROILIAC JOINT, but can also involve asymmetric peripheral joints. Sub

68025861.name: Blood Coagulation Disorders, Inherited
68025861.note: Hemorrhagic and thrombotic disorders that occur as a consequence of inherited abnormalities in blood coagulation.

68025962.name: Septo-Optic Dysplasia
syn: Septo-Optic Dysplasia with Growth Hormone Deficiency
Septo Optic Dysplasia with Growth Hormone Deficiency
68025962.note: A condition resulting from congenital malformations involving the brain. The syndrome of septo-optic dysplasia combines hypoplasia or agenesis of the SEPTUM PELLUCIDUM; CORPUS CALLOSUM and the OPTIC NERVE. The extent of the abnormalities can vary. Septo-optic dysplasia is often associated with abnor

68025981.name: Hip Injuries
68025981.note: General or unspecified injuries involving the hip.

68026681.name: Vitamin B 6 Deficiency
68026681.note: A nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of VITAMIN B 6 in the diet, characterized by dermatitis, glossitis, cheilosis, and stomatitis. Marked deficiency causes irritability, weakness, depression, dizziness, peripheral neuropathy, and seizures. In infants and children typical manifestations

68027601.name: Polyomavirus Infections
68027601.note: Infections with POLYOMAVIRUS, which are often cultured from the urine of kidney transplant patients. Excretion of BK VIRUS is associated with ureteral strictures and CYSTITIS, and that of JC VIRUS with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY, PROGRESSIVE MULTIFOCAL).

68028226.name: Amyloidosis, Familial
68028226.note: Diseases in which there is a familial pattern of AMYLOIDOSIS.

68028227.name: Amyloid Neuropathies, Familial
68028227.note: Inherited disorders of the peripheral nervous system associated with the deposition of AMYLOID in nerve tissue. The different clinical types based on symptoms correspond to the presence of a variety of mutations in several different proteins including transthyretin (PREALBUMIN); APOLIPOPROTEIN A-I;

68028243.name: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy, Familial
syn: Hereditary Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy, Icelandic Type
Icelandic Type Hereditary Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
68028243.note: A familial disorder marked by AMYLOID deposits in the walls of small and medium sized blood vessels of CEREBRAL CORTEX and MENINGES.

68028361.name: Mitochondrial Diseases
68028361.note: Diseases caused by abnormal function of the MITOCHONDRIA. They may be caused by mutations, acquired or inherited, in mitochondrial DNA or in nuclear genes that code for mitochondrial components. They may also be the result of acquired mitochondria dysfunction due to adverse effects of drugs, infecti

68028921.name: Biotinidase Deficiency
syn: Late Onset Biotin Responsive Multiple Carboxylase Deficiency
68028921.note: The late onset form of MULTIPLE CARBOXYLASE DEFICIENCY (deficiency of the activities of biotin-dependent enzymes propionyl-CoA carboxylase, methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase, and PYRUVATE CARBOXYLASE) due to a defect or deficiency in biotinidase which is essential for recycling BIOTIN.

68028922.name: Holocarboxylase Synthetase Deficiency
syn: Early Onset Biotin Responsive Multiple Carboxylase Deficiency
68028922.note: The neonatal form of MULTIPLE CARBOXYLASE DEFICIENCY that is caused by a defect or deficiency in holocarboxylase synthetase. HLCS is the enzyme that covalently links biotin to the biotin dependent carboxylases (propionyl-CoA-carboxylase, pyruvate carboxylase, and beta-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase)

68029021.name: Peste-des-Petits-Ruminants
68029021.note: A highly fatal contagious disease of goats and sheep caused by PESTE-DES-PETITS-RUMINANTS VIRUS. The disease may be acute or subacute and is characterized by stomatitis, conjunctivitis, diarrhea, and pneumonia.

68029241.name: Optic Atrophy, Autosomal Dominant
syn: Autosomal Dominant Optic Atrophy Kjer Type
68029241.note: Dominant optic atrophy is a hereditary optic neuropathy causing decreased visual acuity, color vision deficits, a centrocecal scotoma, and optic nerve pallor (Hum. Genet. 1998; 102: 79-86). Mutations leading to this condition have been mapped to the OPA1 gene at chromosome 3q28-q29. OPA1 codes for a

68029242.name: Optic Atrophy, Hereditary, Leber
68029242.note: A maternally linked genetic disorder that presents in mid-life as acute or subacute central vision loss leading to central scotoma and blindness. The disease has been associated with missense mutations in the mtDNA, in genes for Complex I, III, and IV polypeptides, that can act autonomously or in as

68029424.name: Pulmonary Disease, Chronic Obstructive
68029424.note: A disease of chronic diffuse irreversible airflow obstruction. Subcategories of COPD include CHRONIC BRONCHITIS and PULMONARY EMPHYSEMA.

68029461.name: Sialic Acid Storage Disease
syn: Sialic Acid Storage Disease, Infantile Form
Sialic Acid Storage Disease, Finnish Type
68029461.note: Autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorders caused by lysosomal membrane transport defects that result in accumulation of free sialic acid (N-ACETYLNEURAMINIC ACID) within the lysosomes. The two main clinical phenotypes, which are allelic variants of the SLC17A5 gene, are ISSD, a severe infantil

68029481.name: Bronchitis, Chronic
68029481.note: A subcategory of CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE. The disease is characterized by hypersecretion of mucus accompanied by a chronic (more than 3 months in 2 consecutive years) productive cough. Infectious agents are a major cause of chronic bronchitis.

68029502.name: Anemia, Hypoplastic, Congenital
68029502.note: An inborn condition characterized by deficiencies of red cell precursors that sometimes also includes LEUKOPENIA and THROMBOCYTOPENIA.

68029503.name: Anemia, Diamond-Blackfan
syn: Anemia, Congenital Hypoplastic, Of Blackfan And Diamond
68029503.note: A rare congenital hypoplastic anemia that usually presents early in infancy. The disease is characterized by a moderate to severe macrocytic anemia, occasional neutropenia or thrombocytosis, a normocellular bone marrow with erythroid hypoplasia, and an increased risk of developing leukemia. (Curr Op

68029593.name: Jervell-Lange Nielsen Syndrome
syn: Deafness, Congenital, and Functional Heart Disease
Prolonged QT Interval in EKG and Sudden Death
Cardioauditory Syndrome of Jervell and Lange-Nielsen
Cardioauditory Syndrome of Jervell and Lange Nielsen
68029593.note: A form of long QT syndrome that is associated with congenital deafness. It is characterized by abnormal cardioelectrophysiology involving the VOLTAGE-GATED POTASSIUM CHANNEL. It results from mutation of KCNQ1 gene (Subtype 1 or JLN1) or the KCNE1 gene (Subtype 2 or JLN2).

68029597.name: Romano-Ward Syndrome
syn: Ventricular Fibrillation with Prolonged QT Interval
68029597.note: A form of long QT syndrome that is without congenital deafness. It is caused by mutation of the KCNQ1 gene which encodes a protein in the VOLTAGE-GATED POTASSIUM CHANNEL.

68030243.name: Hemorrhagic Syndrome, Bovine
68030243.note: Clinically severe acute disease of cattle caused by noncytopathic forms of Bovine viral diarrhea virus 2 (DIARRHEA VIRUS 2, BOVINE VIRAL). Outbreaks are characterized by high morbidity and high mortality.

68030321.name: Denys-Drash Syndrome
syn: Nephropathy, Wilms Tumor, and Genital Anomalies
Pseudohermaphroditism, Nephron Disorder and Wilms' Tumor
68030321.note: A disorder of sex development characterized by UROGENITAL ABNORMALITIES; GONADAL DYSGENESIS; and WILMS TUMOR. It is caused by a mutation in the Wilms tumor suppressor gene (GENES, WILMS TUMOR) on chromosome 11.

68030341.name: Nidovirales Infections
68030341.note: Infections with viruses of the order NIDOVIRALES. The concept includes ARTERIVIRUS INFECTIONS and CORONAVIRIDAE INFECTIONS.

68030342.name: Genetic Diseases, Inborn
68030342.note: Diseases that are caused by genetic mutations present during embryo or fetal development, although they may be observed later in life. The mutations may be inherited from a parent's genome or they may be acquired in utero.

68030361.name: Papillomavirus Infections
68030361.note: Neoplasms of the skin and mucous membranes caused by papillomaviruses. They are usually benign but some have a high risk for malignant progression.

68030401.name: Cytochrome-c Oxidase Deficiency
68030401.note: A disease that results from a congenital defect in ELECTRON TRANSPORT COMPLEX IV. Defects in ELECTRON TRANSPORT COMPLEX IV can be caused by mutations in the SURF1, SCO2, COX10, or SCO1 genes. ELECTRON TRANSPORT COMPLEX IV deficiency caused by mutation in SURF1 manifests itself as LEIGH DISEASE; that

68030981.name: Acro-Osteolysis
68030981.note: A condition with congenital and acquired forms causing recurrent ulcers in the fingers and toes. The congenital form exhibits autosomal dominant inheritance; the acquired form is found in workers who handle VINYL CHLORIDE. When acro-osteolysis is accompanied by generalized OSTEOPOROSIS and skull def

68031221.name: Knee Dislocation
68031221.note: Slippage of the FEMUR off the TIBIA.

68031222.name: Patellar Dislocation
68031222.note: Displacement of the PATELLA from the femoral groove.

68031249.name: Erdheim-Chester Disease
68031249.note: A rare form of non-Langerhans-cell histiocytosis (HISTIOCYTOSIS, NON-LANGERHANS-CELL) with onset in middle age. The systemic disease is characterized by infiltration of lipid-laden macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, an inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes in the bone marrow,

68031261.name: Poult Enteritis Mortality Syndrome
68031261.note: An acute, transmissible, infectious disease associated with high MORTALITY and MORBIDITY in young turkeys (poults). It is characterized by DIARRHEA; ANOREXIA; growth depression, and immune dysfunction. The cause is unknown but astroviruses (AVASTROVIRUS) and coronaviruses (CORONAVIRUS, TURKEY) have

68031300.name: Retinal Vasculitis
68031300.note: Inflammation of the retinal vasculature with various causes including infectious disease; LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS, SYSTEMIC; MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS; BEHCET SYNDROME; and CHORIORETINITIS.

68031368.name: Zoster Sine Herpete
68031368.note: HERPES ZOSTER but without eruption of vesicles. Patients exhibit the characteristic pain minus the skin rash, sometimes making diagnosis difficult.

68031845.name: Hajdu-Cheney Syndrome
syn: Acroosteolysis with Osteoporosis and Changes in Skull and Mandible
68031845.note: Rare, autosomal dominant syndrome characterized by ACRO-OSTEOLYSIS, generalized OSTEOPOROSIS, and skull deformations.

68031901.name: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease
68031901.note: A group of diseases arising from pregnancy that are commonly associated with hyperplasia of trophoblasts (TROPHOBLAST) and markedly elevated human CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN. They include HYDATIDIFORM MOLE, invasive mole (HYDATIDIFORM MOLE, INVASIVE), placental-site trophoblastic tumor (TROPHOBLASTIC TU

68031941.name: Hemorrhagic Septicemia, Viral
68031941.note: A systemic infection of various salmonid and a few nonsalmonid fishes caused by Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (see NOVIRHABDOVIRUS),

68031954.name: Choriocarcinoma, Non-gestational
68031954.note: A highly malignant CHORIOCARCINOMA derived from the non-placental origin such as the totipotent cells in the TESTIS, the OVARY, and the PINEAL GLAND. It produces high levels of CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN and can metastasize widely through the bloodstream to the lungs, brain, liver, bone, and other visce

68033461.name: Hyperuricemia
68033461.note: Excessive URIC ACID or urate in blood as defined by its solubility in plasma at 37 degrees C; greater than 0.42mmol per liter (7.0mg/dL) in men or 0.36mmol per liter (6.0mg/dL) in women. This condition is caused by overproduction of uric acid or impaired renal clearance. Hyperuricemia can be acquire

68034062.name: Insomnia, Fatal Familial
68034062.note: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by degeneration of the THALAMUS and progressive insomnia. It is caused by a mutation in the prion protein (PRIONS).

68034081.name: Wasting Disease, Chronic
68034081.note: A transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (prion disease) of DEER and elk characterized by chronic weight loss leading to death. It is thought to spread by direct contact between animals or through environmental contamination with the prion protein (PRIONS).

68034141.name: Hypoalbuminemia
68034141.note: A condition in which albumin level in blood (SERUM ALBUMIN) is below the normal range. Hypoalbuminemia may be due to decreased hepatic albumin synthesis, increased albumin catabolism, altered albumin distribution, or albumin loss through the urine (ALBUMINURIA).

68034161.name: Pelvic Infection
68034161.note: Infection involving the tissues or organs in the PELVIS.

68034321.name: Hyperamylasemia
68034321.note: A condition with abnormally elevated level of AMYLASES in the serum. Hyperamylasemia due to PANCREATITIS or other causes may be differentiated by identifying the amylase isoenzymes.

68034381.name: Hearing Loss
68034381.note: A general term for the complete or partial loss of the ability to hear from one or both ears.

68034701.name: Mastocytosis, Cutaneous
68034701.note: Skin lesions due to abnormal infiltration of MAST CELLS. Cutaneous mastocytosis is confined to the skin without the involvement of other tissues or organs, and is mostly found in children. The three major variants are: URTICARIA PIGMENTOSA; diffuse cutaneous mastocytosis; and SOLITARY MASTOCYTOMA OF

68034721.name: Mastocytosis, Systemic
68034721.note: A group of disorders caused by the abnormal proliferation of MAST CELLS in a variety of extracutaneous tissues including bone marrow, liver, spleen, lymph nodes, and gastrointestinal tract. Systemic mastocytosis is commonly seen in adults. These diseases are categorized on the basis of clinical feat

68034801.name: Mastocytoma
68034801.note: A solid tumor consisting of a dense infiltration of MAST CELLS. It is generally benign.

68035583.name: Rare Diseases
68035583.note: A large group of diseases which are characterized by a low prevalence in the population. They frequently are associated with problems in diagnosis and treatment.

68036821.name: Endometrial Stromal Tumors
68036821.note: Neoplasms of the endometrial stroma that sometimes involve the MYOMETRIUM. These tumors contain cells that may closely or remotely resemble the normal stromal cells. Endometrial stromal neoplasms are divided into three categories: (1) benign stromal nodules; (2) low-grade stromal sarcoma, or endolym

68036841.name: Ciguatera Poisoning
68036841.note: Poisoning caused by ingestion of SEAFOOD containing microgram levels of CIGUATOXINS. The poisoning is characterized by gastrointestinal, neurological and cardiovascular disturbances.

68036981.name: Fasciitis, Plantar
68036981.note: Inflammation of the plantar fascia (APONEUROSIS) on the bottom of the foot causing heel pain. The etiology of plantar fasciitis remains controversial but is likely to involve a biomechanical imbalance. Though often presenting along with HEEL SPUR, they do not appear to be causally related.

68036982.name: Heel Spur
68036982.note: A bony outgrowth on the lower surface of the CALCANEUS. Though often presenting along with plantar fasciitis (FASCIITIS, PLANTAR), they are not considered causally related.

68037061.name: Metatarsalgia
68037061.note: Pain in the region of the METATARSUS. It can include pain in the METATARSAL BONES; METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT; and/or intermetatarsal joints (TARSAL JOINTS).

68037081.name: Posterior Tibial Tendon Dysfunction
68037081.note: A condition characterized by a broad range of progressive disorders ranging from TENOSYNOVITIS to tendon rupture with or without hindfoot collapse to a fixed, rigid, FLATFOOT deformity. Pathologic changes can involve associated tendons, ligaments, joint structures of the ANKLE, hindfoot, and midfoot

68037801.name: Hammer Toe Syndrome
68037801.note: A condition characterized by a series of interrelated digital symptoms and joint changes of the lesser digits and METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINTS of the FOOT. The syndrome can include some or all of the following conditions: hammer toe, claw toe, mallet toe, overlapping fifth toe, curly toe, EXOSTOSIS; H

68038061.name: Lower Extremity Deformities, Congenital
68038061.note: Congenital structural abnormalities of the LOWER EXTREMITY.

68038062.name: Upper Extremity Deformities, Congenital
68038062.note: Congenital structural abnormalities of the UPPER EXTREMITY.

68038223.name: Post-Concussion Syndrome
68038223.note: The organic and psychogenic disturbances observed after closed head injuries (HEAD INJURIES, CLOSED). Post-concussion syndrome includes subjective physical complaints (i.e. headache, dizziness), cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes. These disturbances can be chronic, permanent, or late emerg

68038261.name: Alexander Disease
68038261.note: Rare leukoencephalopathy with infantile-onset accumulation of Rosenthal fibers in the subpial, periventricular, and subependymal zones of the brain. Rosenthal fibers are GLIAL FIBRILLARY ACIDIC PROTEIN aggregates found in ASTROCYTES. Juvenile- and adult-onset types show progressive atrophy of the lo

68038642.name: Shaken Baby Syndrome
68038642.note: Brain injuries resulted from vigorous shaking of an infant or young child held by the chest, shoulders, or extremities causing extreme cranial acceleration. It is characterized by the intracranial and intraocular hemorrhages with no evident external trauma. Serious cases may result in death.

68038901.name: X-Linked Intellectual Disability
68038901.note: A class of genetic disorders resulting in INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY that is associated either with mutations of GENES located on the X CHROMOSOME or aberrations in the structure of the X chromosome (SEX CHROMOSOME ABERRATIONS).

68038921.name: Coffin-Lowry Syndrome
68038921.note: A rare, X-linked INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY syndrome that results from mutations in the RIBOSOMAL PROTEIN S6 KINASE gene. Typical manifestations of the disease include an intelligence quotient of less than 50, facial anomalies, and other malformations.

68039141.name: Muscular Dystrophy, Oculopharyngeal
68039141.note: An autosomal dominant hereditary disease that presents in late in life and is characterized by DYSPHAGIA and progressive ptosis of the eyelids. Mutations in the gene for POLY(A)-BINDING PROTEIN II have been associated with oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy.

68039682.name: HIV-Associated Lipodystrophy Syndrome
68039682.note: Defective metabolism leading to fat maldistribution in patients infected with HIV. The etiology appears to be multifactorial and probably involves some combination of infection-induced alterations in metabolism, direct effects of antiretroviral therapy, and patient-related factors.

68039941.name: Bifidobacteriales Infections
68039941.note: Infections with BACTERIA of the order Bifidobacteriales. This includes infections in the genera BIFIDOBACTERIUM and GARDNERELLA, in the family Bifidobacteriaceae.

68040181.name: Genetic Diseases, X-Linked
68040181.note: Genetic diseases that are linked to gene mutations on the X CHROMOSOME in humans (X CHROMOSOME, HUMAN) or the X CHROMOSOME in other species. Included here are animal models of human X-linked diseases.

68041441.name: Retinoschisis
68041441.note: A vitreoretinal dystrophy characterized by splitting of the neuroretinal layers. It occurs in two forms: degenerative retinoschisis and X chromosome-linked juvenile retinoschisis.

68041761.name: Cholecystolithiasis
68041761.note: Presence or formation of GALLSTONES in the GALLBLADDER.

68041781.name: Jaundice, Obstructive
68041781.note: Jaundice, the condition with yellowish staining of the skin and mucous membranes, that is due to impaired BILE flow in the BILIARY TRACT, such as INTRAHEPATIC CHOLESTASIS, or EXTRAHEPATIC CHOLESTASIS.

68041881.name: Cholecystitis, Acute
68041881.note: Acute inflammation of the GALLBLADDER wall. It is characterized by the presence of ABDOMINAL PAIN; FEVER; and LEUKOCYTOSIS. Gallstone obstruction of the CYSTIC DUCT is present in approximately 90% of the cases.

68041882.name: Emphysematous Cholecystitis
68041882.note: A variant of acute cholecystitis with inflammation of the GALLBLADDER that is characterized by the pockets of gas in the gallbladder wall. It is due to secondary infection caused by gas-forming organisms, and has a high risk of perforation.

68042101.name: Acalculous Cholecystitis
68042101.note: Inflammation of the GALLBLADDER wall in the absence of GALLSTONES.

68042822.name: Genomic Instability
68042822.note: An increased tendency of the GENOME to acquire MUTATIONS when various processes involved in maintaining and replicating the genome are dysfunctional.

68042882.name: Gallstones
68042882.note: Solid crystalline precipitates in the BILIARY TRACT, usually formed in the GALLBLADDER, resulting in the condition of CHOLELITHIASIS. Gallstones, derived from the BILE, consist mainly of calcium, cholesterol, or bilirubin.

68042883.name: Choledocholithiasis
68042883.note: Presence or formation of GALLSTONES in the COMMON BILE DUCT.

68043171.name: Chromosomal Instability
68043171.note: An increased tendency to acquire CHROMOSOME ABERRATIONS when various processes involved in chromosome replication, repair, or segregation are dysfunctional.

68043183.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
68043183.note: A disorder with chronic or recurrent colonic symptoms without a clearcut etiology. This condition is characterized by chronic or recurrent ABDOMINAL PAIN, bloating, MUCUS in FECES, and an erratic disturbance of DEFECATION.

68043202.name: Steroid Metabolism, Inborn Errors
68043202.note: Errors in metabolic processing of STEROIDS resulting from inborn genetic mutations that are inherited or acquired in utero.

68043204.name: Mineralocorticoid Excess Syndrome, Apparent
68043204.note: A hereditary disease characterized by childhood onset HYPERTENSION, hypokalemic alkalosis, and low RENIN and ALDOSTERONE secretion. It results from a defect in the activity of the 11-BETA-HYDROXYSTEROID DEHYDROGENASE TYPE 2 enzyme which results in inadequate conversion of CORTISOL to CORTISONE. The

68043604.name: Glomus Tympanicum Tumor
68043604.note: A rare PARAGANGLIOMA involving the GLOMUS TYMPANICUM, a collection of chemoreceptor tissue adjacent to the TYMPANIC CAVITY. It can cause TINNITUS and conductive hearing loss (HEARING LOSS, CONDUCTIVE).

68043963.name: Diverticulosis, Colonic
68043963.note: A pathological condition characterized by the presence of a number of COLONIC DIVERTICULA in the COLON. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, including colon aging, motor dysfunction, increases in intraluminal pressure, and lack of dietary fibers.

68044148.name: Lymphatic Abnormalities
68044148.note: Congenital or acquired structural abnormalities of the lymphatic system (LYMPHOID TISSUE) including the lymph vessels.

68044225.name: Piscirickettsiaceae Infections
68044225.note: Infections with bacteria of the family PISCIRICKETTSIACEAE, causing septicemic disease of salmonid fish (SALMONIDAE). Piscirickettsia-like bacteria are also associated with disease syndromes in non-salmonid fish.

68044342.name: Malnutrition
68044342.note: An imbalanced nutritional status resulting from insufficient intake of nutrients to meet normal physiological requirement.

68044343.name: Overnutrition
68044343.note: An imbalanced NUTRITIONAL STATUS resulting from excessive intake of nutrients. Generally, overnutrition generates an energy imbalance between food consumption and energy expenditure leading to disorders such as OBESITY.

68044483.name: Intestinal Polyposis
68044483.note: The growth of INTESTINAL POLYPS. Growth processes include neoplastic (ADENOMA and CARCINOMA) and non-neoplastic (hyperplastic, mucosal, inflammatory, and other polyps).

68044504.name: Enterocolitis, Neutropenic
68044504.note: A syndrome characterized by inflammation in the ILEUM, the CECUM, and the ASCENDING COLON. It is observed in cancer patients with CHEMOTHERAPY-induced NEUTROPENIA or in other immunocompromised individuals (IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST).

68044542.name: LEOPARD Syndrome
68044542.note: An autosomal dominant disorder with an acronym of its seven features (LENTIGO; ELECTROCARDIOGRAM abnormalities; ocular HYPERTELORISM; PULMONARY STENOSIS; abnormal genitalia; retardation of growth; and DEAFNESS or SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS). This syndrome is caused by mutations of PTPN11 gene encodi

68044584.name: Carcinoma, Ductal
68044584.note: Malignant neoplasms involving the ductal systems of any of a number of organs, such as the MAMMARY GLANDS, the PANCREAS, the PROSTATE, or the LACRIMAL GLAND.

68044882.name: Glucose Metabolism Disorders
68044882.note: Pathological conditions in which the BLOOD GLUCOSE cannot be maintained within the normal range, such as in HYPOGLYCEMIA and HYPERGLYCEMIA. Etiology of these disorders varies. Plasma glucose concentration is critical to survival for it is the predominant fuel for the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

68044903.name: Congenital Hyperinsulinism
68044903.note: A familial, nontransient HYPOGLYCEMIA with defects in negative feedback of GLUCOSE-regulated INSULIN release. Clinical phenotypes include HYPOGLYCEMIA; HYPERINSULINEMIA; SEIZURES; COMA; and often large BIRTH WEIGHT. Several sub-types exist with the most common, type 1, associated with mutations on a

68044904.name: Mannosidase Deficiency Diseases
68044904.note: Diseases caused by the loss of one or more enzymes involved in the hydrolysis of mannoside linkages (MANNOSIDASES). The defects in enzyme activity are primarily associated with genetic mutation of the genes that codes for a particular mannosidase isoenzyme.

68044905.name: beta-Mannosidosis
68044905.note: An inborn error of metabolism marked by a defect in the lysosomal isoform of BETA-MANNOSIDASE that results in lysosomal accumulation of mannose-rich intermediate metabolites containing 1,4-beta linkages. The human disease occurs through autosomal recessive inheritance and manifests in the form of a

68045169.name: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome
68045169.note: A viral disorder characterized by high FEVER, dry COUGH, shortness of breath (DYSPNEA) or breathing difficulties, and atypical PNEUMONIA. A virus in the genus CORONAVIRUS is the suspected agent.

68045262.name: Reticulocytosis
68045262.note: An increase in circulating RETICULOCYTES, which is among the simplest and most reliable signs of accelerated ERYTHROCYTE production. Reticulocytosis occurs during active BLOOD regeneration (stimulation of red bone marrow) and in certain types of ANEMIA, particularly CONGENITAL HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA.

68045463.name: Avulavirus Infections
68045463.note: Infections with viruses of the genus AVULAVIRUS, family PARAMYXOVIRIDAE. This includes NEWCASTLE DISEASE and other infections of domestic fowl.

68045464.name: Henipavirus Infections
68045464.note: Infections with viruses of the genus HENIPAVIRUS, family PARAMYXOVIRIDAE.

68045602.name: Steatorrhea
68045602.note: A condition that is characterized by chronic fatty DIARRHEA, a result of abnormal DIGESTION and/or INTESTINAL ABSORPTION of FATS.

68045723.name: Diverticulosis, Esophageal
68045723.note: A pathological condition characterized by the presence of a number of ESOPHAGEAL DIVERTICULA in the ESOPHAGUS.

68045724.name: Diverticulosis, Stomach
68045724.note: A pathological condition characterized by the presence of a number of GASTRIC DIVERTICULA in the STOMACH.

68045729.name: Pneumonia of Swine, Mycoplasmal
68045729.note: A chronic, clinically mild, infectious pneumonia of PIGS caused by MYCOPLASMA HYOPNEUMONIAE. Ninety percent of swine herds worldwide are infected with this economically costly disease that primarily affects animals aged two to six months old. The disease can be associated with porcine respiratory di

68045743.name: Scleroderma, Diffuse
68045743.note: A rapid onset form of SYSTEMIC SCLERODERMA with progressive widespread SKIN thickening over the arms, the legs and the trunk, resulting in stiffness and disability.

68045745.name: Scleroderma, Limited
68045745.note: The least progressive form of SYSTEMIC SCLERODERMA with skin thickening restricted to the face, neck and areas distal to the elbows and/or knees, sparing the trunk. The CREST SYNDROME is a form of limited scleroderma.

68045822.name: Intestinal Volvulus
68045822.note: A twisting in the intestine (INTESTINES) that can cause INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION.

68045823.name: Ileus
68045823.note: A condition caused by the lack of intestinal PERISTALSIS or INTESTINAL MOTILITY without any mechanical obstruction. This interference of the flow of INTESTINAL CONTENTS often leads to INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION. Ileus may be classified into postoperative, inflammatory, metabolic, neurogenic, and drug-in

68045824.name: Desulfovibrionaceae Infections
68045824.note: Infections with bacteria of the family Desulfovibrionaceae.

68045825.name: Fusobacteriaceae Infections
68045825.note: Infections with bacteria of the family Fusobacteriaceae, in the order Fusobacterales, phylum FUSOBACTERIA.

68045826.name: Flavobacteriaceae Infections
68045826.note: Infections with bacteria of the family FLAVOBACTERIACEAE.

68045827.name: Cytophagaceae Infections
68045827.note: Infections with bacteria of the family CYTOPHAGACEAE.

68045828.name: Moraxellaceae Infections
68045828.note: Infections with bacteria of the family MORAXELLACEAE.

68045888.name: Ganglion Cysts
68045888.note: Nodular tumor-like lesions or mucoid flesh, arising from tendon sheaths, LIGAMENTS, or JOINT CAPSULE, especially of the hands, wrists, or feet. They are not true cysts as they lack epithelial wall. They are distinguished from SYNOVIAL CYSTS by the lack of communication with a joint cavity or the SYN

68045908.name: Mpox, Monkeypox
68045908.note: A viral disease infecting PRIMATES and RODENTS. Its clinical presentation in humans is similar to SMALLPOX including FEVER; HEADACHE; COUGH; and a painful RASH. It is caused by MONKEYPOX VIRUS and is usually transmitted to humans through BITES or via contact with an animal's BLOOD. Interhuman transm

68046088.name: Hearing Loss, Unilateral
68046088.note: Partial or complete hearing loss in one ear.

68046089.name: Hearing Loss, Mixed Conductive-Sensorineural
68046089.note: Hearing loss due to damage or impairment of both the conductive elements (HEARING LOSS, CONDUCTIVE) and the sensorineural elements (HEARING LOSS, SENSORINEURAL) of the ear.

68046110.name: Hypertension, Pregnancy-Induced
68046110.note: A condition in PREGNANT PEOPLE with elevated systolic (>140 mm Hg) and diastolic (>90 mm Hg) blood pressure on at least two occasions 6 h apart. HYPERTENSION complicates 8-10% of all pregnancies, generally after 20 weeks of gestation. Gestational hypertension can be divided into several broad catego

68046150.name: Laron Syndrome
68046150.note: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by short stature, defective GROWTH HORMONE RECEPTOR, and failure to generate INSULIN-LIKE GROWTH FACTOR I by GROWTH HORMONE. Laron syndrome is not a form of primary pituitary dwarfism (GROWTH HORMONE DEFICIENCY DWARFISM) but the result of mutation of the

68046151.name: Lingual Thyroid
68046151.note: A condition characterized by the presence of rudimentary THYROID tissue at the base of the TONGUE. It is due to failed embryonic development and migration of thyroid tissue to its normal location. The lingual thyroid usually cannot maintain adequate hormone production thereby resulting in HYPOTHYROI

68046152.name: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors
68046152.note: All tumors in the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT arising from mesenchymal cells (MESODERM) except those of smooth muscle cells (LEIOMYOMA) or Schwann cells (SCHWANNOMA).

68046248.name: Pyloric Stenosis, Hypertrophic
68046248.note: Narrowing of the pyloric canal due to HYPERTROPHY of the surrounding circular muscle. It is usually seen in infants or young children.

68046290.name: Liver Abscess, Pyogenic
68046290.note: Single or multiple areas of PUS due to bacterial infection within the hepatic parenchyma. It can be caused by a variety of BACTERIA, local or disseminated from infections elsewhere such as in APPENDICITIS; CHOLECYSTITIS; PERITONITIS; and after LIVER TRANSPLANTATION.

68046349.name: Coproporphyria, Hereditary
68046349.note: An autosomal dominant porphyria that is due to a deficiency of COPROPORPHYRINOGEN OXIDASE in the LIVER, the sixth enzyme in the 8-enzyme biosynthetic pathway of HEME. Clinical features include both neurological symptoms and cutaneous lesions. Patients excrete increased levels of porphyrin precursors

68046350.name: Porphyria, Variegate
68046350.note: An autosomal dominant porphyria that is due to a deficiency of protoporphyrinogen oxidase (EC 1.3.3.4) in the LIVER, the seventh enzyme in the 8-enzyme biosynthetic pathway of HEME. Clinical features include both neurological symptoms and cutaneous lesions. Patients excrete increased levels of porph

68046351.name: Protoporphyria, Erythropoietic
68046351.note: An autosomal dominant porphyria that is due to a deficiency of FERROCHELATASE (heme synthetase) in both the LIVER and the BONE MARROW, the last enzyme in the 8-enzyme biosynthetic pathway of HEME. Clinical features include mainly neurological symptoms, rarely cutaneous lesions, and elevated levels o

68046449.name: Hernia, Abdominal
68046449.note: A protrusion of abdominal structures through the retaining ABDOMINAL WALL. It involves two parts: an opening in the abdominal wall, and a hernia sac consisting of PERITONEUM and abdominal contents. Abdominal hernias include groin hernia (HERNIA, FEMORAL; HERNIA, INGUINAL) and VENTRAL HERNIA.

68046548.name: Pubic Symphysis Diastasis
68046548.note: Separation of the PUBIC SYMPHYSIS. It is an uncommon complication of CHILDBIRTH causing postpartum PAIN, but it can also arise from other causes.

68046589.name: CADASIL
syn: Cerebral Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy
Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy
68046589.note: A familial, cerebral arteriopathy mapped to chromosome 19q12, and characterized by the presence of granular deposits in small CEREBRAL ARTERIES producing ischemic STROKE; PSEUDOBULBAR PALSY; and multiple subcortical infarcts (CEREBRAL INFARCTION). CADASIL is an acronym for Cerebral Autosomal Dominan

68046608.name: Synkinesis
68046608.note: An involuntary movement accompanying a volitional movement. It often refers to facial movements that accompany FACIAL PARALYSIS.

68046628.name: Sphincter of Oddi Dysfunction
68046628.note: Organic or functional motility disorder involving the SPHINCTER OF ODDI and associated with biliary COLIC. Pathological changes are most often seen in the COMMON BILE DUCT sphincter, and less commonly the PANCREATIC DUCT sphincter.

68046648.name: Hematoma, Subdural, Intracranial
68046648.note: Accumulation of blood in the SUBDURAL SPACE over the CEREBRAL HEMISPHERE.

68046649.name: Hematoma, Subdural, Spinal
68046649.note: Subdural hematoma of the SPINAL CANAL.

68046728.name: Colitis, Microscopic
68046728.note: A condition characterized by chronic watery DIARRHEA of unknown origin, a normal COLONOSCOPY but abnormal histopathology on BIOPSY. This syndrome was first described in 1980 by Read and associates. Subtypes include COLLAGENOUS COLITIS and LYMPHOCYTIC COLITIS. Both have similar clinical symptoms and

68046729.name: Colitis, Collagenous
68046729.note: A subtype of MICROSCOPIC COLITIS, characterized by chronic watery DIARRHEA of unknown origin, a normal COLONOSCOPY but abnormal histopathology on BIOPSY. Microscopic examination of biopsy samples taken from the COLON show larger-than-normal band of subepithelial COLLAGEN.

68046730.name: Colitis, Lymphocytic
68046730.note: A subtype of MICROSCOPIC COLITIS, characterized by chronic watery DIARRHEA of unknown origin, a normal COLONOSCOPY but abnormal histopathology on BIOPSY. Microscopic examination of biopsy samples taken from the COLON show infiltration of LYMPHOCYTES in the superficial EPITHELIUM and the underlying c

68046748.name: Hematoma, Epidural, Spinal
68046748.note: A rare epidural hematoma in the spinal epidural space, usually due to a vascular malformation (CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM VASCULAR MALFORMATIONS) or TRAUMA. Spontaneous spinal epidural hematoma is a neurologic emergency due to a rapidly evolving compressive MYELOPATHY.

68046768.name: Nesidioblastosis
68046768.note: An inherited autosomal recessive syndrome characterized by the disorganized formation of new islets in the PANCREAS and CONGENITAL HYPERINSULINISM. It is due to focal hyperplasia of pancreatic ISLET CELLS budding off from the ductal structures and forming new islets of Langerhans. Mutations in the i

68046788.name: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome
68046788.note: A syndrome characterized by retropatellar or peripatellar PAIN resulting from physical and biochemical changes in the patellofemoral joint. The pain is most prominent when ascending or descending stairs, squatting, or sitting with flexed knees. There is a lack of consensus on the etiology and treatm

68046789.name: Chondromalacia Patellae
68046789.note: A degeneration of the ARTICULAR CARTILAGE of the PATELLA, caused by a decrease in sulfated MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDES in the ground substance. When accompanied by pain, it is sometimes considered part of or confused with PATELLOFEMORAL PAIN SYNDROME.

68047268.name: Lingual Goiter
68047268.note: Pathological enlargement of the LINGUAL THYROID, ectopic thyroid tissue at the base of the TONGUE. It may cause upper AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION; DYSPHAGIA; or HYPOTHYROIDISM symptoms.

68047489.name: Preconception Injuries
68047489.note: Damages to reproductive health prior to conception (FERTILIZATION), a legal term for torts liability concerning environmental safety issues. Preconception injuries may involve either the male or the female, such as chromosomal mutations in the OVA or the SPERMATOZOA.

68047508.name: Massive Hepatic Necrosis
68047508.note: Extensive and rapid death of parenchymal cells in the LIVER, often due to exposure to toxic materials or drug-induced injury. It is characterized by a soft, flabby, yellow-brown wrinkled, and shrunken liver. It was called acute yellow atrophy.

68047688.name: Breast Cyst
68047688.note: A fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an EPITHELIUM and found in the BREAST. It may appear as a single large cyst in one breast, multifocal, or bilateral in FIBROCYSTIC BREAST DISEASE.

68047708.name: Myofibroma
68047708.note: A benign tumor that consists chiefly of fibrous CONNECTIVE TISSUE, with variable numbers of MUSCLE CELLS forming portions of the neoplasm (From Stedman's, 27th ed).

68047728.name: Myopia, Degenerative
68047728.note: Excessive axial myopia associated with complications (especially posterior staphyloma and CHOROIDAL NEOVASCULARIZATION) that can lead to BLINDNESS.

68047748.name: Pituitary ACTH Hypersecretion
68047748.note: A disease of the PITUITARY GLAND characterized by the excess amount of ADRENOCORTICOTROPIC HORMONE secreted. This leads to hypersecretion of cortisol (HYDROCORTISONE) by the ADRENAL GLANDS resulting in CUSHING SYNDROME.

68047808.name: Adrenogenital Syndrome
68047808.note: Abnormal SEX DIFFERENTIATION or congenital DISORDERS OF SEX DEVELOPMENT caused by abnormal levels of steroid hormones expressed by the GONADS or the ADRENAL GLANDS, such as in CONGENITAL ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA and ADRENAL CORTEX NEOPLASMS. Due to abnormal steroid biosynthesis, clinical features include

68047868.name: Pulmonary Sclerosing Hemangioma
68047868.note: A benign neoplasm of pneumocytes, cells of the PULMONARY ALVEOLI. Originally considered to be vascular in origin, it is now classified as an epithelial tumor with several elements, including solid cellular areas, papillary structure, sclerotic regions, and dilated blood-filled spaces resembling HEMA

68047928.name: Premature Birth
68047928.note: CHILDBIRTH before 37 weeks of PREGNANCY (259 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period, or 245 days after FERTILIZATION).

68048070.name: Fetal Nutrition Disorders
68048070.note: Disorders caused by nutritional imbalance, either overnutrition or undernutrition, in the FETUS in utero.

68048089.name: Pneumonia of Calves, Enzootic
68048089.note: Chronic endemic respiratory disease of dairy calves and an important component of bovine respiratory disease complex. It primarily affects calves up to six months of age and the etiology is multifactorial. Stress plus a primary viral infection is followed by a secondary bacterial infection. The latt

68048090.name: Bovine Respiratory Disease Complex
68048090.note: A multifactorial disease of CATTLE resulting from complex interactions between environmental factors, host factors, and pathogens. The environmental factors act as stressors adversely affecting the IMMUNE SYSTEM and other host defenses and enhancing transmission of infecting agents.

68048550.name: Hepatic Insufficiency
68048550.note: Conditions in which the LIVER functions fall below the normal ranges. Severe hepatic insufficiency may cause LIVER FAILURE or DEATH. Treatment may include LIVER TRANSPLANTATION.

68048629.name: Micronuclei, Chromosome-Defective
68048629.note: Defective nuclei produced during the TELOPHASE of MITOSIS or MEIOSIS by lagging CHROMOSOMES or chromosome fragments derived from spontaneous or experimentally induced chromosomal structural changes.

68048909.name: Diabetes Complications
68048909.note: Conditions or pathological processes associated with the disease of diabetes mellitus. Due to the impaired control of BLOOD GLUCOSE level in diabetic patients, pathological processes develop in numerous tissues and organs including the EYE, the KIDNEY, the BLOOD VESSELS, and the NERVE TISSUE.

68048949.name: Labor Pain
68048949.note: Pain associated with OBSTETRIC LABOR in CHILDBIRTH. It is caused primarily by UTERINE CONTRACTION as well as pressure on the CERVIX; BLADDER; and the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT. Labor pain mostly occurs in the ABDOMEN; the GROIN; and the BACK.

68048968.name: Morning Sickness
68048968.note: Symptoms of NAUSEA and VOMITING in PREGNANT PEOPLE that usually occur in the morning during the first 2 to 3 months of PREGNANCY. Severe persistent vomiting during pregnancy is called HYPEREMESIS GRAVIDARUM.

68049068.name: Plagiocephaly, Nonsynostotic
68049068.note: A deformity of the SKULL that is not due to bone fusion (SYNOSTOSIS), such as craniosynostoses, and is characterized by an asymmetric skull and face. It is observed with an increased frequency in INFANTS after the adoption of supine sleeping recommendations to prevent SUDDEN INFANT DEATH SYNDROME.

68049188.name: Prenatal Injuries
68049188.note: Damages to the EMBRYO, MAMMALIAN or the FETUS before BIRTH. Damages can be caused by any factors including biological, chemical, or physical.

68049248.name: Decapitation
68049248.note: Traumatic or experimentally induced separation of the head from the body in an animal or human.

68049288.name: Muscular Dystrophies, Limb-Girdle
68049288.note: A heterogenous group of inherited muscular dystrophy that can be autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive. There are many forms (called LGMDs) involving genes encoding muscle membrane proteins such as the sarcoglycan (SARCOGLYCANS) complex that interacts with DYSTROPHIN. The disease is characterize

68049290.name: Tay-Sachs Disease, AB Variant
68049290.note: A progressive neurodegenerative disorder that begins with muscle weakness, then progresses to startle reaction, retardation and seizures. It is characterized by the accumulation of G(M2) GANGLIOSIDE in neurons that is caused by a lack of G(M2) ACTIVATOR PROTEIN function. The AB variant designation r

68049291.name: Seroma
68049291.note: Tumor-like sterile accumulation of serum in a tissue, organ, or cavity. It results from a tissue insult and is the product of tissue inflammation. It most commonly occurs following MASTECTOMY.

68049292.name: Leukoaraiosis
68049292.note: Non-specific white matter changes in the BRAIN, often seen after age 65. Changes include loss of AXONS; MYELIN pallor, GLIOSIS, loss of ependymal cells, and enlarged perivascular spaces. Leukoaraiosis is a risk factor for DEMENTIA and CEREBROVASCULAR DISORDERS.

68049309.name: Acanthoma
68049309.note: A neoplasm composed of squamous or epidermal cells.

68049310.name: Distal Myopathies
68049310.note: A heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterized by progressive MUSCULAR ATROPHY and MUSCLE WEAKNESS beginning in the hands, the legs, or the feet. Most are adult-onset autosomal dominant forms. Others are autosomal recessive.

68049328.name: Mongolian Spot
68049328.note: A bluish-gray to gray-brown benign, melanocytic nevus found usually in the LUMBOSACRAL REGION of dark-skinned people, especially those of East Asian ancestry. It is usually congenital or appears shortly after birth, and disappears in childhood.

68049912.name: Growth Hormone-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma
68049912.note: A pituitary tumor that secretes GROWTH HORMONE. In humans, excess HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE leads to ACROMEGALY.

68049913.name: ACTH-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma
68049913.note: A pituitary adenoma which secretes ADRENOCORTICOTROPIN, leading to CUSHING DISEASE.

68049914.name: DNA Repair-Deficiency Disorders
68049914.note: Disorders resulting from defective DNA REPAIR processes or the associated cellular responses to DNA DAMAGE.

68049932.name: Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome
syn: Microcephaly with Normal Intelligence, Immunodeficiency, and Lymphoreticular Malignancies
Nonsyndromal Microcephaly, Autosomal Recessive, with Normal Intelligence
68049932.note: A chromosome instability syndrome resulting from a defective response to DNA double-strand breaks. In addition to characteristic FACIES and MICROCEPHALY, patients have a range of findings including RADIOSENSITIVITY, immunodeficiency, increased cancer risk, and growth retardation. Causative mutations

68049950.name: Hyperparathyroidism, Primary
68049950.note: A condition of abnormally elevated output of PARATHYROID HORMONE due to parathyroid HYPERPLASIA or PARATHYROID NEOPLASMS. It is characterized by the combination of HYPERCALCEMIA, phosphaturia, elevated renal 1,25-DIHYDROXYVITAMIN D3 synthesis, and increased BONE RESORPTION.

68049970.name: Graves Ophthalmopathy
68049970.note: An autoimmune disorder of the EYE, occurring in patients with Graves disease. Subtypes include congestive (inflammation of the orbital connective tissue), myopathic (swelling and dysfunction of the extraocular muscles), and mixed congestive-myopathic ophthalmopathy.

68050010.name: Hyperthyroxinemia, Familial Dysalbuminemic
68050010.note: An inherited autosomal dominant trait characterized by abnormally elevated levels of total serum THYROXINE; (T4) in euthyroid patients with abnormal SERUM ALBUMIN that binds T4 with enhanced affinity. The serum levels of free T4, free T3, and TSH are normal. It is one of several T4 abnormalities pro

68050030.name: Andersen Syndrome
syn: Periodic Paralysis, Potassium Sensitive Cardiodysrhythmic Type
Potassium-Sensitive Periodic Paralysis, Ventricular Ectopy, and Dysmorphic Features
68050030.note: A form of inherited long QT syndrome (or LQT7) that is characterized by a triad of potassium-sensitive periodic paralysis, VENTRICULAR ECTOPIC BEATS, and abnormal features such as short stature, low-set ears, and SCOLIOSIS. It results from mutations of KCNJ2 gene which encodes a channel protein (INW

68050031.name: Hashimoto Disease
68050031.note: Chronic autoimmune thyroiditis, characterized by the presence of high serum thyroid AUTOANTIBODIES; GOITER; and HYPOTHYROIDISM.

68050032.name: Postpartum Thyroiditis
68050032.note: Transient autoimmune thyroiditis occurring in the POSTPARTUM PERIOD. It is characterized by the presence of high titers of AUTOANTIBODIES against THYROID PEROXIDASE and THYROGLOBULIN. Clinical signs include the triphasic thyroid hormone pattern: beginning with THYROTOXICOSIS, followed with HYPOTHYRO

68050033.name: Thyroid Dysgenesis
68050033.note: Defective development of the THYROID GLAND. This concept includes thyroid agenesis (aplasia), hypoplasia, or an ectopic gland. Clinical signs usually are those of CONGENITAL HYPOTHYROIDISM.

68050035.name: Sexual Infantilism
68050035.note: The permanent lack of SEXUAL DEVELOPMENT in an individual. This defect is usually observed at an age after expected PUBERTY.

68050072.name: White Heifer Disease
68050072.note: A congenital reproductive abnormality in white female offspring (heifers) in certain breeds of CATTLE, such as Belgian Blue and Shorthorn. The white color is inherited as a recessive trait which is associated with defects in the female reproductive tract (Muellerian system). These heifers are usuall

68050090.name: Ovotesticular Disorders of Sex Development
68050090.note: Conditions of sexual ambiguity in which the individual possesses gonadal tissues of both sexes, tissues from the OVARY and the TESTIS. There can be a testis on one side and an ovary on the other (lateral), or there may be combined ovarian and testicular tissue (ovotestes) on each side (bilateral). T

68050171.name: Dyslipidemias
68050171.note: Abnormalities in the serum levels of LIPIDS, including overproduction or deficiency. Abnormal serum lipid profiles may include high total CHOLESTEROL, high TRIGLYCERIDES, low HIGH DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN CHOLESTEROL, and elevated LOW DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN CHOLESTEROL.

68050174.name: Genetic Diseases, Y-Linked
68050174.note: Genetic diseases that are linked to mutant ALLELES on the Y CHROMOSOME in humans (Y CHROMOSOME, HUMAN) or the Y chromosome in other species. Included here are animal models of human Y-linked diseases.

68050177.name: Overweight
68050177.note: A status with BODY WEIGHT that is above certain standards. In the scale of BODY MASS INDEX, overweight is defined as having a BMI of 25.0-29.9 kg/m2. Overweight may or may not be due to increases in body fat (ADIPOSE TISSUE), hence overweight does not equal over fat.

68050197.name: Atherosclerosis
68050197.note: A thickening and loss of elasticity of the walls of ARTERIES that occurs with formation of ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUES within the ARTERIAL INTIMA.

68050336.name: Mulibrey Nanism
68050336.note: Growth failure from birth that is due to mutations in a gene (TRIM37) on chromosome 17q22-q23 which encodes a RING-B-box-coiled-coil protein.

68050379.name: Arteriolosclerosis
68050379.note: Thickening of the walls of small ARTERIES or ARTERIOLES due to cell proliferation or HYALINE deposition.

68050380.name: Monckeberg Medial Calcific Sclerosis
68050380.note: Thickening and loss of elasticity of the walls of muscular ARTERIES due to calcification of the TUNICA MEDIA, the concentric layers of helically arranged SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS.

68050398.name: Adamantinoma
68050398.note: A locally aggressive, osteolytic neoplasm of the long bones, probably of epithelial origin and most often involving the TIBIA.

68050488.name: Hallux Varus
68050488.note: Displacement of the great toe (HALLUX) towards the midline or away from the other TOES. It can be congenital or acquired.

68050489.name: Bunion, Tailor's
68050489.note: Abnormal swelling of the outer aspect of the fifth metatarsal head affecting the fifth METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT.

68050497.name: Stillbirth
68050497.note: The event that a FETUS is born dead or stillborn.

68050500.name: Pancreatitis, Chronic
68050500.note: INFLAMMATION of the PANCREAS that is characterized by recurring or persistent ABDOMINAL PAIN with or without STEATORRHEA or DIABETES MELLITUS. It is characterized by the irregular destruction of the pancreatic parenchyma which may be focal, segmental, or diffuse.

68050738.name: Mesomycetozoea Infections
68050738.note: Infections by MESOMYCETOZOEA, general or unspecified.

68050798.name: SUNCT Syndrome
68050798.note: A primary headache disorder that is characterized by frequent short-lasting, unilateral, neuralgiform pain attacks in the ocular area, with CONJUNCTIVA fluid-filling and tearing. SUNCT syndrome is usually resistant to treatment.

68050805.name: Wandering Spleen
68050805.note: A congenital or acquired condition in which the SPLEEN is not in its normal anatomical position but moves about in the ABDOMEN. This is due to laxity or absence of suspensory ligaments which normally provide peritoneal attachments to keep the SPLEEN in a fixed position. Clinical symptoms include ABD

68050815.name: Fractures, Compression
68050815.note: Crumbling or smashing of cancellous BONE by forces acting parallel to the long axis of bone. It is applied particularly to vertebral body fractures (SPINAL FRACTURES). (Blauvelt and Nelson, A Manual of Orthopedic Terminology, 1994, p4)

68051261.name: Granulomatosis, Orofacial
68051261.note: A condition characterized by persistent or recurrent labial enlargement, ORAL ULCER, and other orofacial manifestations in the absence of identifiable CROHN DISEASE; or SARCOIDOSIS. Among experts there is disagreement on whether orofacial granulomatosis is a distinct clinical disorder or an initial

68051270.name: Headache Disorders, Primary
68051270.note: Conditions in which the primary symptom is HEADACHE and the headache cannot be attributed to any known causes.

68051271.name: Headache Disorders, Secondary
68051271.note: Conditions with HEADACHE symptom that can be attributed to a variety of causes including BRAIN VASCULAR DISORDERS; WOUNDS AND INJURIES; INFECTION; drug use or its withdrawal.

68051298.name: Post-Traumatic Headache
68051298.note: Secondary headache attributed to TRAUMA of the HEAD and/or the NECK.

68051299.name: Post-Dural Puncture Headache
68051299.note: A secondary headache disorder attributed to low CEREBROSPINAL FLUID pressure caused by SPINAL PUNCTURE, usually after dural or lumbar puncture.

68051302.name: Paroxysmal Hemicrania
68051302.note: A primary headache disorder that is similar to the CLUSTER HEADACHE with unilateral head pain, but differs by its multiple short severe attacks. It is usually seen in females, and may be responsive to non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS).

68051303.name: Trigeminal Autonomic Cephalalgias
68051303.note: Primary headache disorders that show symptoms caused by the activation of the AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM of the TRIGEMINAL NERVE. These autonomic features include redness and tearing of the EYE, nasal congestion or discharge, facial SWEATING and other symptoms. Most subgroups show unilateral cranial P

68051346.name: Mobility Limitation
68051346.note: Difficulty in walking from place to place.

68051359.name: Lymphohistiocytosis, Hemophagocytic
68051359.note: A group of related disorders characterized by LYMPHOCYTOSIS; HISTIOCYTOSIS; and hemophagocytosis. The two major forms are familial and reactive.

68051436.name: Renal Insufficiency, Chronic
68051436.note: Conditions in which the KIDNEYS perform below the normal level for more than three months. Chronic kidney insufficiency is classified by five stages according to the decline in GLOMERULAR FILTRATION RATE and the degree of kidney damage (as measured by the level of PROTEINURIA). The most severe form

68051437.name: Renal Insufficiency
68051437.note: Conditions in which the KIDNEYS perform below the normal level in the ability to remove wastes, concentrate URINE, and maintain ELECTROLYTE BALANCE; BLOOD PRESSURE; and CALCIUM metabolism. Renal insufficiency can be classified by the degree of kidney damage (as measured by the level of PROTEINURIA)

68051474.name: Neuralgia, Postherpetic
68051474.note: Pain in nerves, frequently involving facial SKIN, resulting from the activation the latent varicella-zoster virus (HERPESVIRUS 3, HUMAN). The two forms of the condition preceding the pain are HERPES ZOSTER OTICUS; and HERPES ZOSTER OPHTHALMICUS. Following the healing of the rashes and blisters, the

68051516.name: Hemospermia
68051516.note: Blood in the SEMEN, usually due to INFLAMMATION of the PROSTATE, the SEMINAL VESICLES, or both.

68051527.name: Odontogenic Tumor, Squamous
68051527.note: A well-differentiated, benign, hamartomatous proliferation of odontogenic epithelium, probably arising from the rests of Malassez.

68051556.name: Hyperbilirubinemia, Neonatal
68051556.note: Accumulation of BILIRUBIN, a breakdown product of HEME PROTEINS, in the BLOOD during the first weeks of life. This may lead to NEONATAL JAUNDICE. The excess bilirubin may exist in the unconjugated (indirect) or the conjugated (direct) form. The condition may be self-limiting (PHYSIOLOGICAL NEONATAL

68051642.name: Histiocytoma
68051642.note: A neoplasm containing HISTIOCYTES. Important forms include BENIGN FIBROUS HISTIOCYTOMA; and MALIGNANT FIBROUS HISTIOCYTOMA.

68051677.name: Histiocytoma, Malignant Fibrous
68051677.note: The most commonly diagnosed soft tissue sarcoma. It is a neoplasm with a fibrohistiocytic appearance found chiefly in later adult life, with peak incidence in the 7th decade.

68051799.name: Delayed Graft Function
68051799.note: General dysfunction of an organ occurring immediately following its transplantation. The term most frequently refers to renal dysfunction following KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION.

68052016.name: Mucositis
68052016.note: An INFLAMMATION of the MUCOSA with burning or tingling sensation. It is characterized by atrophy of the squamous EPITHELIUM, vascular damage, inflammatory infiltration, and ulceration. It usually occurs at the mucous lining of the MOUTH, the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT or the airway due to chemical irrit

68052065.name: Vaginismus
68052065.note: Recurrent or persistent involuntary SPASM of the outer muscles of the VAGINA, occurring during vaginal penetration.

68052120.name: Glycogen Storage Disease Type IIb
syn: Vacuolar Cardiomyopathy and Myopathy, X linked
X Linked Vacuolar Cardiomyopathy and Myopathy
68052120.note: An X-linked dominant multisystem disorder resulting in cardiomyopathy, myopathy and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY. It is caused by mutation in the gene encoding LYSOSOMAL-ASSOCIATED MEMBRANE PROTEIN 2.

68052159.name: Frasier Syndrome
68052159.note: A syndrome characterized by CHRONIC KIDNEY FAILURE and GONADAL DYSGENESIS in phenotypic females with karyotype of 46,XY or female individual with a normal 46,XX karyotype. It is caused by donor splice-site mutations of Wilms tumor suppressor gene (GENES, WILMS TUMOR) on chromosome 11.

68052177.name: Kidney Diseases, Cystic
