68057049.name: Thrombotic Microangiopathies
68057049.note: Diseases that result in THROMBOSIS in MICROVASCULATURE. The two most prominent diseases are PURPURA, THROMBOTIC THROMBOCYTOPENIC; and HEMOLYTIC-UREMIC SYNDROME. Multiple etiological factors include VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL CELL damage due to SHIGA TOXIN; FACTOR H deficiency; and aberrant VON WILLEBRAND

68057066.name: Low Tension Glaucoma
68057066.note: A form of glaucoma in which chronic optic nerve damage and loss of vision normally attributable to buildup of intraocular pressure occurs despite prevailing conditions of normal intraocular pressure.

68057068.name: Periprosthetic Fractures
68057068.note: Fractures around joint replacement prosthetics or implants. They can occur intraoperatively or postoperatively.

68057072.name: Intra-Articular Fractures
68057072.note: Fractures of the articular surface of a bone.

68057085.name: Tooth Wear
68057085.note: Loss of the tooth substance by chemical or mechanical processes

68057088.name: Anetoderma
68057088.note: Benign DERMATOSIS caused by a loss of dermal ELASTIC TISSUE resulting in localized sac-like areas of flaccid skin. It can be either primary (idiopathic) or secondary to other skin conditions, PENICILLAMINE use, or premature birth.

68057090.name: Eccrine Porocarcinoma
68057090.note: A rare malignant neoplasm of the sweat glands. It most often develops as a form of degenerative progression from a benign ECCRINE POROMA.

68057091.name: Poroma
68057091.note: A benign adnexal neoplasm derived from cells of the terminal duct of eccrine or apocrine SWEAT GLAND lineage. They typically manifest as solitary papules and occur only in the skin but unlike in ACROSPIROMA involves the epidermis.

68057092.name: Geographic Atrophy
68057092.note: A form of MACULAR DEGENERATION also known as dry macular degeneration marked by occurrence of a well-defined progressive lesion or atrophy in the central part of the RETINA called the MACULA LUTEA. It is distinguishable from WET MACULAR DEGENERATION in that the latter involves neovascular exudates.

68057096.name: Shellfish Poisoning
68057096.note: Poisoning from toxins present in bivalve mollusks that have been ingested. Four distinct types of shellfish poisoning are recognized based on the toxin involved.

68057108.name: Corneal Wavefront Aberration
68057108.note: Asymmetries in the topography and refractive index of the corneal surface that affect visual acuity.

68057112.name: Corneal Perforation
68057112.note: A puncture or hole through the CORNEAL STROMA resulting from various diseases or trauma.

68057129.name: Iridocorneal Endothelial Syndrome
syn: Iris Atrophy with Corneal Edema and Glaucoma
68057129.note: A grouping of three closely linked conditions: iris nevus (or Cogan-Reese) syndrome, Chandler Syndrome, and essential (progressive) iris atrophy. The most common features of this syndrome are the movement of endothelial cells off the cornea onto the iris leading to corneal swelling, distortion of th

68057130.name: Leber Congenital Amaurosis
68057130.note: A rare degenerative inherited eye disease that appears at birth or in the first few months of life that results in a loss of vision. Not to be confused with LEBER HEREDITARY OPTIC NEUROPATHY, the disease is thought to be caused by abnormal development of PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS in the RETINA, or by the

68057135.name: Wet Macular Degeneration
68057135.note: A form of RETINAL DEGENERATION in which abnormal CHOROIDAL NEOVASCULARIZATION occurs under the RETINA and MACULA LUTEA, causing bleeding and leaking of fluid. This leads to bulging and or lifting of the macula and the distortion or destruction of central vision.

68057165.name: Proteostasis Deficiencies
68057165.note: Disorders caused by imbalances in the PROTEIN HOMEOSTASIS network - synthesis, folding, and transport of proteins; post-translational modifications; and degradation or clearance of misfolded proteins.

68057174.name: Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration
68057174.note: Heterogeneous group of neurodegenerative disorders characterized by frontal and temporal lobe atrophy associated with neuronal loss, gliosis, and dementia. Patients exhibit progressive changes in social, behavioral, and/or language function. Multiple subtypes or forms are recognized based on presenc

68057177.name: TDP-43 Proteinopathies
68057177.note: Diseases characterized by the presence of abnormally phosphorylated, ubiquitinated, and cleaved DNA-binding protein TDP-43 in affected brain and spinal cord. Inclusions of the pathologic protein in neurons and glia, without the presence of AMYLOID, is the major feature of these conditions, thus maki

68057178.name: Primary Progressive Nonfluent Aphasia
68057178.note: A form of frontotemporal lobar degeneration and a progressive form of dementia characterized by motor speech impairment and AGRAMMATISM, with relative sparing of single word comprehension and semantic memory.

68057180.name: Frontotemporal Dementia
syn: Multiple System Tauopathy with Presenile Dementia
68057180.note: The most common clinical form of FRONTOTEMPORAL LOBAR DEGENERATION, this dementia presents with personality and behavioral changes often associated with disinhibition, apathy, and lack of insight.

68057667.name: Conducted Energy Weapon Injuries
68057667.note: The injuries caused by conducted energy weapons such as stun guns, shock batons, and cattle prods.

68057765.name: Eosinophilic Esophagitis
68057765.note: Chronic ESOPHAGITIS characterized by esophageal mucosal EOSINOPHILIA. It is diagnosed when an increase in EOSINOPHILS are present over the entire esophagus. The reflux symptoms fail to respond to PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS treatment, unlike in GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE. The symptoms are associated

68057767.name: Kashin-Beck Disease
68057767.note: Disabling osteochondrodysplasia with OSTEOSCLEROSIS, cone-shaped METAPHYSIS, and shortening of the DIAPHYSIS. It is endemic in parts of Siberia and northern China. Mineral deficiencies (e.g., selenium, iodine), fungal cereal contamination, and water contamination may be contributing factors in its e

68057768.name: Brief, Resolved, Unexplained Event
68057768.note: An event experienced by an infant or a child that is characterized by some combination of apnea, color change, change in muscle tone, choking, and gagging.

68057770.name: Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome
68057770.note: Autosomal recessive disorder characterized by HYALINE deposition in the skin, bone, gastrointestinal tract, muscles and glands; multiple subcutaneous skin nodules; GINGIVAL HYPERTROPHY; and joint CONTRACTURES. Mutations in the capillary morphogenesis protein-2 are associated with the disorder.

68057772.name: Vascular System Injuries
68057772.note: Injuries to blood vessels caused by laceration, contusion, puncture, or crush and other types of injuries. Symptoms vary by site and mode of injuries and may include bleeding, bruising, swelling, pain, and numbness. It does not include injuries secondary to pathologic function or diseases such as AT

68057774.name: Post-Exercise Hypotension
68057774.note: Transient reduction in blood pressure levels immediately after exercises that lasts 2-12 hours. The reduction varies but is typically 5-20 mm Hg when compared to pre-exercise levels. It exists both in normotensive and hypertensive individuals and may play a role in excercise related PHYSIOLOGIC ADAP

68057792.name: Mirizzi Syndrome
68057792.note: Complication of CHOLELITHIASIS characterized by OBSTRUCTIVE JAUNDICE; abdominal pain, and fever.

68057826.name: Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy
68057826.note: Autosomal dominant hereditary maculopathy with childhood-onset accumulation of LIPOFUSION in RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. Affected individuals develop progressive central acuity loss, and distorted vision (METAMORPHOPSIA). It is associated with mutations in bestrophin, a chloride channel.

68057831.name: Lemierre Syndrome
68057831.note: A superinfection of the damaged oropharyngeal mucosa by FUSOBACTERIUM NECROPHORUM leading to the secondary septic THROMBOPHLEBITIS of the internal jugular vein.

68057851.name: Posterior Capsular Rupture, Ocular
68057851.note: A breach in the continuity of the posterior chamber of the eyeball.

68057867.name: Endoleak
68057867.note: Postoperative hemorrhage from an endovascular AORTIC ANEURYSM repaired with endoluminal placement of stent grafts (ENDOVASCULAR ANEURYSM REPAIR). It is associated with pressurization, expansion, and eventual rupture of the aneurysm.

68057868.name: Anastomotic Leak
68057868.note: Breakdown of the connection and subsequent leakage of effluent (fluids, secretions, air) from a SURGICAL ANASTOMOSIS of the digestive, respiratory, genitourinary, and cardiovascular systems. Most common leakages are from the breakdown of suture lines in gastrointestinal or bowel anastomosis.

68057873.name: Peri-Implantitis
68057873.note: An inflammatory process with loss of supporting bone in the tissues surrounding functioning DENTAL IMPLANTS.

68057885.name: Triploidy
68057885.note: Polyploidy with three sets of chromosomes. Triploidy in humans are 69XXX, 69XXY, and 69XYY. It is associated with HOLOPROSENCEPHALY; ABNORMALITIES, MULTIPLE; PARTIAL HYDATIDIFORM MOLE; and MISCARRAGES.

68057887.name: Overbite
68057887.note: A malocclusion in which maxillary incisor and canine teeth project over the mandibular teeth excessively. The overlap is measured perpendicular to the occlusal plane and is also called vertical overlap. When the overlap is measured parallel to the occlusal plane it is referred to as overjet.

68057891.name: Tetraploidy
68057891.note: The presence of four sets of chromosomes. It is associated with ABNORMALITIES, MULTIPLE; and MISCARRAGES.

68057896.name: Striae Distensae
68057896.note: Linear dermal scars accompanied by epidermal atrophy that affects skin that is subjected to continuous stretching. They usually do not cause any significant medical problems, only cosmetic problems.

68057910.name: Implant Capsular Contracture
68057910.note: The shrinkage of the foreign body encapsulation scar tissue that forms around artificial implants imbedded in body tissues.

68057925.name: Femoracetabular Impingement
68057925.note: A pathological mechanical process that can lead to hip failure. It is caused by abnormalities of the ACETABULUM and/or FEMUR combined with rigorous hip motion, leading to repetitive collisions that damage the soft tissue structures.

68057971.name: Anterior Capsular Rupture, Ocular
68057971.note: A breach in the continuity of the ANTERIOR CHAMBER of the eyeball.

68057973.name: Dent Disease
68057973.note: X-linked recessive NEPHROLITHIASIS characterized by HYPERCALCIURIA; HYPOPHOSPHATEMIA; NEPHROCALCINOSIS; and PROTEINURIA. It is associated with mutations in the voltage-gated chloride channel, CLC-5 (Dent Disease I). Another group of mutations associated with this disease is in phosphatidylinositol 4

68058065.name: Diabetic Cardiomyopathies
68058065.note: Diabetes complications in which VENTRICULAR REMODELING in the absence of CORONARY ATHEROSCLEROSIS and hypertension results in cardiac dysfunctions, typically LEFT VENTRICULAR DYSFUNCTION. The changes also result in myocardial hypertrophy, myocardial necrosis and fibrosis, and collagen deposition due

68058066.name: Digital Dermatitis
68058066.note: Highly contagious infectious dermatitis with lesions near the interdigital spaces usually in cattle. It causes discomfort and often severe lameness (LAMENESS, ANIMAL). Lesions can be either erosive or proliferative and wart-like with papillary growths and hypertrophied hairs. DICHELOBACTER NODOSUS a

68058069.name: Neglected Diseases
68058069.note: Diseases that are underfunded and have low name recognition but are major burdens in less developed countries. Neglected diseases include many tropical infectious diseases, e.g., HELMINTHIASIS; LEPROSY; LYMPHATIC FILARIASIS; ONCHOCERCIASIS; SCHISTOSOMIASIS; and TRACHOMA.

68058070.name: Asymptomatic Diseases
68058070.note: Diseases that do not exhibit symptoms.

68058088.name: Sarcoglycanopathies
syn: Duchenne-Like Autosomal Recessive Muscular Dystrophy, Type 2
Duchenne Like Autosomal Recessive Muscular Dystrophy, Type 2
68058088.note: Deficiencies or mutations in the genes for the SARCOGLYCAN COMPLEX subunits. A variety of phenotypes are associated with these mutations including a subgroup of autosomal recessive limb girdle muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and respiratory deficiency.

68058165.name: 22q11 Deletion Syndrome
68058165.note: Condition with a variable constellation of phenotypes due to deletion polymorphisms at chromosome location 22q11. It encompasses several syndromes with overlapping abnormalities including the DIGEORGE SYNDROME, VELOCARDIOFACIAL SYNDROME, and CONOTRUNCAL AMOMALY FACE SYNDROME. In addition, variable d

68058186.name: Acute Kidney Injury
68058186.note: Abrupt reduction in kidney function. Acute kidney injury encompasses the entire spectrum of the syndrome including acute kidney failure; ACUTE KIDNEY TUBULAR NECROSIS; and other less severe conditions.

68058225.name: Plaque, Amyloid
68058225.note: Accumulations of extracellularly deposited AMYLOID FIBRILS within tissues.

68058226.name: Plaque, Atherosclerotic
68058226.note: Lesions formed within the walls of ARTERIES associated with deposits of fat and other substances that accumulate in the lining of the artery wall.

68058246.name: Prehypertension
68058246.note: Blood pressure levels that are between normotension and hypertension. Individuals with prehypertension are at a higher risk for developing cardiovascular diseases. Generally, prehypertension is defined as SYSTOLIC PRESSURE of 131-139 mm Hg and/or DIASTOLIC PRESSURE of 81-89 when the optimal is 120/8

68058247.name: Loose Anagen Hair Syndrome
68058247.note: Benign childhood alopecia that improves spontaneously with aging. It is characterized by anagen hairs (misshapen hair bulbs and absent inner and outer root sheaths), thin, and sparse hairs that pulls out easily.

68058249.name: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
68058249.note: Autosomal dominant neoplastic syndrome characterised by genodermatosis, lung cysts, spontaneous and recurrent PNEUMOTHORAX; and RENAL CANCER. It is associated with mutations in the folliculin protein gene (FLCN protein).

68058252.name: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
68058252.note: A cutaneous necrobiotic disorder characterized by firm, yellow plaques or nodules, often in a periorbital distribution. It is often accompanied by an elevated ERYTHROCYTE SEDIMENTATION RATE; LEUKOPENIA; and MONOCLONAL GAMMOPATHY (IgG-kappa type) and systemic involvement.

68058267.name: Flea Infestations
68058267.note: Parasitic attack by members of the order SIPHONAPTERA.

68058285.name: Tungiasis
68058285.note: An infestation with the flea TUNGA PENETRANS causing inflammation, pruritus, and pain, in both humans and other mammals. There is a high incidence of secondary infections such as BACTEREMIA and TETANUS.

68058288.name: Sister Mary Joseph's Nodule
68058288.note: Metastatic lesion of the UMBILICUS associated with intra-abdominal neoplasms especially of the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT or OVARY.

68058345.name: Asymptomatic Infections
68058345.note: Infections that do not exhibit symptoms.

68058365.name: Candidiasis, Invasive
68058365.note: An important nosocomial fungal infection with species of the genus CANDIDA, most frequently CANDIDA ALBICANS. Invasive candidiasis occurs when candidiasis goes beyond a superficial infection and manifests as CANDIDEMIA, deep tissue infection, or disseminated disease with deep organ involvement.

68058387.name: Candidemia
68058387.note: A form of invasive candidiasis where species of CANDIDA are present in the blood.

68058405.name: Desmoplastic Small Round Cell Tumor
68058405.note: A rare, aggressive soft tissue sarcoma that primarily affects adolescents and young adults. It is most commonly found in the abdomen.

68058426.name: Neointima
68058426.note: The new and thickened layer of scar tissue that forms on a PROSTHESIS, or as a result of vessel injury especially following ANGIOPLASTY or stent placement.

68058429.name: Gnathostomiasis
68058429.note: Infections with nematodes of the genus GNATHOSTOMA, superfamily THELAZIOIDEA. Gnathostomiasis is a food-borne zoonosis caused by eating undercooked or raw fish or meat.

68058437.name: Hypertensive Retinopathy
68058437.note: Degenerative changes to the RETINA due to HYPERTENSION.

68058442.name: Capsule Opacification
68058442.note: Clouding or loss of transparency of the posterior lens capsule, usually following CATARACT extraction.

68058447.name: Eye Pain
68058447.note: A dull or sharp painful sensation associated with the outer or inner structures of the eyeball, having different causes.

68058456.name: Retinal Telangiectasis
68058456.note: A group of rare, idiopathic, congenital retinal vascular anomalies affecting the retinal capillaries. It is characterized by dilation and tortuosity of retinal vessels and formation of multiple aneurysms, with different degrees of leakage and exudates emanating from the blood vessels.

68058457.name: Trichiasis
68058457.note: A disease of the eye in which the eyelashes abnormally turn inwards toward the eyeball producing constant irritation caused by motion of the lids.

68058489.name: 46, XX Disorders of Sex Development
68058489.note: Congenital conditions in individuals with a female karyotype, in which the development of the gonadal or anatomical sex is atypical.

68058490.name: Disorder of Sex Development, 46,XY
syn: 46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis, Complete or Partial, With or Without Adrenal Failure
46,XY Sex Reversal, Partial or Complete, NR5A1-Related
Sex Reversal, XY, With Or Without Adrenal Failure
68058490.note: Congenital conditions in individuals with a male karyotype, in which the development of the gonadal or anatomical sex is atypical.

68058494.name: Walker-Warburg Syndrome
68058494.note: Rare autosomal recessive lissencephaly type 2 associated with congenital MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY and eye anomalies (e.g., RETINAL DETACHMENT; CATARACT; MICROPHTHALMOS). It is often associated with additional brain malformations such as HYDROCEPHALY and cerebellar hypoplasia and is the most severe form of

68058495.name: Sotos Syndrome
68058495.note: Congenital or postnatal overgrowth syndrome most often in height and occipitofrontal circumference with variable delayed motor and cognitive development. Other associated features include advanced bone age, seizures, NEONATAL JAUNDICE; HYPOTONIA; and SCOLIOSIS. It is also associated with increased r

68058496.name: Smith-Magenis Syndrome
68058496.note: Complex neurobehavioral disorder characterized by distinctive facial features (FACIES), developmental delay and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY. Behavioral phenotypes include sleep disturbance, maladaptive, self-injurious and attention-seeking behaviors. The sleep disturbance is linked to an abnormal circad

68058497.name: Fraser Syndrome
68058497.note: Rare autosomal recessive congenital malformation syndrome characterized by cryptophthalmos, SYNDACTYLY and UROGENITAL ABNORMALITIES. Other anomalies of bone, ear, lung, and nose are common. Mutations on FRAS1 and FREM2 are associated with the syndrome.

68058499.name: Retinal Dystrophies
68058499.note: A group of disorders involving predominantly the posterior portion of the ocular fundus, due to degeneration in the sensory layer of the RETINA; RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM; BRUCH MEMBRANE; CHOROID; or a combination of these tissues.

68058502.name: Pentalogy of Cantrell
68058502.note: Rare congenital deformity syndrome characterized by a combination of five anomalies as a result of neural tube defect. The five anomalies are a midline supraumbilical abdominal wall defect (e.g., OMPHALOCELE), a lower STERNUM defect, a congenital intracardiac defect, an anterior DIAPHRAGM defect, an

68058527.name: Enteropathy-Associated T-Cell Lymphoma
68058527.note: A primary peripheral T-cell lymphoma in the gastrointestinal tract, most often in the jejunum, associated with a history of CELIAC DISEASE or other gastrointestinal diseases.

68058529.name: Single Umbilical Artery
68058529.note: Congenital abnormality where one, instead of the usual two, UMBILICAL ARTERY connects the fetus to the placenta.

68058531.name: 46, XX Testicular Disorders of Sex Development
syn: 46, XX Testicular Disorder of Sex Development
68058531.note: Congenital conditions in individuals in which male GONADS develop in a genetic female (female to male sex reversal).

68058533.name: Sex Chromosome Disorders of Sex Development
68058533.note: Congenital conditions of atypical sexual development associated with abnormal sex chromosome constitutions including MONOSOMY; TRISOMY; and MOSAICISM.

68058535.name: Echogenic Bowel
68058535.note: A PRENATAL ULTRASONOGRAPHY finding of excessively dense fetal bowel due to MECONIUM buildup.

68058536.name: Pyelectasis
68058536.note: Dilation of fetal KIDNEY PELVIS. It is a common PRENATAL ULTRASONOGRAPHY finding with no significant long-term sequelae.

68058540.name: Aicardi Syndrome
syn: Corpus Callosum, Agenesis Of, With Chorioretinal Abnormality
Agenesis of Corpus Callosum with Infantile Spasms and Ocular Abnormalities
Agenesis of Corpus Callosum with Chorioretinal Abnormality
68058540.note: A rare genetic disorder characterized by partial or complete absence of the CORPUS CALLOSUM, resulting in infantile spasms, MENTAL RETARDATION, and lesions of the RETINA or OPTIC NERVE.

68058545.name: Inhalant Abuse
68058545.note: Illicit use of chemicals and products whose vapors can be inhaled to produce a rapid mind-altering effect. Inhalants include aerosols, gases, and volatile solvents that are often inhaled repeatedly to achieve the short-lived intoxicating effect.

68058566.name: Sacroiliitis
68058566.note: Inflammation of the SACROILIAC JOINT. It is characterized by lower back pain, especially upon walking, fever, UVEITIS; PSORIASIS; and decreased range of motion. Many factors are associated with and cause sacroiliitis including infection; injury to spine, lower back, and pelvis; DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITI

68058568.name: Necrolytic Migratory Erythema
68058568.note: Recurrent cutaneous manifestation of GLUCAGONOMA characterized by necrolytic polycyclic migratory lesions with scaling borders. It is associated with elevated secretion of GLUCAGON by the tumor. Other conditions with elevated serum glucagon levels such as HEPATIC CIRRHOSIS may also result in similar

68058606.name: Accessory Atrioventricular Bundle
68058606.note: Extra impulse-conducting tissue in the heart that creates abnormal impulse-conducting connections between HEART ATRIA and HEART VENTRICLES.

68058617.name: Composite Lymphoma
68058617.note: Two or more distinct types of malignant lymphoid tumors occurring within a single organ or tissue at the same time. It may contain different types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells or both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells.

68058625.name: End Stage Liver Disease
68058625.note: Final stage of a liver disease when the liver failure is irreversible and LIVER TRANSPLANTATION is needed.

68058627.name: Megalencephaly
68058627.note: A congenital abnormality in which the occipitofrontal circumference is greater than two standard deviations above the mean for a given age. It is associated with HYDROCEPHALUS; SUBDURAL EFFUSION; ARACHNOID CYSTS; or is part of a genetic condition (e.g., ALEXANDER DISEASE; SOTOS SYNDROME).

68058631.name: Pycnodysostosis
68058631.note: Rare autosomal recessive syndrome characterized by delayed closing of CRANIAL SUTURES, short stature, ACRO-OSTEOLYSIS of distal phalanges, dental and MAXILLOFACIAL ABNORMALITIES and an increase in bone density that results in frequent BONE FRACTURES. It is associated with BONE RESORPTION defect due

68058670.name: Tetrasomy
68058670.note: The possession of four chromosomes of any one type in an otherwise diploid cell.

68058674.name: Chromosome Duplication
68058674.note: An aberration in which an extra chromosome or a chromosomal segment is made.

68058686.name: Coronary-Subclavian Steal Syndrome
68058686.note: A complication of INTERNAL MAMMARY-CORONARY ARTERY ANASTOMOSIS whereby an occlusion or stenosis of the proximal SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY causes a reversal of the blood flow away from the CORONARY CIRCULATION, through the grafted INTERNAL MAMMARY ARTERY (internal thoracic artery), and back to the distal sub

68058687.name: Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
68058687.note: Occurrence of heart arrest in an individual when there is no immediate access to medical personnel or equipment.

68058729.name: Peripheral Arterial Disease
68058729.note: Lack of perfusion in the EXTREMITIES resulting from atherosclerosis. It is characterized by INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION, and an ANKLE BRACHIAL INDEX of 0.9 or less.

68058734.name: Exsanguination
68058734.note: Rapid and extreme blood loss leading to HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK.

68058736.name: Intrauterine Device Migration
68058736.note: The shifting in position or location of an INTRAUTERINE DEVICE from its original placement.

68058739.name: Aberrant Crypt Foci
68058739.note: Clusters of colonic crypts that appear different from the surrounding mucosa when visualized after staining. They are of interest as putative precursors to colorectal adenomas and potential biomarkers for colorectal carcinoma.

68058745.name: Iliotibial Band Syndrome
68058745.note: An overuse injury causing lateral knee pain that results from repetitive friction of the iliotibial band over the lateral femoral epicondyle.

68058747.name: CHARGE Syndrome
syn: CHARGE Association--Coloboma, Heart Anomaly, Choanal Atresia, Retardation, Genital and Ear Anomalies
Coloboma, Heart Anomaly, Choanal Atresia, Retardation, Genital and Ear Anomalies
68058747.note: Rare disease characterized by COLOBOMA; CHOANAL ATRESIA; and abnormal SEMICIRCULAR CANALS. Mutations in CHD7 protein resulting in disturbed neural crest development are associated with CHARGE Syndrome.

68058866.name: Osteoporotic Fractures
68058866.note: Breaks in bones resulting from low bone mass and microarchitectural deterioration characteristic of OSTEOPOROSIS.

68058890.name: Granulomatous Mastitis
68058890.note: A rare, benign, inflammatory breast disease occurring in premenopausal women shortly after a recent pregnancy. The origin is unknown but it is commonly mistaken for malignancy and sometimes associated with BREAST FEEDING and the use of ORAL CONTRACEPTIVES.

68058922.name: Inflammatory Breast Neoplasms
68058922.note: Metastatic breast cancer characterized by EDEMA and ERYTHEMA of the affected breast due to LYMPHATIC METASTASIS and eventual obstruction of LYMPHATIC VESSELS by the cancer cells.

68058923.name: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome
68058923.note: SKELETAL MUSCLE pain and tenderness along the posteromedial TIBIA resulting from exercise such as running and other physical activity.

68058926.name: Intraoperative Awareness
68058926.note: Occurence of a patient becoming conscious during a procedure performed under GENERAL ANESTHESIA and subsequently having recall of these events. (From Anesthesiology 2006, 104(4): 847-64.)

68058968.name: Pythiosis
68058968.note: A granulomatous disease caused by the aquatic organism PYTHIUM insidiosum and occurring primarily in horses, cattle, dogs, cats, fishes, and rarely in humans. It is classified into three forms: ocular, cutaneous, and arterial.

68059041.name: Plagiocephaly
68059041.note: The condition characterized by uneven or irregular shape of the head often in parallelogram shape with a flat spot on the back or one side of the head. It can either result from the premature CRANIAL SUTURE closure (CRANIOSYNOSTOSIS) or from external forces (NONSYNOSTOTIC PLAGIOCEPHALY).

68059226.name: Nociceptive Pain
68059226.note: Dull or sharp aching pain caused by stimulated NOCICEPTORS due to tissue injury, inflammation or diseases. It can be divided into somatic or tissue pain and VISCERAL PAIN.

68059228.name: Renal Nutcracker Syndrome
68059228.note: Left RENAL VEIN compression between the AORTA, ABDOMINAL and the SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY. Variable symptoms include HYPERTENSION, RENOVASCULAR; HEMATURIA; and VARICOSE VEINS.

68059245.name: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn
68059245.note: Abnormal increase in RESPIRATORY RATE in the newborn. It is self-limiting and attributed to the delayed fetal lung fluid clearance often in CAESAREAN SECTION delivery.

68059249.name: Otomycosis
68059249.note: Fungus infection of the external ear, usually by ASPERGILLUS species

68059265.name: Visceral Pain
68059265.note: Pain originating from internal organs (VISCERA) associated with autonomic phenomena (PALLOR; SWEATING; NAUSEA; and VOMITING). It often becomes a REFERRED PAIN.

68059266.name: Bisphosphonate-Associated Osteonecrosis of the Jaw
syn: Bisphosphonate Associated Osteonecrosis of the Jaw
Osteonecrosis of the Jaws, Bisphosphonate Associated
Bisphosphonate Induced Osteonecrosis of the Jaw
Bisphosphonate Induced Osteonecrosis of the Jaws
Bisphosphonate Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw
Osteonecrosis of the Jaw, Bisphosphonate Induced
Osteonecrosis of the Jaw, Bisphosphonate Related
Osteonecrosis of the Jaws, Bisphosphonate Induced
68059266.note: Necrotic jaws or other maxillofacial skeleton necrosis associated with bisphosphonate use (see BISPHOSPHONATES). Injury, dental procedures, and trauma can trigger the necrotic process.

68059268.name: Atrophic Vaginitis
68059268.note: Inflammation of the vagina due to thinning of the vaginal wall and decreased lubrication associated with reduced estrogen levels at MENOPAUSE.

68059269.name: Chilaiditi Syndrome
68059269.note: Interposition of a portion of the colon (e.g., SIGMOID COLON) between the liver and the diaphragm. It is associated with abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, anorexia and volvulus. Chilaiditi anomaly refers to asymptomatic interposition.

68059325.name: Intra-Abdominal Hypertension
68059325.note: Pathological elevation of intra-abdominal pressure (>12 mm Hg). It may develop as a result of SEPSIS; PANCREATITIS; capillary leaks, burns, or surgery. When the pressure is higher than 20 mm Hg, often with end-organ dysfunction, it is referred to as abdominal compartment syndrome.

68059327.name: Brachydactyly
68059327.note: Congenital anomaly of abnormally short fingers or toes.

68059345.name: Cerebral Small Vessel Diseases
68059345.note: Pathological processes or diseases where cerebral MICROVESSELS show abnormalities. They are often associated with aging, hypertension and risk factors for lacunar infarcts (see LACUNAR INFARCTION); LEUKOARAIOSIS; and CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE.

68059347.name: Cardio-Renal Syndrome
68059347.note: Condition where a primary dysfunction of either heart or kidney results in failure of the other organ (e.g., HEART FAILURE with worsening RENAL INSUFFICIENCY).

68059350.name: Chronic Pain
68059350.note: Aching sensation that persists for more than a few months. It may or may not be associated with trauma or disease, and may persist after the initial injury has healed. Its localization, character, and timing are more vague than with acute pain.

68059352.name: Musculoskeletal Pain
68059352.note: Discomfort stemming from muscles, LIGAMENTS, tendons, and bones.

68059366.name: Asthma, Occupational
68059366.note: Asthma attacks caused, triggered, or exacerbated by OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURE.

68059369.name: Pott Puffy Tumor
68059369.note: Infection of the FRONTAL BONE often as a complication of FRONTAL SINUSITIS or trauma to the frontal bone and skull. It is characterized by subperiosteal abscess with OSTEOMYELITIS.

68059373.name: Mastodynia
68059373.note: Pain in the breast generally classified as cyclical (associated with menstrual periods), or noncyclical, i.e. originating from the breast or nearby muscles or joints, ranging from minor discomfort to severely incapacitating.

68059388.name: Pelvic Girdle Pain
68059388.note: Discomfort associated with the bones that make up the pelvic girdle. It occurs frequently during pregnancy.

68059390.name: Breakthrough Pain
68059390.note: Acute pain that comes on rapidly despite the use of pain medication.

68059407.name: Pinguecula
68059407.note: A yellowish thickened lesion on the conjunctiva near the CORNEA representing a benign degenerative change in the CONJUNCTIVA caused by the leakage and deposition of certain blood proteins through the permeable capillaries near the LIMBUS.

68059409.name: Stroke, Lacunar
68059409.note: Stroke caused by lacunar infarction or other small vessel diseases of the brain. It features hemiparesis (see PARESIS), hemisensory, or hemisensory motor loss.

68059411.name: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms
68059411.note: Symptoms of disorders of the lower urinary tract including frequency, NOCTURIA; urgency, incomplete voiding, and URINARY INCONTINENCE. They are often associated with OVERACTIVE BLADDER; URINARY INCOMPETENCE; and INTERSTITIAL CYSTITIS. Lower urinary tract symptoms in males were traditionally called P

68059413.name: Intraabdominal Infections
68059413.note: Infection within the PERITONEAL CAVITY. A frequent cause is an ANASTOMOTIC LEAK following surgery.

68059445.name: Anhedonia
68059445.note: Inability to experience pleasure due to impairment or dysfunction of normal psychological and neurobiological mechanisms. It is a symptom of many PSYCHOTIC DISORDERS (e.g., DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, MAJOR; and SCHIZOPHRENIA).

68059446.name: Heterotaxy Syndrome
68059446.note: Abnormal thoracoabdominal VISCERA arrangement (visceral heterotaxy) or malformation that involves additional CONGENITAL HEART DEFECTS (e.g., heart isomerism; DEXTROCARDIA) and/or abnormal SPLEEN (e.g., asplenia and polysplenia). Irregularities with the central nervous system, the skeleton and urinar

68059466.name: White Coat Hypertension
68059466.note: Phenomenon where BLOOD PRESSURE readings are elevated only when taken in clinical settings.

68059468.name: Masked Hypertension
68059468.note: Phenomenon where increased BLOOD PRESSURE readings taken in non-clinical settings (e.g., HOME BLOOD PRESSURE MONITORING) do not replicate in clinical settings.

68059525.name: Supraglottitis
68059525.note: Inflammation of the EPIGLOTTIS and supraglottic structures including the PHARYNX; UVULA; base of tongue; and aryepiglottic folds. It is usually caused by HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE in children but often by different organisms in adults.

68059545.name: Paraneoplastic Syndromes, Ocular
68059545.note: Ocular manifestations secondary to various NEOPLASMS in which antibodies to antigens of the primary tumor cross-react with ocular antigens. This autoimmune response often leads to visual loss and other ocular dysfunctions.

68059606.name: Polydipsia
68059606.note: Excessive thirst manifested by excessive fluid intake. It is characteristic of many diseases such as DIABETES MELLITUS; DIABETES INSIPIDUS; and NEPHROGENIC DIABETES INSIPIDUS. The condition may be psychogenic in origin.

68059607.name: Polydipsia, Psychogenic
68059607.note: A clinical disorder characterized by excessive fluid intake (polydipsia); HYPONATREMIA; and POLYURIA in SCHIZOPHRENIA and other psychiatric disorders. Impaired water metabolism in psychogenic polydipsia can result in WATER INTOXICATION.

68059608.name: Laryngocele
68059608.note: Congenital anomalous dilitation of the laryngeal saccule that may extend internally into the airway or externally through the thyrohyoid membrane.

68059707.name: Aliivibrio Infections
68059707.note: Infections with bacteria of the genus ALIIVIBRIO.

68059786.name: Abnormal Karyotype
68059786.note: A variation from the normal set of chromosomes characteristic of a species.

68059787.name: Acute Pain
68059787.note: Intensely discomforting, distressful, or agonizing sensation associated with trauma or disease, with well-defined location, character, and timing.

68059885.name: Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome
68059885.note: Rapidly growing vascular lesion along the midline axis of the neck, upper trunk, and extremities that is characterized by CONSUMPTION COAGULOPATHY; THROMBOCYTOPENIA; and HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA. It is often associated with infantile Kaposiform HEMANGIOENDOTHELIOMA and other vascular tumors such as tufted A

68059905.name: Endocarditis, Non-Infective
68059905.note: Formation of a non-infectious THROMBUS, referred to as vegetation, on previously undamaged ENDOCARDIUM. It usually occurs as a complication of connective-tissue diseases and cancers because of the associated hypercoagulable state (see THROMBOPHILIA).

68059952.name: Pelvic Floor Disorders
68059952.note: Injury, weakening, or PROLAPSE of the pelvic muscles, surrounding connective tissues or ligaments (PELVIC FLOOR).

68060048.name: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphyses
68060048.note: A developmental deformity in which the metaphysis of the FEMUR moves proximally and anteriorly away from FEMUR HEAD (epiphysis) at the upper GROWTH PLATE. It is most common in male adolescents and is associated with a greater risk of early OSTEOARTHRITIS of the hip.

68060050.name: Angina, Stable
68060050.note: Persistent and reproducible chest discomfort usually precipitated by a physical exertion that dissipates upon cessation of such an activity. The symptoms are manifestations of MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA.

68060051.name: Occupational Injuries
68060051.note: Injuries sustained from incidents in the course of work-related activities.

68060085.name: Coinfection
68060085.note: Simultaneous infection of a host organism by two or more pathogens. In virology, coinfection commonly refers to simultaneous infection of a single cell by two or more different viruses.

68060368.name: Lobomycosis
68060368.note: A chronic, fungal, subcutaneous infection endemic in rural regions in South America and Central America. The causal organism is Lacazia labol.

68060425.name: Cerebral Phaeohyphomycosis
68060425.note: CNS infections caused by neurotropic dematiaceous fungi that contain melanin in their cell walls. The infections often result in BRAIN ABSCESS; ENCEPHALITIS; and MENINGITIS in patients who are often immunocompetent. The common causative fungi include members Cladophialophora bantiana, Exophiala derm

68060426.name: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis
syn: Anti N Methyl D Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis
68060426.note: Disorder characterized by symptoms of CATATONIA; HYPOVENTILATION; DYSKINESIAS; ENCEPHALITIS; and SEIZURES followed by a reduced CONSCIOUSNESS. It is often followed by a viral-like prodrome. Many cases are self-limiting and respond well to IMMUNOMODULATORY THERAPIES against the NMDA RECEPTORS antibod

68060437.name: Artificial Lens Implant Migration
68060437.note: The shifting and or tilting of implanted artificial lens resulting in impaired vision.

68060446.name: Phaeohyphomycosis
68060446.note: OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS caused by the dematiaceous (darkly pigmented) MITOSPORIC FUNGI of ALTERNARIA, Bipolaris, CLADOSPORIUM, Curvularia, and EXOPHIALA. These fungi have pigmented HYPHAE due to MELANIN in the cell wall. The initial subcutaneous cyst from the infection can become systemic and sprea

68060467.name: Disease Resistance
68060467.note: The capacity of an organism to defend itself against pathological processes or the agents of those processes. This most often involves innate immunity whereby the organism responds to pathogens in a generic way. The term disease resistance is used most frequently when referring to plants.

68060486.name: Ophthalmoplegic Migraine
68060486.note: Childhood-onset of recurrent headaches with an oculomotor cranial nerve palsy. Typically, ABDUCENS NERVE; OCULOMOTOR NERVE; and TROCHLEAR NERVE are involved with DIPLOPIA and BLEPHAROPTOSIS.

68060487.name: Alternariosis
68060487.note: Opportunistic fungal infection by a member of ALTERNARIA genus.

68060545.name: Pudendal Neuralgia
68060545.note: Pain associated with a damaged PUDENDAL NERVE. Clinical features may include positional pain with sitting in the perineal and genital areas, sexual dysfunction and FECAL INCONTINENCE and URINARY INCONTINENCE.

68060585.name: Fusariosis
68060585.note: OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS with the soil fungus FUSARIUM. Typically the infection is limited to the nail plate (ONYCHOMYCOSIS). The infection can however become systemic especially in an IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST (e.g., NEUTROPENIA) and results in cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions, fever, KERATITIS, and

68060586.name: Trichosporonosis
68060586.note: Fungal infections caused by TRICHOSPORON that may become systemic especially in an IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST. Clinical manifestations range from superficial cutaneous infections to systemic lesions in multiple organs.

68060605.name: Hyalohyphomycosis
68060605.note: OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS caused by a heterogeneous group of MITOSPORIC FUNGI with clear (hyalo-) HYPHAE in the host. Common causative agents include ACREMONIUM; ASPERGILLUS; CHRYSOSPORIUM; FUSARIUM; PAECILOMYCES; PENICILLIUM; PSEUDALLESCHERIA; SCEDOSPORIUM; and SCOPULARIOPSIS. Normally a dermatomyco

68060705.name: Dyscalculia
68060705.note: Impaired ability in numerical concepts. These inabilities arise as a result of primary neurological lesion, are syndromic (e.g., GERSTMANN SYNDROME ) or acquired due to brain damage.

68060725.name: Uterine Retroversion
68060725.note: A condition in which the UTERUS is found tilted backward toward the spine. The uterus is more commonly found in a straight vertical or anteverted (tipped forward) position. Although retroverted uterus is a normal variant position without symptoms, it is sometimes associated with pain, discomfort and

68060737.name: Reproductive Tract Infections
68060737.note: Infections of the genital tract in females or males. They can be caused by endogenous, iatrogenic, or sexually transmitted organisms.

68060750.name: Bone Anteversion
68060750.note: Malalignment of a bone in which its head and neck is rotated excessively forward or inward.

68060751.name: Bone Retroversion
68060751.note: Attachment of a bone in which its head and neck is rotated excessively backward.

68060831.name: Hand-Foot Syndrome
68060831.note: Chemotherapy-induced dermal side effects that are associated with the use of various CYTOSTATIC AGENTS. Symptoms range from mild ERYTHEMA and/or PARESTHESIA to severe ulcerative dermatitis with debilitating pain involving typically palmoplantar and intertriginous areas. These cutaneous manifestation

68060905.name: Coxa Vara
68060905.note: Hip deformity in which the femoral neck leans forward resulting in a decrease in the angle between femoral neck and its shaft. It may be congenital often syndromic, acquired, or developmental.

68060906.name: Coxa Valga
68060906.note: Hip deformity in which the angle between the femoral neck and its shaft is increased. It may be congenital, acquired, or developmental.

68061085.name: Agenesis of Corpus Callosum
68061085.note: Birth defect that results in a partial or complete absence of the CORPUS CALLOSUM. It may be isolated or a part of a syndrome (e.g., AICARDI'S SYNDROME; ACROCALLOSAL SYNDROME; ANDERMANN SYNDROME; and HOLOPROSENCEPHALY). Clinical manifestations include neuromotor skill impairment and INTELLECTUAL DIS

68061205.name: Vascular Calcification
68061205.note: Deposition of calcium into the blood vessel structures. Excessive calcification of the vessels is associated with ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUES formation particularly after MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION (see MONCKEBERG MEDIAL CALCIFIC SCLEROSIS) and chronic kidney diseases which in turn increase VASCULAR STIFFNES

68061206.name: Neoplasm Micrometastasis
68061206.note: Newly arising secondary tumors so small they are difficult to detect by physical examination or routine imaging techniques.

68061219.name: Olfactory Nerve Injuries
68061219.note: Traumatic injuries to the OLFACTORY NERVE. It may result in various olfactory dysfunction including a complete loss of smell.

68061220.name: Oculomotor Nerve Injuries
68061220.note: Traumatic injuries to the OCULOMOTOR NERVE. This may result in various eye movement dysfunction.

68061221.name: Trigeminal Nerve Injuries
68061221.note: Traumatic injuries to the TRIGEMINAL NERVE. It may result in extreme pain, abnormal sensation in the areas the nerve innervates on face, jaw, gums and tongue and can cause difficulties with speech and chewing. It is sometimes associated with various dental treatments.

68061222.name: Lingual Nerve Injuries
68061222.note: Traumatic injuries to the LINGUAL NERVE. It may be a complication following dental treatments.

68061223.name: Vagus Nerve Injuries
68061223.note: Traumatic injuries to the VAGUS NERVE. Because the vagus nerve innervates multiple organs, injuries in the nerve fibers may result in any gastrointestinal organ dysfunction downstream of the injury site.

68061224.name: Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
68061224.note: Traumatic injuries to the LARYNGEAL NERVE.

68061226.name: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
68061226.note: Traumatic injuries to the RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE that may result in vocal cord dysfunction.

68061227.name: Accessory Nerve Injuries
68061227.note: Traumatic injuries to the ACCESSORY NERVE. Damage to the nerve may produce weakness in head rotation and shoulder elevation.

68061228.name: Hypoglossal Nerve Injuries
68061228.note: Traumatic injuries to the HYPOGLOSSAL NERVE.

68061247.name: Trochlear Nerve Injuries
68061247.note: Traumatic injuries to the TROCHLEAR NERVE.

68061270.name: Nasal Septal Perforation
68061270.note: An opening or hole in the NASAL SEPTUM that is caused by TRAUMA, injury, drug use, or pathological process.

68061285.name: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Injuries
68061285.note: Traumatic injuries to the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE.

68061287.name: Glossopharyngeal Nerve Injuries
68061287.note: Traumatic injuries to the GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE.

68061325.name: Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Syndrome
68061325.note: Autosomal dominant HEREDITARY CANCER SYNDROME in which a mutation most often in either BRCA1 or BRCA2 is associated with a significantly increased risk for breast and ovarian cancers.

68061387.name: Chlamydial Pneumonia
68061387.note: Pneumonia caused by infections with the genus CHLAMYDIA; and CHLAMYDOPHILA, usually with CHLAMYDOPHILA PNEUMONIAE.

68061686.name: Premature Ejaculation
68061686.note: The emission of SEMEN and seminal fluid during the act of preparation for sexual intercourse, i.e. before there is penetration, or shortly after penetration.

68062025.name: Organophosphate Poisoning
68062025.note: Poisoning due to exposure to ORGANOPHOSPHORUS COMPOUNDS, such as ORGANOPHOSPHATES; ORGANOTHIOPHOSPHATES; and ORGANOTHIOPHOSPHONATES.

68062026.name: Alice in Wonderland Syndrome
68062026.note: Neurological condition characterized by disturbances in VISUAL PERCEPTION, most often of BODY SCHEMA, TIME PERCEPTION and HALLUCINATIONS. It is associated with MIGRAINE, infections (e.g., INFECTIOUS MONONUCLEOSIS), FEVER, EPILEPSY, and other neurological and psychiatric disorders.

68062027.name: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
syn: Drug induced Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
68062027.note: Autoimmune disease characterized by subepidermal blisters and linear deposition of autoantibodies at the dermoepidermal junction. The accumulated autoantibodies are of IMMUNOGLOBULIN A and occasionally IMMUNOGLOBULIN G classes against epidermal BASEMENT MEMBRANE proteins. The dermatosis is sometimes

68062108.name: May-Thurner Syndrome
68062108.note: A compression of ILIAC VEIN that results in a decreased flow in the vein and in the left LOWER EXTREMITY due to a vascular malformation. It may result in left leg EDEMA, pain, iliofemoral DEEP VENOUS THROMBOSIS and POSTTHROMBOTIC SYNDROME. Compression of the left common ILIAC VEIN by the right commo

68062625.name: Cystadenofibroma
68062625.note: Benign or borderline malignant neoplasm of the ovary and surrounding tissues. It is characterized by tumor(s) with cystic glands which are lined by cuboidal EPITHELIAL CELLS with clear cytoplasm, resembling ENDOMETRIUM cells. The glands are separated by fibroblastic STROMAL CELLS.

68062685.name: Steatocystoma Multiplex
68062685.note: A disorder characterized by multiple, wide spread cutaneous cysts that often become inflamed and rupture. It is caused by the same mutations in the gene coding for KRT-17 that are causative mutations for Pachyonychia congenita, Type 2. Natal teeth involvement is sometimes associated with steatocysto

68062688.name: Buschke-Lowenstein Tumor
syn: Giant Condyloma of Buschke and Lowenstein
Giant Condyloma of Buschke and Löwenstein
68062688.note: Exophytic tumor of the anogenital region associated with HPV infections. It becomes a large cauliflower-like, hyperkeratotic, verrucous mass that is locally destructive with little atypical cells. Histologically, tumor cells are broad rete peg structures that tend to invade deeper than CONDYLOMATA A

68062689.name: Lipoblastoma
68062689.note: Benign tumors of fatty tissues found in infancy and childhood. It is associated chromosomal aberrations that result in activation of an oncogene on chromosome band 8q12.

68062706.name: Prodromal Symptoms
68062706.note: Clinical or physiological indicators that precede the onset of disease.

68062787.name: Drug Overdose
68062787.note: Accidental or deliberate use of a medication or street drug in excess of normal dosage.

68062788.name: Adenomyosis
68062788.note: The extension of endometrial tissue (ENDOMETRIUM) into the MYOMETRIUM. It usually occurs in women in their reproductive years and may result in a diffusely enlarged uterus with ectopic and benign endometrial glands and stroma.

68062846.name: Non-Filarial Lymphedema
68062846.note: A form of elephantiasis caused by soil particles which penetrate the skin of the foot. It is limited to tropical regions with soils of high volcanic content.

68063129.name: Parental Death
68063129.note: The death of the father or mother or another person in this role.

68063130.name: Maternal Death
68063130.note: The death of the female parent.

68063169.name: Dentofacial Deformities
68063169.note: An abnormality of the jaws or teeth affecting the contour of the face. Such abnormality could be acquired or congenital.

68063173.name: Retrognathia
68063173.note: A physical misalignment of the upper (maxilla) and lower (mandibular) jaw bones in which either or both recede relative to the frontal plane of the forehead.

68063192.name: Pregnancy, Heterotopic
68063192.note: MULTIPLE PREGNANCY with EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occuring at different locations, involving both an intrauterine site and an extrauterine (ECTOPIC PREGNANCY) site.

68063205.name: Pneumorrhachis
68063205.note: Presence of air or gas within the spinal canal cavity (EPIDURAL SPACE; or SUBARACHNOID SPACE). It may result from traumatic injuries, emphysema, infection and other conditions. It can also develop as a complication of various SURGICAL PROCEDURES (e.g., MYELOGRAPHY).

68063371.name: Myringosclerosis
68063371.note: The formation of dense connective tissue and calcification in the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE that does not necessarily cause or lead to loss of hearing.

68063425.name: Binge Drinking
68063425.note: Drinking an excessive amount of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES in a short period of time.

68063466.name: Respiratory Aspiration of Gastric Contents
68063466.note: Inhaling refluxed gastric or duodenal contents.

68063485.name: Acanthocheilonemiasis
68063485.note: A tropical infectious disease found mainly in Africa that is caused by the filarial parasite ACANTHOCHEILONEMA. Symptoms include skin rashes, abdominal, chest, muscle, and joint pains, neurologic disorders, skin lumps, and elevated levels of white blood cells. The parasite is transmitted through the

68063487.name: Prescription Drug Misuse
syn: Non Medical Use of Prescription Drugs
68063487.note: Improper use of prescription drugs or medications outside the intended purpose, scope, or guidelines for use.

68063646.name: Carcinogenesis
68063646.note: The origin, production or development of cancer through genotypic and phenotypic changes which upset the normal balance between cell proliferation and cell death. Carcinogenesis generally requires a constellation of steps, which may occur quickly or over a period of many years.

68063647.name: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders
syn: Growth Retardation, Facial Abnormalities, and Central Nervous System Dysfunction
68063647.note: An umbrella term used to describe a pattern of disabilities and abnormalities that result from fetal exposure to ETHANOL during pregnancy. It encompasses a phenotypic range that can vary greatly between individuals, but reliably includes one or more of the following: characteristic facial dysmorphis

68063730.name: Rickets, Hypophosphatemic
68063730.note: A disorder characterized by HYPOPHOSPHATEMIA; RICKETS; OSTEOMALACIA; resulting from lack of phosphate reabsorption by the kidneys and possible defects in vitamin D metabolism.

68063748.name: Bland White Garland Syndrome
68063748.note: A congenital coronary vessel anomaly in which the left main CORONARY ARTERY originates from the PULMONARY ARTERY instead of from AORTA. The congenital heart defect typically results in coronary artery FISTULA; LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE and MITRAL VALVE INSUFFICIENCY during the first months of life.

68063766.name: Pediatric Obesity
68063766.note: BODY MASS INDEX in children (ages 2-12) and in adolescents (ages 13-18) that is grossly above the recommended cut-off for a specific age and sex. For infants less than 2 years of age, obesity is determined based on standard weight-for-length percentile measures.

68063807.name: Dandruff
68063807.note: Excessive shedding of dry scaly material from the scalp in humans.

68063926.name: Drug Hypersensitivity Syndrome
syn: Drug Reaction With Eosinophilia And Systemic Symptom
Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms Syndrome
Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms
68063926.note: Severe drug eruption characterized by high fever, erythematous rash and inflammation of internal organ(s).

68064068.name: Collagenous Sprue
68064068.note: A malabsorption syndrome characterized by collagenous mucosal lesions of the SMALL INTESTINE, atrophy of MICROVILLI, severe malabsorption, diarrhea, and MALNUTRITION often refractory to a gluten-free diet.

68064090.name: Intraocular Lymphoma
68064090.note: A form of malignant cancer which occurs within the eyeball.

68064128.name: Nodding Syndrome
68064128.note: Unexplained neurologic condition characterized by episodes of atonic seizures, convulsions or staring spells with further cognitive decline.

68064129.name: Prostatic Neoplasms, Castration-Resistant
68064129.note: Tumors or cancer of the PROSTATE which can grow in the presence of low or residual amount of androgen hormones such as TESTOSTERONE.

68064146.name: Chemotherapy-Induced Febrile Neutropenia
68064146.note: FEVER accompanied by a significant reduction in NEUTROPHIL count associated with CHEMOTHERAPY.

68064147.name: Febrile Neutropenia
68064147.note: Fever accompanied by a significant reduction in the number of NEUTROPHILS.

68064250.name: Hypertriglyceridemic Waist
68064250.note: A screening phenotype consisting of both elevated WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE and elevated fasting TRIGLYCERIDES level.

68064386.name: Ankle Fractures
68064386.note: Fractures of any of the bones of the ANKLE.

68064419.name: Chemically-Induced Disorders
68064419.note: Disorders caused by the intentional or unintentional ingestion or exposure to chemical substances such as PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS; NOXAE; and PESTICIDES.

68064420.name: Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
syn: Drug Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reaction
Drug Related Side Effects and Adverse Reaction
68064420.note: Disorders that result from the intended use of PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS. Included in this heading are a broad variety of chemically-induced adverse conditions due to toxicity, DRUG INTERACTIONS, and metabolic effects of pharmaceuticals.

68064706.name: Vocal Cord Dysfunction
68064706.note: A disorder characterized by an intermittent abnormal VOCAL CORDS movement toward the midline during inspiration or expiration resulting in upper AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION.

68064726.name: Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms
syn: ER Negative PR Negative HER2 Negative Breast Cancer
ER Negative PR Negative HER2 Negative Breast Neoplasms
68064726.note: Breast neoplasms that do not express ESTROGEN RECEPTORS; PROGESTERONE RECEPTORS; and do not overexpress the NEU RECEPTOR/HER-2 PROTO-ONCOGENE PROTEIN.

68064749.name: Retrocaval Ureter
68064749.note: A rare congenital abnormality resulting in the URETER passing dorsal to and being obstructed by the INFERIOR VENA CAVA.

68064752.name: Atrial Remodeling
68064752.note: Long-term changes in the electrophysiological parameters and/or anatomical structures of the HEART ATRIA that result from prolonged changes in atrial rate, often associated with ATRIAL FIBRILLATION or long periods of intense EXERCISE.

68064806.name: Dysbiosis
68064806.note: Changes in quantitative and qualitative composition of MICROBIOTA. The changes may lead to altered host microbial interaction or homeostatic imbalance that can contribute to a disease state often with inflammation.

68064807.name: Anticholinergic Syndrome
68064807.note: Adverse drug effects associated with CHOLINERGIC ANTAGONISTS. Clinical features include TACHYCARDIA; HYPERTHERMIA; MYDRIASIS, dry skin and dry mucous membranes, decreased bowel sounds and urinary retention in peripheral anticholinergic syndrome; and HALLUCINATIONS; PSYCHOSES; SEIZURES; and COMA in c

68064927.name: Tick Bites
68064927.note: The effects, both local and systemic, caused by the bites of TICKS.

68065008.name: Scorpion Stings
68065008.note: The effects, both local and systemic, caused by the bite of SCORPIONS.

68065134.name: Lipedema
68065134.note: Disorder of adipose tissue characterized by symmetric and bilateral enlargement of the lower extremities due to abnormal deposition of SUBCUTANEOUS FAT often in obese women. It is associated with HEMATOMA, pain and may progress to secondary LYMPHEDEMA which is known as lipolymphedema.

68065148.name: Nicolau Syndrome
68065148.note: An uncommon complication of INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION leading to variable degrees of necrosis of skin and underlying tissue.

68065166.name: Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy
68065166.note: Acute neurological dysfunction during severe SEPSIS in the absence of direct brain infection characterized by systemic inflammation and BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER perturbation.

68065167.name: Pregnancy, Interstitial
68065167.note: A type of ectopic pregnancy in which the extrauterine EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in the portion of the FALLOPIAN TUBE that traverses the muscular wall of the uterus.

68065170.name: Pregnancy, Angular
68065170.note: A rare type of abnormal pregnancy in which EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs at a lateral angle of the UTERUS, medial to the uterotubal junction and the ROUND LIGAMENT OF UTERUS.

68065172.name: Pregnancy, Ovarian
68065172.note: A type of pregnancy in which EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in an OVARY instead of in the uterine cavity.

68065173.name: Pregnancy, Cornual
68065173.note: A type of pregnancy in which the EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in the horn of the UTERUS instead of in the uterine cavity, i.e. at the junction of the uterus and one of the FALLOPIAN TUBES.

68065227.name: Transfusion Reaction
68065227.note: Complications of BLOOD TRANSFUSION. Included adverse reactions are common allergic and febrile reactions; hemolytic (delayed and acute) reactions; and other non-hemolytic adverse reactions such as infections and adverse immune reactions related to immunocompatibility.

68065290.name: Acute-On-Chronic Liver Failure
68065290.note: Sudden liver failure in the presence of underlying compensated chronic LIVER DISEASE (e.g., LIVER CIRRHOSIS; HEPATITIS; and liver injury and failure) due to a precipitating acute hepatic insult.

68065306.name: Corneal Injuries
68065306.note: Damage or trauma inflicted to the CORNEA by external means.

68065308.name: Morphological and Microscopic Findings
68065308.note: Morphological findings useful in differentiation and classification of results in CYTODIAGNOSIS and related techniques.

68065309.name: Atypical Squamous Cells of the Cervix
syn: Atypical Squamous Cells of Undetermined Significance
Atypical Squamous Cells, Cannot Rule Out High-Grade Squamous Intra-Epithelial Lesion
Atypical Squamous Cells, Cannot Rule Out High Grade Squamous Intra Epithelial Lesion
ASC-H Atypical Squamous Cells, Cannot Rule Out High-Grade Squamous Intra-epithelial Lesion
ASC H Atypical Squamous Cells, Cannot Rule Out High Grade Squamous Intra epithelial Lesion
68065309.note: Morphological abnormalities of the cervical EPITHELIUM, usually revealed in PAP SMEAR, which do not meet the criteria for squamous CERVICAL INTRAEPITHELIAL NEOPLASIA or SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMAS of the CERVIX . It may be a sign of infection with certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV).or sign of

68065310.name: Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions of the Cervix
68065310.note: A cytological test finding often from PAP SMEARS that shows abnormal lesions of SQUAMOUS EPITHELIAL CELLS of the CERVIX. It is a diagnostic criterion used in the Bethesda System for UTERINE CERVICAL NEOPLASMS and represents the PAP TEST result that is abnormal. Although squamous intraepithelial lesi

68065311.name: Adenocarcinoma in Situ
68065311.note: A lesion with cytological characteristics associated with invasive adenocarcinoma but the tumor cells are confined to the GLANDULAR EPITHELIAL CELLS of origin. Adenocarcinoma in situ of the CERVIX and the LUNG are the most common.

68065446.name: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder
68065446.note: A condition in which a woman suffers from severe depression, irritability, and tension before MENSTRUATION. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) may involve a wide range of physical or emotional symptoms, which are more severe and debilitating than those seen with premenstrual syndrome (PMS), and

68065606.name: Metabolic Side Effects of Drugs and Substances
68065606.note: Specific effects of drugs and substances on metabolic pathways such as those occurring through the CYTOCHROME P-450 ENZYME SYSTEM. These include effects that often result in DRUG INTERACTIONS; FOOD-DRUG INTERACTIONS; and HERB-DRUG INTERACTIONS.

68065626.name: Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
68065626.note: Fatty liver finding without excessive ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION.

68065627.name: Familial Primary Pulmonary Hypertension
syn: Pulmonary Hypertension, Primary, 1, With Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
68065627.note: Familial or idiopathic hypertension in the PULMONARY CIRCULATION which is not secondary to other disease.

68065630.name: Hernias, Diaphragmatic, Congenital
68065630.note: Protrusion of abdominal structures into the THORAX as a result of embryologic defects in the DIAPHRAGM often present in the neonatal period. It can be isolated, syndromic, non-syndromic or be a part of chromosome abnormality. Associated pulmonary hypoplasia and PULMONARY HYPERTENSION can further com

68065631.name: Rhinitis, Allergic
68065631.note: An inflammation of the NASAL MUCOSA triggered by ALLERGENS.

68065632.name: Chikungunya Fever
68065632.note: An acute infection caused by a mosquito-borne alphavirus CHIKUNGUNYA VIRUS characterized by RASH; FEVER; JOINT PAINS; CONJUNCTIVITIS; MENINGOENCEPHALITIS; LYMPHOPENIA; and THROMBOCYTOPENIA.

68065634.name: Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak
68065634.note: Discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through a hole through the skull bone most commonly draining from the nose (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID RHINORRHEA) or the ear (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID OTORRHEA).

68065635.name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
68065635.note: Idiopathic recurrent VERTIGO associated with POSITIONAL NYSTAGMUS. It is associated with a vestibular loss most often with OTOCONIA dislodge but without other neurological or auditory signs. Unlike in LABYRINTHITIS and VESTIBULAR NEURONITIS, inflammation in the ear is not observed.

68065646.name: Thyroid Carcinoma, Anaplastic
68065646.note: An aggressive THYROID GLAND malignancy which generally occurs in IODINE-deficient areas in people with previous thyroid pathology such as GOITER. It is associated with CELL DEDIFFERENTIATION of THYROID CARCINOMA (e.g., FOLLICULAR THYROID CARCINOMA; PAPILLARY THYROID CANCER). Typical initial presenta

68065666.name: Mesenteric Ischemia
68065666.note: Ischemic tissue injury produced by insufficient perfusion of intestinal tissue by the MESENTERIC CIRCULATION (i.e., CELIAC ARTERY; SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY; INFERERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY; and MESENTERIC VEINS). It can progress from ISCHEMIA; EDEMA; and GANGRENE of the bowel wall to PERITONITIS and

68065703.name: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group I
syn: Malformations Secondary to Abnormal Neuronal and Glial Proliferation or Apoptosis
Malformations Due to Abnormal Neuronal and Glial Proliferation or Apoptosis
68065703.note: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal and glial CELL PROLIFERATION or APOPTOSIS in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes congenital MICROCEPHALIES; MICROLISSENCEPHALIES, megalencephalies, HEMIMEGALENCEPHALIES and cortical dysplasias with balloon cells.

68065704.name: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group III
syn: Malformations Secondary to Abnormal Postmigrational Development
Malformations Due to Abnormal Postmigrational Development
68065704.note: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal cortical maturation after CELL MIGRATION in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes injury to the cortex during later stages of cortical development such as POLYMICROGYRIA and focal cortical dysplasias.

68065705.name: Hemimegalencephaly
68065705.note: Rare MALFORMATIONS OF CORTICAL DEVELOPMENT, GROUP I characterized by the enlargement of one side of the brain. It is associated with seizures, partial paralysis, and mental retardation.

68065706.name: Polymicrogyria
68065706.note: Heterogeneous disorders of cortical malformation characterized by excessive and small fused gyri and shallow sulci of the CORTEX with abnormal cortical lamination. It is considered a malformation secondary to abnormal post-migrational development of the neurons during cerebral cortical development a

68065707.name: Schizencephaly
68065707.note: Cortical malformations characterized by grey matter-lined cleft or cyst that extends from the EPENDYMA often to the PIA MATER outer surface. The grey matter that lines the cleft is often POLYMICROGYRIA. It is associated with developmental delay, motor disturbance and seizures.

68065708.name: Porencephaly
syn: Retinal Arteriolar Tortuosity, Infantile Hemiparesis, and Leukoencephalopathy, Autosomal Dominant
68065708.note: Cortical malformations characterized by white matter-lined cleft or cyst associated with ISCHEMIA and hemorrhagic insults. Symptoms include delayed growth and development, HYPOTONIA; SEIZURES; SPASTIC HEMIPLEGIA and MACROCEPHALY; MICROCEPHALY; or HYDROCEPHALUS. Mutations in the genes encoding COLLAG

68065710.name: Glossoptosis
68065710.note: Posterior displacement of the TONGUE toward the PHARYNX. It is often a feature in syndromes such as in PIERRE ROBIN SYNDROME and DOWN SYNDROME and associated with AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION during sleep (OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEAS).

68065766.name: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome
68065766.note: An hereditary hemolytic uremic syndrome associated with variations in the gene that encodes COMPLEMENT FACTOR H, or the related proteins CFHR1 and CFHR3. Disease often progresses to CHRONIC KIDNEY FAILURE without the prodromal symptoms of ENTEROCOLITIS and DIARRHEA that characterize typical hemolyti

68065817.name: Congenital Microtia
68065817.note: Malformation of external portion of EAR AURICLE.

68065906.name: Hyperlactatemia
68065906.note: Increase in blood LACTATE concentration often associated with SEPTIC SHOCK; LUNG INJURY; SEPSIS; and DRUG TOXICITY. When hyperlactatemia is associated with low body pH (acidosis) it is LACTIC ACIDOSIS.

68065907.name: Karoshi Death
68065907.note: Sudden death from overwork, most often as a result of acute CARDIOVASCULAR STROKE.

68066087.name: Perinatal Death
68066087.note: The death of a FETUS of GESTATIONAL AGE 28 weeks or more, or the death of a live-born INFANT less than 28 days of age.

68066088.name: Infant Death
68066088.note: The death of a live-born INFANT within its first year of life.

68066126.name: Cardiotoxicity
68066126.note: Damage to the HEART or its function secondary to exposure to toxic substances such as drugs used in CHEMOTHERAPY; IMMUNOTHERAPY; or RADIATION.

68066166.name: Pectus Carinatum
68066166.note: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal anterior protrusion of the STERNUM and adjacent COSTAL CARTILAGE.

68066190.name: Allesthesia
68066190.note: A neurological disorder in which a sensory stimulus, usually tactile but more rarely other sensory modalities, is misperceived in a location distant from the original stimulus.

68066253.name: Vascular Remodeling
68066253.note: The active alterations of vascular wall structures, often leading to elevated VASCULAR RESISTANCE. It is associated with AGING; ATHEROSCLEROSIS; DIABETES MELLITUS; HYPERTENSION; PREGNANCY; PULMONARY HYPERTENSION; and STROKE, but is also a normal part of EMBRYOGENESIS.

68066263.name: Protein Aggregation, Pathological
68066263.note: A biochemical phenomenon in which misfolded proteins aggregate either intra- or extracellularly. Triggered by factors such as MUTATION; POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS, and environmental stress, it is generally associated with ALZHEIMER DISEASE; PARKINSON DISEASE; HUNTINGTON DISEASE; and TYPE 2 DIA
